title: File: file.serialize returns the file's bytes (base64) — web Save wrote corrupt documents
author: storybored379
body:
file.serialize returned {json: String::from_utf8_lossy(to_bytes(doc))},
but since M6.1 the native format is a zip (deflated document.json + raw
assets), not JSON text. from_utf8_lossy turns every invalid UTF-8
sequence into U+FFFD, so the result is not the file: on the web, File ›
Save downloads exactly those bytes (download_document), and the
downloaded .designcraft can't be opened again ("invalid Zip archive").
Agents calling file.serialize got the same unusable string.

Return {base64, bytes} like the other byte-producing commands
(file.exportIdml, file.exportPdf, snippet.export) and decode it in
download_document.

Test: serialized_document_opens_again.

**Note — API change:** `file.serialize` now returns `{base64, bytes}` instead of `{json}` (the old value was never a usable file since the zip format landed). The web `download_document` is updated accordingly; anything else calling `file.serialize` would need the same one-line change.

### How it was found and tested
- Reproduced end-to-end through the headless MCP server (`designcraft-cli mcp`), then fixed.
- Regression test added; verified it **fails without the change and passes with it**. `cargo test -p designcraft-engine` passes on current `main`; `cargo fmt --check` clean on the touched crate.
- Files: `crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tests.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted; only public specs and black-box tools (poppler/ffprobe etc.) as oracles.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Layers: the active layer falls back to the top layer when it is removed
author: storybored379
body:
The active layer lives on DocState, outside the undo snapshots, and
nothing re-checked it when the document's layers changed. After New
Layer → Undo (or Delete Layer / Delete Unused Layers / Merge Layers on
the active layer) it kept pointing at a layer that no longer exists, and
every object created next (frames, lines, placed images, pasted items)
was put on that phantom layer: not drawn on the canvas, missing from PDF
export, ItemLayer referencing an undefined layer in IDML, and preflight
reported nothing.

After each command, if the active layer is gone, make the top layer
active (as on opening a document).

Test: active_layer_survives_undoing_new_layer.

title: EPUB: styles whose names slug alike keep their own CSS classes
author: storybored379
body:
Paragraph and character styles become CSS classes through `slug()`, which keeps only ASCII
letters and digits. Different styles could therefore end up with the same class: every
all-non-ASCII name ("見出し", "本文", Cyrillic, Greek…) becomes `basic`, and "Body Text" /
"Body-Text" / "body text" all become `body-text`. `style.css` then holds several rules for one
class and the last one wins, so e.g. a 30 pt centred Japanese heading style came out at the
body style's 10 pt, left-aligned, in the exported EPUB.

### What changed
- Each style name is mapped to a class once per export (paragraph and character styles
  separately); on a collision the later style gets `-2`, `-3`…. The same map is used for the
  stylesheet and for the XHTML, so they always agree.
- A class set in Export Tagging still takes precedence in the XHTML, as before. Styles whose
  names don't collide keep exactly the class they had.

### How it was found and tested
- Found by exporting a document with Japanese and near-duplicate style names to EPUB and
  comparing `style.css` with the XHTML.
- New test `styles_whose_names_slug_alike_keep_their_own_classes` (`crates/epub/src/lib.rs`):
  four styles (two CJK names, "Body Text", "Body-Text") must get four distinct classes with one
  rule each. Verified it **fails on current `main` without the fix** (`one rule for `basic``)
  and passes with it.
- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-epub --all-targets` (no warnings),
  `cargo fmt --check` on the touched file, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm` all pass.
- Files: `crates/epub/src/lib.rs`
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted.

title: CI: fix new Rust 1.99 clippy lints
author: echelon
body:
Rust 1.99's clippy adds lints that current `main` fails under `cargo xtask ci` (`-D warnings`), so every commit is blocked:

- `chunks_exact(N)` / `chunks_exact_mut(N)` with a constant `N` → `as_chunks::<N>().0` / `as_chunks_mut::<N>().0` (same iteration: full chunks only, remainder dropped)
- a `match` that is just `?` (`pdf/src/pdfx.rs`)
- a redundant `&` in a `format!` argument (`pdf/src/transitions.rs`)

Mechanical (`cargo clippy --fix`, plus one hand edit in a test). No behaviour change; the full gate passes.

title: UI: tool shortcuts work right after clicking the canvas (#1)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #1.

Clicking or dragging on the canvas gives it egui keyboard focus (`canvas.rs`, so the active tool gets keys). But the global shortcut handler skipped *all* keys whenever `egui_wants_keyboard_input()` was true, which in egui means "any widget has focus", not "a text field has focus". So after drawing a frame with the Rectangle Frame tool (F), pressing V did nothing until Esc cleared egui's focus.

### Change
- `menus::shortcuts`: only a focused **text field** (`ctx.text_edit_focused()`) blocks global and tool shortcuts. Typing in panel fields, dialogs and the story editor is unaffected; all of those are `TextEdit`s. Typing into a text frame is still handled by the existing `session.wants_text()` check.
- `canvas.rs`: the same correction for Space (temporary Hand tool) and for the canvas's own key handling, which had the same "any widget focused" test.

### Test
`tool_shortcuts_work_after_drawing_on_the_canvas` drives real egui frames: F, draw a frame on the canvas, V, F. It fails on `main` ("V switches tools straight after drawing") and passes with the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Linux: use the X11 backend under XWayland so files can be dropped (#2)
author: echelon
body:
Fixes #2.

winit 0.30 (under eframe) implements file drag-and-drop on Linux only for the **X11** backend; its Wayland backend has no DnD support. On a Wayland session (KDE Plasma, which CachyOS uses by default) the app ran as a native Wayland client, so the compositor showed a "no" cursor and the drop never reached us.

### Change
On Linux, when an X server is available (`DISPLAY` set, i.e. XWayland), the desktop app now selects winit's X11 backend, and dropping files works. With the window on X11, dropping an image onto the canvas with an empty frame selected (for example the frame you just drew) places the image into that frame, as before.
- `DESIGNCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` keeps the native Wayland backend.
- macOS, Windows and the web build are unchanged (the code is `cfg(target_os = "linux")`).
- `winit` is added as a Linux-only dependency of the app crate, at the version eframe already uses (no new crates in `Cargo.lock`).

### Notes
- Trade-off: under XWayland the compositor handles fractional scaling, which can look slightly softer than native Wayland on HiDPI screens. That's why the opt-out exists. When winit gains Wayland DnD we can switch back.
- The Flatpak manifest grants X11 only as `fallback-x11`, so inside the Flatpak on Wayland there is no `DISPLAY` and the app stays on Wayland (no file drops yet). I didn't change the sandbox permissions in this PR.

### Testing
Checked with `cargo clippy -p designcraft --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- -D warnings` and the full `cargo xtask ci` on macOS. I couldn't run it on a Linux desktop here, so a confirmation from a Wayland user would be welcome.

title: Never crash: last-resort guard around every command
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (craftrules [`standards/never-crash.md`](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/main/standards/never-crash.md), "Last-resort guard"). Before this PR nothing caught an escaped panic: one panicking command took the app, with every open document, down.

**What it does (small, no shell redesign)**
- `Session::execute` wraps each command in `std::panic::catch_unwind` (new `crates/engine/src/guard.rs`). Every edit, file import and export goes through `execute`, whether it comes from the UI (`app.run`), the CLI, MCP or the control channel, so this is the single choke point.
- On a panic: the active document and selection go back to how they were before the command, any half-finished interaction is dropped, crash recovery is saved when a recovery folder is set, and the caller gets `EngineError::Internal(command, message)`: "internal error in `…` (the document was kept as it was): …". The UI shows it like any other command error.
- `guard::install_panic_hook()` logs each panic's message and location, then runs the previous hook (stderr). The first `Session::new()` installs it, once per process, so the desktop app, CLI and MCP server all get it and no app file changes.
- `panic = "unwind"` is already the default (no profile sets `abort`). On wasm32, panics still abort.

Test: `guard::tests::a_panicking_command_is_an_error_and_keeps_the_document`. A command edits the document and then panics; the result is an error, the document is the one from before, and the session keeps working.

This is a safety net. The crate PRs remove the panics themselves.

**Merging with the engine PR:** both touch `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, in non-adjacent places (this PR: the `EngineError` enum, `pub mod guard`, `execute`; the engine PR: the crate attribute and the smart-reflow loop). Git merges them cleanly in either order; verified by merging every never-crash branch together.

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-t…

title: Never crash: importers (text, IDML, fonts, format, EPUB, images)
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (craftrules [`standards/never-crash.md`](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/main/standards/never-crash.md)). These crates read untrusted files, so they go first. Independent of the other never-crash PRs; merge in any order.

### Real crash fixed (input-reachable)
- **`.xlsx` import: out of memory from one cell reference.** `xlsx::import` allocated the whole used range (`vec![vec![String; cols]; rows]`) *before* applying its 100 000-cell cap. One cell at `A999999999`, or a long column name like `AANANE308` (about 300M columns), meant billions of cells, and the process was killed. Fuzzing hit this within seconds. The range is now capped before allocating (1 000 columns; rows up to the cell cap), cells outside it are dropped with a warning, and column names use checked arithmetic (a long name overflowed `usize`).
  Regression test: `xlsx::tests::far_away_cell_references_are_capped`.

### Hardening
- IDML import: `Vec::with_capacity` no longer trusts the zip entry's declared size (capped at 16 MiB up front; the data still reads in full). `HeaderRowCount + FooterRowCount` add saturating (`1e308` from the file overflowed).
- IDML export: `next_id + 0x100` saturates. With a `.designcraft` whose `next_id` is near `u64::MAX` this overflowed; the doc PR also rejects such documents on load.
- Tagged Text import and IDML table export: `expect()` → `let … else` / `if let`.
- Fonts: `FontDb::face` ends in a compiled-in last-resort face instead of `expect("bundled fonts are always present")`. Parsing the `include_bytes!` font is the one documented `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` exception, and the new test `last_resort_face_parses` proves it on every run.

`#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]` added to textimport, idml, fonts, format, epub and images. `clippy.toml` is added too (identical to #8).

title: FreeBSD: CI job and X11 drag-and-drop on every non-Apple Unix

author: storybored379
body:

title: Snap: smart guides and snapping
author: CameronGilroy
body:
Adds one snapping runner for the document grid, the baseline grid, ruler guides with margins and columns, object alignment, equal spacing, and smart dimensions, including rotation. Pen clicks and anchor drags use the same runner.

The first hit on an axis wins. Pass order is document grid, baseline, guides, alignment, spacing, then dimensions. A later pass cannot override an earlier one. A pass never fails the gesture: non-finite input, a zone of 0, a grid spacing of 0, and a baseline increment of 0 produce no hit.

View switches live on `UiState`, not in the document:

- Snap to Guides (`Cmd+Shift+;`), on by default
- Snap to Document Grid, off by default
- Smart Guides, on by default
- Align to Object Edges, Align to Object Centers, Smart Dimensions, Smart Spacing, and Snap to Zone (default 4 screen pixels) on Guides & Pasteboard

Parent items attract at the stroked visible edge. A group's box is the union of each child's visible bounds after the group transform. Smart Dimensions matches a rotated item's own side length. A move snaps on the spread under the pointer. Shift constrains first, then the driving edge still snaps.

The design and the ten-task plan are included:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-smart-guides-snapping-design.md`
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-05-smart-guides-snapping.md`

Those docs were not on upstream `main`. This branch also ignores `.worktrees/`.

### Checks

`cargo xtask ci` passed on the branch tip (`3eeb8eb`): fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, and wasm.

`main` has moved since the fork (FreeBSD CI and the 0.2.0 version bump). A merge-tree against current `upstream/main` is clean, and those commits do not touch the snapping files. The merged result was not retested.

title: Fix #22: installed fonts are found by name whatever ran before
author: japbcoelho
body:
Fixes #22.

`FontDb` only cataloged the system fonts when a character needed a fallback font (the fallback path is the only caller of `load_system_fonts`). So a document set in an installed family was composed in Source Sans 3, and `font.list` and preflight reported the family missing.

This follows storytold/vectorcraft#130. Every lookup by family name now waits for one scan of the font folders per session. The app starts the scan in the background at startup; the CLI and other processes run it on first use. The scan reads only each file's table directory and `name` table, and it skips folders it has already read, so a symlink loop can't hang it. `has_family`, which `font.list` and preflight call, now also counts installed families. `FontDb::with_font_dirs` and `system_font_dirs` let tests use their own font folders.

Validation: the new unit tests in `crates/fonts/src/tests_sysfonts.rs` scan temporary font folders (a renamed copy of the bundled Source Sans 3, a font collection, a damaged file, a symlink back to a parent folder), and `crates/fonts/tests/system_fonts.rs` checks the first lookup in a fresh process against the fonts installed on the machine. With the catalog step made a no-op, three of the six unit tests and the fresh-process test fail. `cargo xtask ci` passes on Rust 1.99. On my machine, with 4,407 font files installed, the fresh-process test scans them twice in 0.09 s.

title: Text: text.select documents its offsets as UTF-8 bytes
author: japbcoelho
body:
`text.select` takes `anchor` and `focus` as UTF-8 byte offsets into the story text, the offsets `find.find` returns, but its params doc said only `{story, anchor, focus}`. A script that counts characters, as Python's `len()` does, selects too little after the first accented letter: selecting "Matemática Básica" with `focus: 17` and then running `type.char` left the last two letters unchanged.

The params doc now reads `{story, anchor, focus} (UTF-8 byte offsets into the story text, as find.find reports them: á or — counts 2 or 3)`. Nothing else changes.

Validation: `designcraft-cli describe text.select` shows the new text, and `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Engine: commands given ids run without a selection
author: japbcoelho
body:
Commands whose params document `ids` (`object.textFrameOptions`, `transform.rotate` and others) act on the objects a call names, but their `enabled` check looked only at the selection. With a text caret or nothing selected, a call with `{"ids": [5]}` failed:

```
command `object.textFrameOptions` is not available right now: nothing selected
```

`Session::execute` now lets such a call through when every named object exists, and fails with `no object with id N` when one doesn't. Calls without `ids`, and commands disabled for any other reason, behave as before. `transform.set`, `object.arrange` and `edit.stepAndRepeat` already acted on `ids`; their params now say so.

This assumes `ids` is meant to work without a selection, as the params docs suggest.

title: PDF: placed PDF 1.7 files go into PDF/X-4 exports
author: japbcoelho
body:
A PDF/X-4 export, which is PDF 1.6, failed at the very end when a page held a placed PDF 1.7, the version VectorCraft and most other tools write:

```
designcraft-cli: PDF writer error: Pdf(PdfDocument(PdfDocumentRepr { .. }), VersionMismatch(Pdf17), None)
```

krilla refuses to embed a PDF newer than the file it writes. PDF 1.7 added nothing to how page content is drawn, so a placed 1.7 file now goes in as 1.6, with its header relabelled the way `qpdf --force-version=1.6` does it, and the export report gets a warning. A PDF 2.0 file, or one whose catalog declares 1.7, still can't go in. The export now fails with a message that names it:

```
a placed PDF is newer than the PDF 1.6 this export writes (logo.pdf is PDF 2.0): save it as PDF 1.6 or older and place it again
```

`hayro-syntax` moves from dev-dependencies to dependencies because the check names its `PdfVersion`; krilla already builds it.

Validation: `placed_pdf_print_tests::pdf_17_placed_in_pdfx4` in `cmd/export.rs` fails on main `02f187c` and passes with the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: PDF: [Paper] prints as no ink in print exports

That put DeviceRGB in a CMYK print file, which PDF/X-4 doesn't allow under a CMYK output intent. title: PDF: transparency groups blend in CMYK in print exports
author: japbcoelho
body:
krilla gives every transparency group it writes a DeviceRGB blending space, including the group around a placed PDF page:

```
/Group<</Type/Group/S/Transparency/I true/CS/DeviceRGB>>
```

So print exports carried DeviceRGB, which PDF/X-4 doesn't allow under a CMYK output intent, and blended CMYK art through RGB. A placed logo whose black is C91 M78 Y61 K97 in its own file came out as C72 M67 Y67 K88 in a CMYK render of the export.

When the document's transparency blend space is CMYK (the default for print documents) or the export is PDF/X-4, the new `cmyk_group_spaces` rewrites these groups to `/CS/DeviceCMYK` after krilla has written the file. It edits in place and keeps the length: dropping the optional `/Type/Group` makes room, and spaces pad the rest. It only looks inside object dictionaries found through the cross-reference table, never in stream data, so every offset stays valid. Booklet exports get the same; books merged by `merge_pdfs` don't yet.

If krilla gets an option to choose the group colour space, this rewrite can go.

Validation: `print_group_tests::print_transparency_groups_blend_in_cmyk` in `cmd/export.rs` fails on main `02f187c` and passes with the fix. It also checks that the file still parses and that an RGB blend space keeps RGB groups. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: CLI: a closed stdout ends designcraft-cli quietly
author: japbcoelho
body:
`designcraft-cli commands | head -1` panicked and exited with status 101:

thread 'main' panicked at /rustc/b940084d7eb6a299eb4bfeb8e34901bc051e7ac4/library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1168:9:

author: echelon
body:
Ported from printcraft#66.

title: Windows on ARM64: release builds, tested on ARM64 hardware (#45)
author: echelon
body:
Closes #45, requested by @maxffarrell.

**Release:**
- `release.yml` builds, signs and packages a **Windows ARM64** MSI and portable zip alongside x64 and x86: `designcraft-<version>-windows-arm64.msi` and `…-arm64-portable.zip`.
- It's cross-compiled (`aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`) on the x64 Windows runner, so signing (certificate or Azure Trusted Signing) and WiX run exactly as they do for x64.
- `package.ps1` takes `-Arch arm64` (WiX `-arch arm64`). A new pre-packaging check verifies each binary's **PE Machine** and subsystem (app = GUI, CLI = console), so an x64 build can never ship labelled ARM64. The `.wxs` has nothing arch-specific (`ProgramFiles6432Folder` → `C:\Program Files` on ARM64).

**Validation, the issue's third point** (new `windows-arm64.yml`; runs on PRs touching Cargo or Windows packaging files, on `main`, and weekly):
1. **package**: builds the ARM64 MSI exactly as the release does (unsigned here) and keeps it as an artifact for 7 days, so anyone with ARM hardware can try it.
2. **install and run on ARM64**: on GitHub's Windows 11 ARM64 runner, installs the MSI silently and checks that both installed binaries are ARM64. With the **installed** `designcraft-cli` it then lays out a page through engine commands (`frame.create` + `story.get`), saves a `.designcraft`, exports PNG, PDF and IDML, reopens the IDML and renders it, and exports the sample magazine (fonts and images) to PDF, checking each output's file signature. Finally it uninstalls. I ran the same smoke script locally with the macOS CLI.
3. **test (native ARM64)**: `cargo test --workspace` natively on ARM64, which covers the engine, composition, import/export and the UI's command layer.

**Docs:** the README says Windows builds come for x64, x86 and ARM64.

**Not covered:** the GUI isn't launched interactively on ARM64 in CI. The engine, the packaged binaries and the test suite are.

title: PDF: placed CMYK TIFFs keep their inks
author: EthanSuquet
body:
A placed CMYK TIFF was written to every PDF, PDF/X-4 included, as DeviceRGB: `load_image` sent TIFFs through `decode_rgba`, and `image` decodes CMYK to RGB. 100% K became RGB black, which separates as four-colour black on press.

- `designcraft-images`: `decode_cmyk_tiff` reads a CMYK TIFF's ink values with the `tiff` crate (the version `image` already uses, so no new packages): 8/16-bit, interleaved, opaque or unassociated alpha. `is_cmyk_tiff` detects the rest. All lengths are checked; no panics in non-test code.
- PDF export writes them via krilla's `CustomImage` as DeviceCMYK, like a CMYK JPEG. The TIFF's ICC profile is left out so the numbers reach the output intent unchanged. PDF/A stays RGB.
- CMYK TIFFs this can't read (planar, premultiplied alpha, other inks, >256 MiB) still convert to RGB, now with an export warning.
- Screen rendering is unchanged.

**Test:** `cmyk_tiff_keeps_its_inks` builds a synthetic CMYK TIFF (100% K + C0 M100 Y100 K0), exports plain and PDF/X-4, and checks for one DeviceCMYK image with the original samples. Before the fix it reads `DeviceRGB` `(0,0,0)/(255,0,0)`. A unit test in `designcraft-images` covers 8-bit, 16-bit, CMYK+alpha, RGB and truncated TIFFs.

Ran: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-images -p designcraft-pdf --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p designcraft-images -p designcraft-pdf`, `cargo xtask layers`, all green. Not run locally: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 target here) and the full `cargo xtask ci`.

Not covered: planar CMYK and JPEG-compressed CMYK TIFFs (they fall back to RGB with the warning), and `check_pdfx4` still doesn't flag DeviceRGB images under a CMYK output intent (the issue's fallback suggestion).

Fixes #35

title: PDF/X-4: flag device RGB under the CMYK output intent
author: EthanSuquet
body:
`check_pdfx4` didn't look at colour spaces, so a placed RGB image went into a PDF/X-4 file as DeviceRGB under the CMYK output intent with no warning (#35's fallback). PDF/X-4 (ISO 15930-7) allows RGB only if it's colour-managed: ICCBased, or DeviceRGB remapped by a `DefaultRGB`. DeviceCMYK and DeviceGray are the intent's own values.

- When the output intent's profile is CMYK, the check reads the exported file with hayro-syntax (already a dependency) and walks each page: content, images, forms (placed PDFs), patterns, shadings, soft masks and transparency groups. Recursion is bounded (depth limit plus a visited set).
- It reports DeviceRGB images (object number and px size), RGB fills and strokes, gradients, inline images and RGB-blending groups, each with its pages, e.g. `PDF/X-4: an RGB image (object 53, 1400 × 1812 px) on page 1: under a CMYK output intent RGB needs an ICC profile`. Like the other PDF/X findings, these are export warnings.
- The separate "some transparency groups still blend in RGB" warning is gone; the group check covers it, with the page.

**Tests (synthetic):**
- RGB PNG → flagged.
- RGB swatch fill → flagged.
- DeviceRGB with a `DefaultRGB` in scope → not flagged.
- RGB page group and RGB inline image → flagged; grey inline image → not.
- CMYK box, grey PNG, ICC-tagged RGB PNG and a placed PDF holding a CMYK image → no warnings.

The RGB tests fail without the change. The built-in sample magazine exported as PDF/X-4 now gets 2 warnings, both for its RGB photos.

Ran `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-pdf -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` for both crates and `cargo xtask layers`, all green. Not run locally: `xtask wasm`.

Independent of #55. A trial merge with it is clean, and #55's `cmyk_tiff_keeps_its_inks` (which asserts a warning-free PDF/X-4) still passes.

Refs #35, #55

title: Control: close the connection on input that isn't a request
author: Luskish
body:
Same bug as storytold/filmcraft#119. The control server answers a non-JSON line with an error and keeps reading. So while `--control` is open, a web page's cross-origin POST to `127.0.0.1:<port>` gets its JSON body run as a command.

Ports LightCraft's fix (storytold/lightcraft#129):

- A line that isn't a JSON object with a string `method` gets one error reply, then the connection closes.
- Lines over 4 MiB are refused, and at most 16 connections are served at once.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the rules.

`designcraft-cli mcp --connect` sends valid requests, so it's unaffected.

**Testing:** new tests in `control_server.rs` cover the browser POST and other junk input. They failed before the fix and pass now. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p designcraft`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` all pass.

title: Data merge: linked source, placeholders, preview, and tiled merge
author: CameronGilroy
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of data merge, specified in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-data-merge-design.md`.

A document links one CSV, TSV, text, or Excel file. Placeholders mark text, images, QR codes, and hyperlinks. Preview shows one record in the session and is not saved. Create Merged Document writes a new document: one record per page, or several records tiled on a single non-facing page. The template and its undo stack stay as they were. A missing or changed data file is marked, and the merge still uses the cached rows.

title: Complete Arabic translations, refine Chinese terminology, and cache RTL label layouts
author: ShaoWenbinSaleh
body:
This PR fills gaps in Arabic interface translations, refines Chinese and Arabic terminology, and reduces repeated translation lookup and RTL layout work during UI rendering.

### 1. Complete Arabic translation coverage

- Add 393 Arabic translation entries, increasing the Arabic table from 1,006 to 1,399 entries.
- Cover every key currently present in the shared interface translation table, including menu commands, panels, dialogs, preferences, and utility labels.
- Revise existing Arabic terminology, including using `عينات الألوان` for “Swatches” and consistent wording for related commands.

### 2. Refine Chinese and Arabic feature terminology

Revise feature names and related labels using terminology from public Adobe InDesign help where verified. Changes cover areas such as typography, styles, color management, layout, and preferences.

Project-specific labels remain original translations. These changes do not claim exact equivalence with every label in an official Adobe interface.

title: Transform: Rotate and Shear open their dialogs (#34)
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #34.

Object › Transform › Rotate… and Shear… (and Basic Feather) did nothing. The command form parser dropped any parameter written as `key (description)`, so those commands had no required field, opened no dialog and ran with their defaults. The key is now the leading word and the parenthetical becomes its hint, so each item opens its dialog.

Also:
- Double-clicking the Selection, Rotate, Scale or Shear tool opens the Move, Rotate, Scale or Shear dialog.
- The Scale and Shear tools get their own icons. They used Free Transform's drawing. Both are drawn in code in the icon set's stroke weight; Free Transform keeps its drawing.

Validation: `transform_menu_items_open_their_dialogs` and `transform_tools_have_their_own_icons` fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Show an alert when a file can't be opened or placed
author: aiongg
body:
A file that can't be opened or placed used to fail quietly: the reason went only to the status line, which is easy to miss.

- A file that can't be opened or placed now shows an alert with the file name and the reason, as well as the status line. This covers File › Open, Place, a drop and the command line. Scripted `engine.execute` errors stay in the status line, and the control channel's `app.open` returns its error in the response.
- The alert's title says which it was: "Can't Open the File" or "Can't Place the File" (translated, with an OK button only).
- Dropped files keep their routing (documents open, anything else is placed); the rule is now one function, `opens_as_document`, shared by drops on the desktop and the web inbox.

INDD support is discussed in #114.

Validation: `dropping_an_unreadable_file_alerts` and `file_open_failures_show_an_alert` fail before the change; `dropped_documents_open_and_the_rest_is_placed` pins the drop routing and `other_command_errors_stay_in_the_status_line` the scripted and control-channel cases. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Text: kerning survives a colour change (#29)
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #29.

Each formatting run was shaped on its own. So a pair split by a colour, underline or other paint-only change lost its kerning, and also its ligatures and Arabic joining across the change.

Now the pieces of a paragraph whose shaping attributes are equal are shaped as one run, and each glyph takes the style of its cluster. Shaping attributes are everything except fill, stroke, underline and strikethrough options, skew, ruby, kenten, conditions, tracked insertion and XML tags. A cluster that would span two styles, such as a ligature over a colour change, is still shaped apart, so each letter keeps its colour.

Validation: `colour_change_keeps_kerning_and_ligatures_keep_colour` fails before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.



Update: upstream main is merged in, and the conflicts are resolved (listed in the merge commit). No other changes. `cargo xtask ci` passes (on the combined branch).

title: Images: PSD composites decode by colour mode
author: aiongg
body:
Placed PSDs could render in the wrong colours or disappear. The `psd` crate assigns colours by the number of channels, not by colour mode:
- grayscale files with extra alpha or spot channels came out yellow, blue or invisible;
- RGB with one spot channel was read as RGBA.

The crate can also crash the app: truncated or corrupted files hit a slice out of bounds, 16-bit files an index out of bounds, and ZIP compression an `unimplemented!`.

This decodes the merged composite of `.psd` and `.psb` files in `designcraft-images` from the public file format spec, and removes the `psd` dependency:
- Channels map by colour mode: Bitmap, Grayscale, Duotone, Indexed (palette), RGB, CMYK (the uncalibrated formula used for other CMYK images) and Lab. 8 and 16 bit, raw and PackBits.
- The first extra channel is the transparency only when the layer count is negative (also read from the `Lr16`/`Lr32` blocks), and it is un-matted from white. Other alpha and spot channels are ignored, as in a layout app's preview.
- Damaged, truncated or oversized files return `None` without panicking. Dimensions and allocations are capped and the arithmetic is checked.

Screen rendering and PDF export use the same decoder. This doesn't change how CMYK reaches PDF; #55 covers that for TIFF.

Validation:
- 16 tests in `designcraft-images` build small PSDs in memory, covering each mode, the transparency rules, PSB, truncations, corruption and hostile headers. With the `psd` crate, the colour-mode tests fail and the truncated, 16-bit and ZIP cases panic.
- End to end, synthetic grayscale PSDs with 1–5 channels, flat and layered, placed through IDML and exported to PDF, render mid grey 150 / dark 60. Before, they came out yellow, blue-tinted or invisible. The screen render matches.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

One judgement call: where the merged transparency is partial, colours are un-matted from white, so soft edges don't get white halos. The public spec doesn't state this.

title: Layout: first baselines, Jump Object wrap, drop caps, IDML defaults
author: aiongg
body:
Text layout fixes: first baselines, Jump Object wrap, drop caps (which were imported but never laid out), the defaults IDML files assume, and object-style inheritance.

**First baseline**
- *Ascent* uses the font's typographic ascender (OS/2 `sTypoAscender`), falling back to the ascent.
- *Cap Height* and *x Height* use the font's cap and x heights (OS/2, else the `H` / `x` outline), with plausibility checks.

**Text wrap: Jump Object**
- A line clears the wrap with its leading box, `[baseline − leading, baseline]`. It stays above the object while its baseline is at or above the wrap top, so descenders may hang into the wrap.
- The next line moves down by whole leadings from the line above, after any space before or after.
- A column that starts under an object starts as if the frame top were the wrap bottom.
- Other wraps that leave no usable slot (a full-width bounding box) push the line exactly to the wrap bottom, instead of stepping down 1 pt at a time.
- Lines aligned to the baseline grid snap back onto the grid after a push.
- Wrap offsets, negative ones included, set the wrap's edges.

**Drop caps**
- `dropCapLines` / `dropCapChars` were imported and exported but never laid out. The first N characters now span the lines: the cap sits on line N's baseline with its top at line 1's cap height, the lines beside it are indented by its advance, and no baseline moves.
- The drop cap's character style applies, and nested styles count the drop cap characters.
- *Align Left Edge*, on by default: the cap's ink starts at the indent. Characters are counted as code points without splitting a cluster.
- Short paragraphs, column breaks and right-to-left text are handled. Vertical frames get no drop cap.
- Caret placement, hit-testing and selection work on the cap. Drop cap fields are in Paragraph Style Options › Drop Caps and Nested Styles.

**Defaults for attributes an IDML file leaves out (and the model's defaults)**
- Keep Lines Together defaults to *At Start/End of Parag…

title: Text editing, snapping and text threading (#23)
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #23.

Text editing, snapping and text threading: fixes and missing pieces in the Selection and Type tools.

**Text editing (#23)**
- Double-clicking a text frame with the Selection tool edits its text, with the caret where you clicked.
- Clicking selects by count: 2 clicks the word or run of spaces, 3 the line, 4 the paragraph, 5 the story (`text.selectAt`; pointer events carry `clicks`). egui reports double clicks only on release, so the canvas counts presses itself.
- The caret moves past spaces typed at the end of a line.
- Bold and Italic (Shift+Cmd+B / Shift+Cmd+I, and B / I in the Character panel) toggle the family's own styles, keeping the other trait. Formatting chosen at a caret applies to what is typed next.
- Copy, Cut and Paste reach the system clipboard however they are chosen, including the native macOS menu.
- Formatting Affects Text (J, Tools panel) sends swatches, colours, tints, None, Swap and Default to the text of the selected frames. The Swatches and Color panels show the text's colours.

**Snapping**
- When the snap zone is wider than the baseline grid spacing (66 % zoom and below with a 12 pt grid), frames always snapped to the grid and couldn't reach the margins. The grid and the guides now compete by distance, and a tie goes to the guide.
- Frames drawn with the Type tool snap like the frame tools'.

**Threading**
- The document model could thread frames, but nothing let a person do it.
- New commands, all undoable: `text.thread {from?, to?, rect?, autoflow?}`, `text.unthread {frame?, side?}` and `text.removeFromThread`. Invalid threads (to itself, to a non-text item, backwards) are errors that change nothing.
- With the Selection tool, clicking a selected frame's in or out port (or the red + of overset text) loads the text. Then:
  - click a frame to thread it;
  - click empty space for a frame one column wide, down to the bottom margin;
  - drag to make a frame that size;

title: CJK: language-aware shaping and fallback, vertical metrics, document fonts, missing-glyph boxes (builds on #75)
author: aiongg
body:
**Builds on #75.** This branch is based on #75's commit (`02c5f61`), so until #75 merges the diff here includes it. Once #75 is in, I'll rebase this onto `main` and only our 16 commits will remain. #75 adds composite fonts, kinsoku, aki/tsume/jidori, hanging punctuation and the Arabic work. This adds the CJK foundations next to it: language, fallback, vertical text, and documents' own fonts.

**Fixes for #75**
- **`locl` never applies for most languages.** #75's `language_tag` maps only Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Hebrew and English. Every other name reaches harfrust as written ("Japanese", "Turkish", "Chinese: Simplified"), and that gives no OpenType language. This branch uses one mapping for every language in the list (CJK 1.1, 1.11 and the locale-code commit), and keeps #75's surrounding-text and script context. `language_picks_localized_forms_through_the_word_cache` (a Turkish dotted i) and `chinese_and_japanese_take_their_localized_forms` (直, which needs the craft-fonts build) fail on #75 alone.
- **Vertical text:** #75 still adds `vert`/`vrt2` to every run, so Latin in vertical frames is turned twice and comes out upside down and mirrored. CJK 1.6 replaces this; #75's `hkna → vkna` applies to upright runs.
- **Threading drops the column direction:** threading or breaking a thread makes new stories for the frames split off, and they came out left to right even when the thread was right to left. They now keep both the column direction and vertical (CJK 1.7; `frames_keep_their_column_direction_through_threading` fails without the fix).
- **Korean under a kinsoku set:** a set allowed a break between any two CJK characters, which split Korean between syllables. It now keeps Korean's word breaking.
- **Composite fonts and kenten** look fonts up through the document's own fonts (CJK 1.9) and follow the missing-glyph setting.
- **Font loading race** (also on `main`): a parallel fallback lookup could take a family's bold before its regular had loaded. With fallback on, #75'…

title: Compose: an empty paragraph takes its mark's character format
author: denizkoekden
body:
## Summary An empty paragraph's line height now comes from the character format of its **paragraph mark**, not from the paragraph style. ## Why A paragraph with no glyphs fell back to `base_chars`, the paragraph style's character properties, in `line_metrics`. InDesign sizes an empty line by its paragraph mark instead: in IDML, that is the `CharacterStyleRange` holding the paragraph's `
`. A common case is a paragraph style at 12 pt with every character, the empty line included, set to 8.5 pt / 10 pt leading. That empty line took 14.4 pt instead of 10 pt and pushed the following text into overset. It showed up in IDML files where a blank line separates a name from a subtitle. ## Change `compose` resolves the character format at the paragraph's start (`Story::char_format_at`, which is the mark of an empty paragraph) and uses it for that paragraph's line metrics. Non-empty paragraphs are unchanged: they still use their glyphs' metrics. ## Test plan - [x] New regression test `empty_paragraph_takes_its_marks_format`. It fails without the change (empty line advances 14.4) and passes with it (8). - [x] `cargo test -p designcraft-compose`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fonts: read Microsoft Office's bundled fonts on macOS
author: denizkoekden
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the system font scan now also reads the fonts that Microsoft Office bundles inside its apps (`<App>.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts`): Calibri, Cambria, Candara, Consolas and others.

## Why

Office for Mac does not install its fonts system-wide. Documents set in Calibri, which is very common in IDML coming from Office-heavy workflows, therefore fell back to the default family even when Office was installed. InDesign on the same Mac finds them.

## Change

`system_font_dirs()` adds the `DFonts` folder of the first installed Office app: Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Outlook. They all bundle the same set. The fonts are read in place and nothing is copied. If Office isn't installed, nothing changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p designcraft-fonts`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-fonts --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] Manual check with Office installed: an IDML using Calibri Light/Bold renders in Calibri instead of the fallback.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: INDD: clean-room InDesign document (.indd) import
author: denizkoekden
body:
## Summary

Adds **InDesign document (`.indd`) import**. A new crate, `designcraft-indd`, converts the binary document into an IDML package in memory, and the existing IDML importer takes it from there. `.indd` files open through File → Open, drag-and-drop, `file.open` / `file.openBytes`, the CLI (`--in x.indd`) and the web shell.

The roadmap currently lists INDD as "not readable clean-room". This PR shows that it can be read clean-room, at least for the common subset.

## Clean-room provenance

- The format was worked out only from InDesign documents I created myself, by comparing their bytes with the PDFs I exported from them.
- No Adobe code, SDK headers, format documentation or InDesign bundle contents were read or used.
- No InDesign-produced file is committed. The tests build synthetic documents byte by byte (`crates/indd/src/synthetic.rs`).
- The format notes are in `docs/indd.md`.

## What is read

- **Container:** 4 KiB pages, master pages (newest save sequence), the shadow-paged root and the logical page map, the UID B-trees (location and class), split records and multi-page objects.
- **Document:** spread order, pages (bounds, transform), layers (order), page items (rectangles/polygons, text frames, groups) with path geometry, transforms, visibility, fill/stroke colour, tint and weight.
- **Swatches:** CMYK, RGB and Lab; process and spot.
- **Styles and stories:** paragraph and character styles with `BasedOn` and local overrides (font family, style, size, leading, auto-leading, colour, justification); stories built from the text, paragraph-run and character-run strands.
- **Placed graphics:**
  - Embedded PDF/AI is written as `<PDF>` with `Contents`.
  - Embedded EPS uses its TIFF preview. Palette TIFFs are converted to PNG, since the image decoder reads only RGB/grey TIFFs.
  - Links without embedded data use InDesign's proxy image.

## Not yet

Text frame insets, first-baseline options, vertical justification, threading, tracking and kerning, master pa…

title: IDML: resolve nested packaged image links after relocation
author: skylartaylor
body:
## Summary
Relocated IDML packages could lose nested linked images or select a different file with the same basename. A successful flat fallback also left `asset.link` pointing to the original computer.

- Try safe relative paths and preserve the suffix below `Links/` before basename fallbacks, accepting Windows and Unix separators.
- Record the resolved absolute path so preflight and link updates use the packaged file.
- Keep filesystem lookup native-only; the WASM path is unchanged.

## Validation
This standalone branch was tested independently against `main` at `f17397c305ecda9d644105f7a4e9b9d65d34bb60`:
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask ci`: all six gates passed (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, WASM), 584 tests passed, 2 ignored, 0 failed.
- Synthetic regressions cover a nested Windows author-machine path, a conflicting root-level basename, and resolved link status for nested and flat packages.
- A separately rebuilt CLI restored the missing back artwork in a relocated package and reported the linked asset as `ok`.

Tested on Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.99.0, including WASM compilation. Windows paths are simulated; Windows/macOS runtime behavior was not exercised. Only source and synthetic tests are included.

## Scope and nearby work
One-file fix based directly on `main`; no dependency on an open PR. #85 adds document-font setup in this file and #98 adds nearby INDD routing, so those changes should be preserved during any later rebase. This does not change image decoding or recursively scan directories.

title: IDML: honor explicit cell edges at table borders
author: skylartaylor
body:
## Summary
The table perimeter always replaced cell-edge strokes after IDML import, so an explicitly cleared edge could acquire an unwanted border.

- Preserve a per-edge override flag in the document model when IDML `StrokePriority` is positive.
- Use an explicit cell stroke, including `None`, at the table perimeter and export its priority.
- Default older native documents to no overrides, preserving their existing behavior.

## Validation
This standalone branch was tested independently against `main` at `f17397c305ecda9d644105f7a4e9b9d65d34bb60`:
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo xtask ci`: all six gates passed (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, WASM), 586 tests passed, 2 ignored, 0 failed.
- Synthetic tests cover explicit `None`, custom strokes, merged cells, old native JSON, serialization, `blank_like`, and IDML import/export round-trip with positive, zero, and absent edge priorities.
- A separately rebuilt CLI rerendered three affected guide-layout pages; visual inspection confirmed the unwanted borders were removed.

Tested on Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.99.0, including WASM compilation. Windows/macOS runtime behavior was not exercised. Only source and synthetic tests are included.

## Scope and nearby work
Five-file fix based directly on `main`; no dependency on an open PR. #75/#85 change RTL table geometry and #83 touches nearby table/IDML code. Their changes should be preserved during any later rebase.

Positive numeric priorities are normalized to 1 on export. General priority ordering between adjacent cells and table/region-style materialization remain separate work.

title: i18n: add Brazilian Portuguese (pt-br) UI translation
author: RicSchonfelder
body:
### What

Adds **Brazilian Portuguese (`pt-br`)** as a supported interface language (**Edit › Interface Language**).

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/pt_br.rs` — new catalog following the existing `ar.rs` module pattern: `pub(super) const TABLE: &[(&str, &str)]` with **1005 (en, pt-br) pairs**, covering exactly the same key set as `ar.rs`, written from the English source in ordinary Brazilian Portuguese computing vocabulary (Arquivo, Editar, Exibir, Janela, Ajuda, camada, traçado, amostra, quadro de texto, sangria …). Product/technology names stay in Latin letters; dialog commands keep the trailing `…`; placeholders (`{count}`, `{pages}`, `{spreads}`, `{missing}`), whitespace and punctuation match the EN column.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs` — registers `("pt-br", "Português (Brasil)")` in `LANGUAGES` (which also drives `app.language` validation) and dispatches `lang == "pt-br"` in `i18n::tr`, mirroring the Arabic branch. `is_rtl()` is untouched (pt-br is LTR).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` — adds the `Português (Brasil)` entry to the Interface Language submenu and documents `pt-br` in the `app.language` command help.

### Validation

- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo test --workspace --locked` ✅ — all suites pass, including the extended `i18n::tests::translates_known_strings_and_keeps_the_rest`, `menus::tests::interface_language_switches_and_validates` (pt-br switch + every menu title translated, with `Layout` as the natural PT-BR loanword) and `arabic_dialog_and_language_switch_keep_finite_widget_geometry` (now also exercises `pt-br`).

Notes: `Layout` is kept identical to English because it is the natural Brazilian Portuguese word (InDesign BR uses it too); a handful of other loanwords (OK, Web, Interface, Rubi/Ruby, Linhas Col ← …) intentionally stay identical. Docs/README are untouched: no file in the repo lists the supported interface languages.

title: Render: keep outside-aligned strokes out of closed interiors
author: skylartaylor
body:
Fixes closed outside-aligned strokes painting the inside of the shape. The old even-odd operation filled the center of an already-hollow stroke outline. The stroke now draws in its own layer, with the filled path subtracted from it.

Added eight synthetic pixel tests for fills, transparency, opacity, compound paths, stroke widths, open paths, joins, dashes, transforms and render threads.

Tests:
- cargo xtask ci: all six gates passed, including WASM. 590 passed, 2 ignored, 0 failed.
- Five of the six initial pixel tests failed before the fix; all eight final tests pass.
- Two real-layout pages regain their white interiors while keeping the artwork, outlines and shadows. The input and fonts were held fixed.

Based directly on main, with no PR dependencies. #83 adds an inside-stroke test but doesn't change the outside-stroke code. Text-layout issues are separate.

Tested on Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.99.0; Windows/macOS runtime behavior wasn't tested. Only source and synthetic tests are included.

title: IDML: import scalar InsetSpacing property values
author: skylartaylor
body:
Fixes scalar InsetSpacing properties being ignored. A property with type="unit" and value 9 now gives all four edges a 9 pt inset, just like the existing attribute and list forms.

Property elements still take precedence over attributes. Malformed and non-finite values are ignored, and finite negative insets still work.

Tests:

author: skylartaylor

Review caught two regressions in the first version: a second line could overlap on a text path, and keep-chain rollback could empty an earlier frame. Both are fixed and covered by tests, including a check that satisfiable keep chains still move together.

Tests:

title: About: contributor and model credits compiled in (grab bag + table, self-submitted names)
author: echelon
body:
Adds contributor credits to the About window, per craftrules [`standards/contributors.md`](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/pr/contributors-json/standards/contributors.md).

- **About · Contributors · Models** tabs. Contributors shows every contributor as a grab bag or a table (one line each: @username, PRs, commits, +LOC, −LOC, ΔLOC, +binary, −binary, first/last commit), sortable by every field; alphabetical sorting is case-insensitive and ignores the `@`. title: Data merge phase 2: JSON, several sources, filters, and record grids
author: CameronGilroy
body:
Stacks on #76. Merge that first. The commits through `a2078ec` are phase 1. Phase 2 starts at `ba3314b`.

## Summary

- Several linked sources. Select adds a source. Passing an id replaces that source and keeps its enable flag, filter, and sort. JSON is a top-level array of objects, next to CSV, text, and Excel.
- Enabled sources are concatenated in panel order. Each output record comes from one source. Placeholders for the other sources are blank. Each source has a filter and a sort.
- A drawn grid repeats its children, one record per cell. A document may have any number of grids, including several on one page and on a multi-page or facing template. The grids share one record cursor.

- The grid draws its cell lines, and the frame and dividers can be selected.

title: UI: text fields take Select All, Copy, Cut, Paste, Undo and Redo from the Mac menu (#30)
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #30.

On macOS the menu bar takes Cmd+A, Cmd+C, Cmd+X, Cmd+V, Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z before the window sees them. In a panel, dialog or search field these ran the document's commands instead: Select All selected every frame, Paste pasted into the layout, and Undo undid the last change to the document.

While a text field has keyboard focus, these Edit items now act on the field, whether they're chosen by shortcut or from the menu. Select All, Undo and Redo reach the field as their keys and Copy and Cut as clipboard events; Paste asks the window for the system clipboard. The items stay enabled for the field even when the document has nothing to copy or undo. With no field focused, and for every other item, the menu works as before. Windows, Linux and the web build have no native menu bar and already left these keys to the field.

Validation: `native_select_all_selects_the_focused_fields_text`, `native_paste_and_copy_act_on_the_focused_field`, `native_undo_and_redo_act_on_the_focused_field` and `native_editing_items_are_enabled_for_a_focused_field` fail before the change. Without a focused field, Select All still selects the document's items. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: UI: toolbars that don't fit the window switch to two columns or scroll (#57)
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #57.

In a window too short or too narrow for them, the Tools panel, the Control panel and the application bar were cut off, and the tools and controls past the edge couldn't be reached.

- Tools panel: when one column doesn't fit the window's height, the tools are laid out in two columns. The single/double-column preference doesn't change, so one column comes back when the window grows again. While the window forces two columns, the column toggle is disabled. If two columns still don't fit, the panel scrolls vertically.
- Control panel: scrolls sideways when its controls are wider than the window. Its height stays the same, and popups open under the scrolled control.
- Application bar: when the menus are drawn in the window (Windows, Linux, web), the workspace controls follow the menus instead of overlapping them, and the bar scrolls sideways when it's too narrow.

A plain mouse wheel scrolls these one-direction bars. A thin floating scroll bar shows only when something overflows, so nothing changes while everything fits. Tool buttons, icon buttons and the Fill proxy now carry accessibility labels, which the tests use to find them.

Validation: `a_short_window_reaches_every_tool`, `tools_take_two_columns_while_one_does_not_fit`, `a_narrow_window_scrolls_the_control_bar` and `a_narrow_window_scrolls_the_app_bar` fail before the change. At 1400×900, `a_tall_window_keeps_one_column_and_does_not_scroll` and `a_wide_window_does_not_scroll_the_bars` check that nothing moves. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Compose: don't panic when a hyphenated paragraph starts with a no-break letter
author: IHAGI-c
body:
`hyphenation_points` walks each word up to the first glyph that isn't a letter or is marked No Break. When the paragraph's first glyph is itself a No Break letter, that walk stops at once (`j == i == 0`) and the next line reads `glyphs[j - 1]`, which panics. Hyphenation is on by default, so any paragraph that starts with a No Break letter hits it.

To reproduce with v0.2.1:

```
designcraft-cli run --sample \
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[36,36,300,200],"content":"text"}' \
  --cmd 'text.insert={"text":"Extraordinarily long words"}' \
  --cmd 'text.select={"story":65,"anchor":0,"focus":15}' \
  --cmd 'type.char={"attrs":{"noBreak":true}}' \
  --export out.png
```

```
panicked at crates/compose/src/lib.rs:1949:39:
index out of bounds: the len is 26 but the index is 18446744073709551615
```

Nothing up to the next breakable letter can be hyphenated, so the loop now moves on by one glyph. Later in a paragraph this case already came out as a skip (the empty range fails the `b > a` check), so only the start of a paragraph behaves differently.

Tests:
- New `hyphenation_skips_a_no_break_word_at_the_start`: panics on main (`attempt to subtract with overflow` at `crates/compose/src/lib.rs:2085` in the test build), passes with the fix, and checks the No Break word stays whole on the first line.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-compose`: 100 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-compose --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: Images: set SVG text in the shared fonts when the bundled ones lack it
author: IHAGI-c
body:
Text in a placed SVG is set by usvg against a font database that holds only the bundled faces and the craft-fonts Japanese ones. Anything else comes out wrong: a family the SVG names but that we don't bundle falls back to Source Serif 4, and Korean, Arabic and other scripts the bundled faces don't cover draw as missing-glyph boxes. This shows up with charts and diagrams from tools that keep their labels as `<text>` rather than outlines.

This plugs usvg's font resolver into the shared `FontDb`, the same fonts a text frame uses:
- A named family that isn't loaded yet is looked up with `has_family` and its styles are added before usvg's own query runs.
- A character no loaded face covers goes to `fallback_for`. usvg doesn't pass a language, so Hangul, kana and Bopomofo get their language's chain and everything else gets the loaded-then-installed fallback. A face usvg has already tried ends the search, since usvg keeps asking until the selector gives up.

Faces are handed to usvg as `Source::Binary` over the shared face's bytes, so the font data isn't copied, and each face is added once per tree (a collection file brings its other faces along; we pick ours by index). Looking a family up can trigger the first scan of installed fonts, the same cost a text frame pays. On the web, `FontDb` has no installed fonts, so nothing changes there.

The synthetic test fonts in `designcraft_fonts::testing` now carry a PostScript name (name ID 6). fontdb rejects fonts without one, so usvg couldn't see them.

Tests:
- New `svg_text_uses_the_shared_fonts`: a family named in the SVG is used, and Hangul without a family gets real glyphs from a shared face instead of the default's missing-glyph box. Without the resolver both fail (both come out as .notdef: the named case in Source Serif 4, the other in Source Sans 3).
- `cargo test -p designcraft-images` (23) and `-p designcraft-fonts` (45): pass.
- `cargo check -p designcraft-images --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: builds.
- clippy `-D w…

title: Honor MCP typing, story, and page contracts
author: skylartaylor
body:
Explicit `type_text` now inserts at a live document caret or replaces its range after `text.select` or `text.placeCaret`, including with the Selection tool active. Connected typing preserves input to focused UI fields and dialogs.

`story.get` rejects a nonexistent story before querying composition. Headless and connected render/export requests reject supplied invalid or out-of-range pages before rendering or writing. Omitted pages retain the existing defaults: page zero headlessly and the current page in the connected app.

title: Preserve browser import intent and document targets
author: skylartaylor
body:
Browser file reads now retain Open/Place/swatches intent and the originating document UID. A delayed Place reactivates its original document, or cancels clearly if it was closed. Native and IDML Place merge content into that document; Open retains its separate-document behavior.

Multipage browser PDFs now use the existing page/crop dialog with retained bytes and filename. Confirmation resolves the target again; cancellation, closure or dialog replacement releases the payload. Additional deliveries while a modal is unresolved are cancelled with a visible retry message. Native PDF confirmation also resolves its originating UID. PDF page numbers are checked before narrowing so oversized values cannot wrap to another page on Wasm.

Real Chrome checks reproduced all three original bugs and verified targeting, Place/Open, undo/redo, cancellation and closed-tab reuse. Poppler rendering confirmed that selecting PDF page two exports its green content rather than red page one. Independent review found no actionable issues, reran all eleven import tests and verified delayed placement in optimized Chrome.

Fixes #89.

Fixes #91.

title: Preserve typed values in generic command dialogs
author: skylartaylor

Existing boolean handling, string conversion, optional blank omission, field allowlisting and error retention remain.

title: README: install on Gentoo from the ::snakebyte overlay
author: switch87

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger, so every `log::warn!` / `log::error!` in the workspace is discarded: the engine's panic hook report, a failed crash-recovery save, font folders that can't be read, the app icon failing to load. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal either, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app's own crash guard had already decided to switch GPU backends and its warning explaining why went nowhere. A log file next to the settings would have shown it in the first minute.

## What

`apps/designcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (just `log`):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `<settings dir>/logs/designcraft.log`, next to `ui.json` and `prefs.json` (Linux `~/.config/designcraft/logs/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/DesignCraft/logs/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\DesignCraft\logs\`).
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `designcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start, which is when a user notices and files the issue.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the settings directory is known are buffered (max 512, with a "N earlier lines dropped" note) and written once the file is attached.
- **Levels:** `info` for `designcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else (wgpu/naga/zbus are chatty at info). `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable log directory or a failed write (full disk) drops the file sink and keeps standard error; lock poisoning is handled.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first (before the engine's panic hook is set up with the first `Session`), and t…

title: IDML: preserve anchored text frames and footnote artwork

Measure inline objects by geometry, fill open contours, reject cyclic frame references, and distinguish unplaced stories from located overset text.

Add synthetic round-trip, composition, preflight, pixel-rendering, and PDF regressions. Update the roadmap with the supported import and rendering paths.

title: Fix composite font resolution, missing-glyph diagnostics, and document-wide font replacement
author: ShaoWenbinSaleh
body:
## Summary

Imported documents can resolve composite fonts as ordinary font families, miss fonts inherited through styles, and render generated footnote labels with incomplete glyph fallback. Font inventory and preflight can also disagree with the fonts actually used for rendering.

This PR unifies font resolution across composition, font inventory, replacement, and preflight. It preserves composite font references during IDML import/export, prompts users to resolve missing fonts when opening documents, and recommends replacement faces using the characters actually present in the document.

## Changes

### Composite font import and resolution

- Resolve composite fonts through their IDML resource identity while preserving their display names.
- Export composite AppliedFont values as object references instead of registering composite definitions as ordinary font families.
- Share composite font lookup between composition, font inventory, and preflight.
- Report the component fonts selected by actual document characters, avoiding missing-font reports for unused components.
- Include nested table cells, footnotes, and endnotes in font usage and replacement traversal.

### Document-wide font replacement

- Resolve effective font family and style against the original paragraph and character styles before redefining styles.
- Replace fonts inherited through formatting, including cases where family and style are inherited independently.
- Update composite font components and nested text.
- Validate replacement families and explicitly requested styles.
- Normalize replacement names to the resolved family and style.
- Select an available target style for effective text runs when no explicit target style is supplied.
- Preserve undo support for document-wide replacements.

### Missing-font workflow

- Automatically open the Find/Replace Font dialog when an opened document uses unavailable fonts or styles.
- Display the font face currently used for rendering.

title: PDF/A keeps placed images; right-to-left tables and columns
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #71. Part of #100 (parts 2 and 3; part 1, bullets splitting the first letter, no longer reproduces on main).

**PDF/A exports keep placed images (#71)**
PDF/A-2b export failed with `ImageInterpolation` whenever a document had a placed PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, including the sample. PDF/A forbids image interpolation, and every image was written with it on. The exporter now writes images without interpolation for PDF/A exports and keeps it on for plain, PDF/X-4 and booklet exports. The image cache belongs to one export, so an image can't carry the wrong setting across.

**Right-to-left tables (#100 part 3)**
- `table.convertFromText` and `table.insert` give the new table the direction of the paragraph it's made in (resolved through the paragraph style, as composition does). Right-to-left text makes a table whose first column is on the right.
- The Table panel has a Direction control (Left to Right / Right to Left) for `table.options {direction}`.

**Right-to-left columns (#100 part 2)**
- A story made in a document with right-to-left binding (`layout.documentSetup {binding: "rightToLeft"}`) fills its columns from the right. This covers text frames from `frame.create`, the Type tool, placed text, primary text frames, `object.content` turning a frame into a text frame, and type on a path, through one helper, `Document::new_story_direction`. Threaded and pasted stories keep their own direction, and changing the binding doesn't change existing stories; their direction stays with the story direction command.

Validation: new tests `archival_exports_keep_placed_images_without_interpolation` (PNG with and without alpha, JPEG, GIF, WebP; image recompression on and off; checks no `/Interpolate true` in PDF/A and that plain exports keep it), `tables_take_the_direction_of_their_paragraph` and `new_stories_follow_the_binding_direction` fail before the change. `designcraft-cli run --sample --pdf-options '{"standard":"a2b"}' --export a2b.pdf` writes 4 pages with both sample ima…

title: Fix IDML Mojikumi spacing, kinsoku composition, and nested text preflight
author: ShaoWenbinSaleh
body:
## Summary

IDML documents could retain Mojikumi table definitions without applying their spacing rules during composition. Paragraph references could remain unresolved resource IDs, while preflight reported Mojikumi as unsupported even when the engine could apply the selected rules.

This PR resolves table references and applies supported Mojikumi spacing consistently during line selection and glyph placement. It also fixes spacing allocation defects and extends typography diagnostics to nested text.

## Mojikumi table resolution and IDML import

- Resolve IDML Mojikumi resource references to their imported table names.
- Apply directional custom overrides to character-pair and line-boundary spacing.
- Use the same rule resolver for composition and preflight.
- Reject malformed or non-finite numeric values and prevent silent truncation of character-class and priority values.
- Preserve finite, representable rules outside the composer's supported range. Report unsupported rules through preflight rather than rejecting the entire document.

## Composition fixes

- Include Mojikumi minimum, desired, and maximum spacing in line-fitting calculations.
- Account for paragraph-start, line-start, and line-end spacing during both breaking and placement.
- Apply supported kinsoku push-in and push-out policies.
- Allocate continuous gaps of equal priority together, including leading and internal gaps.
- Honor discrete compression endpoints instead of leaving a line overfull when an entire endpoint adjustment is required.
- Apply leading-only compression to ragged lines when needed.
- Attach pair spacing after the complete shaped cluster so combining marks remain attached to their base glyph.
- Use shaped body width before tracking to avoid treating narrow punctuation as full-width punctuation merely because tracking increased its advance.
- Preserve explicit custom spacing and prevent generic justification from stretching fixed Mojikumi gaps.

title: macOS DMG: branded window background and icon layout
author: XusBadia
body:
## What

The macOS DMG opened as a plain white Finder window. It now opens like this:

![DesignCraft DMG window in Finder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/XusBadia/designcraft/dmg-preview/finder.png)

The icon's figure as a cover on the DesignCraft colour field, DesignCraft.app and the `Applications` link side by side on Paper, and a small DesignCraft-specific touch: the arrow and the mono line under the title come from the app's craft. Ink, Paper and the app colour only; Inter and JetBrains Mono.

## How

Same approach as PhotoCraft's and VectorCraft's, which have landed (storytold/photocraft#1201, storytold/vectorcraft#493):

- `packaging/macos/dmg/background.svg`: the source. Its text is outlined, so rendering it needs no fonts, and the figure is an `<image>` of the existing icon in `assets/app-icon/`.
- `background.tiff`: 1x 660×400 + 2x 1320×800 in one HiDPI TIFF (16-colour palette, Deflate, sRGB; 90 KB). No paper grain: noise doesn't compress, and this keeps the binary small.
- `dmg-layout.DS_Store`: Finder's view settings (window 660×400 content, icon size 128, DesignCraft.app at (326, 205), Applications at (574, 205), the background). It's named so it isn't mistaken for, or ignored like, a Finder-generated `.DS_Store`.
- `generate.py`: writes both from the SVG on any OS (`pip install 'pillow>=12' ds_store==1.3.3 mac_alias==2.2.3`, resvg on PATH). The output is byte-for-byte reproducible and carries nothing from the machine that ran it: no paths, users, disk names or volume UUIDs.

title: Images: PSD decode passes clippy on Rust 1.98
author: jahala
body:
> This is an automated AI-contribution made by an Opus 5.5 (high) agent

## Problem

On current stable (Rust 1.98.1), `cargo xtask ci` fails at the clippy step on unmodified `main` (14e677b). Rust 1.98 adds the lint `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, and it flags two loops in `crates/images/src/psd.rs`:

```
error: using `chunks_exact_mut` with a constant chunk size
   --> crates/images/src/psd.rs:147:25
error: using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size
   --> crates/images/src/psd.rs:317:22
```

These are the only two clippy findings in the workspace (`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`).

## Fix

Both loops use `as_chunks_mut::<4>()` / `as_chunks::<2>()`. These are stable since Rust 1.88, below the workspace `rust-version = "1.90"`. The chunks are now arrays, so the `try_from` that could never fail is removed. Trailing bytes that don't fill a chunk are ignored, as before.

## Evidence

- Before: `cargo xtask ci` on `main` reports `FAIL clippy`, and skips test, assets, layers and wasm.
- After: `CI summary: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)`.
- No behaviour change. The existing PSD tests in `designcraft-images` cover both loops and pass.

Three commands take a count from their parameters and use it unchecked. This is a robustness fix: the trigger is a caller that sends an absurd number, which today means an agent over MCP, a script or the control channel. title: Web: AltGr and other named keys no longer type their names (#134)
author: jahala
body:
> This is an automated AI-contribution made by an Opus 5.5 (high) agent

Closes #134.

## Root cause

eframe's web backend (0.36.2, `web/input.rs`, `text_from_keyboard_event`) turns every `keydown` into a text event unless the key is on a fixed list of names (`Alt`, `Control`, `Shift`, the arrows and so on). Browsers report more named keys than that list holds: `AltGraph`, `Dead`, `Unidentified`, the media keys. Each of those reaches the app as `Event::Text("AltGraph")`, and the canvas passes text events to `text.insert`.

Panel text fields are not affected. A focused egui text field gets the browser's hidden text input, and eframe skips the `keydown` path while that input has focus.

The list is the same on egui's `main` branch today, so a dependency bump would not fix it.

## Fix

`designcraft_ui_egui::drop_key_name_text` removes a text event that is a key name: ASCII letters and digits, starting with a capital, longer than one character. The web shell calls it from `raw_input_hook`. It does nothing while an egui text field has the keyboard, because that text comes from input events, which can hold a whole word.

The desktop app is unchanged: winit reports text separately from key names.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `main` (14e677b) in headless Chromium against a `trunk build` of the web app: Type tool, draw a frame, type `before `, press AltGr, type ` after`. The story reads `before AltGraph after`.

body:
> This is an automated AI-contribution made by an Opus 5.5 (high) agent

## Problem

In every workspace that shows the Control panel (Advanced, Typography, Printing and Proofing, Book), the second row of fields is cut off at the panel's lower edge on `main` (14e677b). In object mode that is Y, H, the second scale field and shear. In text mode it is the lower row of the character and paragraph fields. author: jahala

title: PDF: a damaged PNG, GIF or WebP is skipped, not fatal
author: jahala
body:
> This is an automated AI-contribution made by an Opus 5.5 (high) agent

## Problem

Place a PNG, GIF or WebP that is cut off (an interrupted download, for example) or has a bad checksum. The file is accepted and its frame shows empty. Exporting the document to PDF then fails completely:

```
designcraft-cli: PDF writer error: Image(Image(ImageRepr {..}), None, "unexpected end of file")
```

The message names no file, so the user cannot tell which image to replace. A damaged TIFF or BMP in the same place is handled as intended: `warning: image 'name' could not be decoded and was skipped`, and the rest of the document is exported.

Measured on `main` (14e677b) with files cut to 90% of their length, `file.new`, `file.place`, `--export out.pdf`:

| Format | On `main` | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| PNG | export fails, "unexpected end of file" | exported, image skipped with a warning |
| PNG, bad IDAT checksum | export fails, "CRC error" | exported, image skipped with a warning |
| GIF | export fails, "Unexpected End of File" | exported, image skipped with a warning |
| WebP | export fails, "corrupt bitstream" | exported, image skipped with a warning |
| BMP, TIFF | skipped with a warning | unchanged |
| JPEG | exported (the data is passed through) | unchanged |

## Root cause

`load_image` decides whether an image can be embedded by asking krilla to open it, and warns and skips when that returns nothing. krilla opens PNG, GIF and WebP lazily: `Image::from_png` reads the header and succeeds, and the pixels are decoded only when the PDF is written, where an error ends the export. TIFF and BMP are decoded by `designcraft_images::decode_rgba` first, so only they reached the skip path.

## Fix

`lossless()` decodes the image with `decode_rgba` first, for every format. A file that does not decode returns `None` and takes the existing skip-with-warning path. Undamaged PNG, GIF and WebP files still go to krilla as before, so their embedding is unchanged.

One extra d…

title: Import: RTF and Tagged Text keep characters past U+FFFF
author: jahala
body:
> This is an automated AI-contribution made by an Opus 5.5 (high) agent

## Problem

Placing an RTF or Tagged Text file drops every character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane: emoji, mathematical letters, and the rarer CJK ideographs such as 𠮷 (U+20BB7, used in Japanese names). The text around them comes in, so nothing tells the user that characters are missing.

It also breaks DesignCraft's own round trip. On `main` (14e677b), a story reading `é 中文 😀 ñ` exported with `file.exportText` as RTF or Tagged Text and placed again reads `é 中文  ñ`.

## Root cause

Both formats carry such a character as a UTF-16 surrogate pair, two units in a row:

- RTF: `\u-10179?\u-8704?` (what Word writes, and what `export::rtf` writes)
- Tagged Text: `<0xD83D><0xDE00>` (what `tagged_text` writes)

The export side is correct. Both readers passed each unit to `char::from_u32` on its own (`rtf.rs` in the `\u` handler, `tagged.rs` in the `<0x…>` handler). Half a pair is not a character, so `from_u32` returns `None` and each half was dropped.

## Fix

A small shared `Utf16Units` in `designcraft-textimport` joins the units: a first half waits for the second, and the pair becomes one character. Both readers use it. Half a pair with no partner is still left out, as before, and a first half is forgotten when other text comes in between.

`.docx` import is not affected: XML character references hold whole code points.

## Tests

`rtf::tests::surrogate_pairs_become_one_character` and `tagged::tests::surrogate_pairs_become_one_character`. Each checks a hand-written file, a round trip through the exporter, and an unpaired half. On `main` both fail with `left: "AB 田", right: "A😀B 𠮷田"`.

End to end through the CLI (`frame.create`, `file.exportText`, `file.place`, `story.get`): the story `é 中文 😀 𠮷田 𝔘𝔫𝔦 👩‍👩‍👧 🇳🇴 end` now comes back identical in both formats.

I found this with a round-trip check of 16 strings (braces, backslashes, tabs, control characters, right-to-left text and so on) through RTF, …

title: Fix relink atomicity and EPS source retention
author: skylartaylor
body:

- Write and import EPS resource types in IDML, including linked-only assets whose source is unavailable.

Native documents containing raw EPS source now declare format 2, so older builds request an update instead of silently omitting artwork. Documents without raw EPS and legacy preview-only documents continue to use format 1. Supported EPS dimensions are 0.001–20,000 points per side.
