title: feat(pptx): export documents as editable PowerPoint presentations
author: PhilippKrueger
body:
Adds PowerPoint export: every page becomes a slide of editable PowerPoint objects (shapes, pictures, text boxes and tables), not a picture of the page.

- **Where:** new `designcraft-pptx` crate (L3, next to `epub`/`idml`), `file.exportPptx` command, File › Export PowerPoint…, CLI `--export x.pptx` (and in `script --export`).
- **Command options:** `pages`, `lineBreaks: keep|reflow`, `rasterize`, `embedFonts`, `title`, `author`. The result lists warnings for anything approximated or dropped.

## What maps to what

| DesignCraft | PowerPoint |
|---|---|
| Frames | Preset rectangle/ellipse, custom geometry otherwise (corner options, polygons, paths, compound paths); rotation and flips kept |
| Fills, strokes | Solid and gradient fills, opacity; dashes, compound strokes, caps, joins, arrowheads, inside alignment |
| Effects | Drop shadow, inner shadow, outer glow, feather |
| Placed images | Pictures cropped like their frames (PNG, JPEG and GIF as they are, SVG kept as SVG with a PNG fallback, other rasters as PNG) |
| Groups, anchored objects | Groups; anchored objects placed where they show |
| Tables | Native tables: merged cells, fills, per-edge borders, cell text |
| Parent-page items | Copied onto each slide, page numbers and running heads resolved per page |
| Fonts | TrueType fonts embedded as Embedded OpenType (PowerPoint's format) when `fsType` allows |

## Text

By default (`lineBreaks: keep`) text keeps DesignCraft's composition:

- **Line breaks:** each composed line ends in a line break; the composer's hyphens stay.
- **Spacing:** justified word spacing and tracking become per-run character spacing. PowerPoint has no word spacing and doesn't justify lines that end in a manual break, so a run's spacing is chosen to keep each glyph within 0.3 pt of where the composer put it.
- **Leading:** written as *percentage* line spacing. PowerPoint rounds exact point spacing to whole points (which adds up line after line), but its 100% line is 1.2 em for every font, s…

title: Memory: release retired layouts and reserve text growth exactly
author: skylartaylor
body:
Depends on https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/175. The memory change is commit `4e4eaad`; the shared compatibility commit is included until that prerequisite lands.

Retire the session composition cache after the last document closes. Outstanding jobs keep their existing cache, while later work gets a new one. Glyph-cache entries use a weak layout identity, so cached outlines no longer keep expired composition buffers alive.

The Job test checks ownership, not queue timing or real-job font-scope ownership.

title: Swatch menus: make the whole row (chip included) clickable and show chips in the Contextual Task Bar
author: vpkoskinen
body:
## Problem

Two confirmed defects in the swatch ("colour selector") menus:

1. **Clicking the colour chip does nothing.** Every swatch menu drew its rows as
   `chip (Sense::hover) + Button(name)` and read the click from the `Button` only, so
   only the *name text* was clickable. Picking a colour by clicking its square — the
   obvious gesture — did nothing.
2. **The Contextual Task Bar's fill/stroke menus showed no colours.** Its rows were
   plain `selectable_label(name)` with no chip at all, so you only saw names/values.

The dead chip is shared by the Properties **Appearance** Fill/Stroke menus, the
Properties text Appearance menus, and the shared `swatch_picker` (Control bar, Stroke
panel, Character panel, Paragraph Border/Shading pickers). The Task Bar issue is its
own pair of menus.

## Fix

Add **one shared row helper** and use it everywhere a swatch list is drawn:

```rust
/// One swatch-menu row: a chip and the swatch name; the whole row is clickable
/// (the chip included). `name == current` highlights it. Returns true when clicked.
pub fn swatch_menu_row(ui, doc, name, current) -> bool
```

It is modelled on the Swatches panel's already-correct `swatch_row`: a full-width
`allocate_exact_size(_, Sense::click())` with the chip + RTL-safe name painted in,
current-row highlight and hover. Callers keep their own iteration, scroll height and
"picked" plumbing; the click is now read from the whole row.

- `panels/mod.rs` — the helper + `swatch_picker` uses it.
- `panels/properties.rs` — the Appearance/text `swatch_menu` uses it.
- `taskbar.rs` — both fill/stroke popups use it, so each row now shows a chip and
  stays whole-row clickable.

The popups are capped at 280 pt (`set_max_width`).
The chip controls and rows
also carry accessibility labels.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p designcraft-ui-egui` — 49 passed, 1 ignored.
- New kittest: **clicking a swatch chip in the Appearance Fill menu applies it**.
  It opens the Fill menu, asserts the row spans the menu (c…

title: fix(macos): add system clipboard fallback for paste from other apps
author: kubuntugamer
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the egui `Event::Paste` may not contain text when copying from other apps (e.g., TextEdit.app). This fix adds a fallback using the `arboard` crate to read directly from the system clipboard when the paste command fails.

### Changes

- Added `clipboard` feature to `designcraft-ui-egui` (optional, native platforms only)
- Enabled `clipboard` feature in `designcraft` desktop app
- Added `read_system_clipboard()` helper using `arboard`
- Modified Paste event handler to try system clipboard on failure

### How it works

1. User presses Cmd+V in a text field
2. egui generates `Event::Paste(t)` with text `t` from system clipboard
3. If `t` is empty or the paste command fails (e.g., "clipboard is empty"), the handler now:
   - Logs a warning
   - Attempts to read directly from system clipboard using `arboard`
   - If successful, retries the paste with the clipboard text
   - If still fails, shows error status to user

Fixes #201

title: Hyphenation: Spanish text is hyphenated with Javier Bezos's patterns
author: rossaai
body:
Refs #87, #130

## Problem

Text set in Spanish, through Character panel ▸ Language or `type.char {language}`, is never hyphenated. `foreign_ranges` in `crates/compose/src/lib.rs` collects every run whose language is not English, and `hyphenation_points` skips every word in those runs. The bundled dictionary and patterns are US English only.

## Change

- `crates/compose/Cargo.toml`: `hypher = { version = "0.1.8", default-features = false, features = ["alloc", "spanish"] }`. hypher has no dependencies, and the lock gains one package. The `full` feature stays off, so only the Spanish trie is compiled in.
- `crates/compose/src/hyphen/mod.rs`: `Lang` is `English` or `Patterns(hypher::Lang)`. `Lang::for_language` maps a language name or locale code through `designcraft_doc::language_tag` to a hyphenator, and returns `None` for a language with no patterns built in. `core_breaks` sends a non-English word to `hypher::hyphenate_bounded` with bounds 1 and 1, so the paragraph's `Limits` still set the minimum letters before and after a break. A word with an apostrophe gets no break in a pattern language. `word_breaks_in` and `hyphen_points_in` take the language. `word_breaks` and `hyphen_points` stay as the English entry points, so their callers do not change.
- `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`: `foreign_ranges` returns each non-English range with its hyphenator or `None`. `hyphenation_points` hyphenates a range whose language has one and skips the rest. The word cache key includes the language. User dictionary exceptions still win over the patterns.
- `NOTICE`: the copyright line of `hyph-es.tex` 5.0, "Copyright (C) 1993, 1997 Javier Bezos, 2001-2019 Javier Bezos, CervanTeX", and its MIT text. hypher on crates.io does not carry this notice.
- `ROADMAP.md`: the Language entry says Spanish is hyphenated.

The patterns are `hyph-es.tex` version 5.0, 2019-09-24, from hyph-utf8, MIT. hypher 0.1.8 is MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Other languages stay unhyphenated, as before. Adding one is a hyphe…

title: PDF/X-4: RGB images carry sRGB, no image interpolation, pdf:Trapped in XMP
author: rossaai
body:
Refs #71

## Problem

A PDF/X-4 export of a document with placed RGB images has three defects:

1. An RGB image with no ICC profile of its own is written as DeviceRGB under the CMYK output intent. `check_pdfx4` reports it, but the export path turns every issue into a warning, so the file is written anyway.
2. Every image constructor passes `true` for `interpolate`, so images carry `/Interpolate true`. PDF/X-4 and PDF/A do not allow it. In PDF/A the flag makes krilla's validator fail the export with `ImageInterpolation`, which is #71.
3. The document information says `/Trapped/False`, and the XMP that `make_pdfx4` appends has no `pdf:Trapped`.

## Change

`crates/pdf/src/export.rs`:

- `RasterMode` holds the two image settings for the export's standard. `interpolate` is true only for plain exports. `tag_rgb` is true only for PDF/X-4. `load_image`, `lossless`, `recompress` and `cmyk_tiff` take it.
- With `tag_rgb`:
  - A JPEG is still passed through. It keeps its own profile, and one without a profile gets sRGB through `Image::from_jpeg_with_icc`. krilla uses a profile only when its channels match the JPEG's, so a grey or CMYK JPEG without a profile stays DeviceGray or DeviceCMYK.
  - A PNG, GIF or WebP that is RGB with no profile of its own is decoded and written through `SrgbImage`, a `CustomImage` with the sRGB profile and an alpha channel only when a pixel is not opaque. A grey image, or one with its own profile, goes to krilla as before.
  - The decoded fallback for TIFF, BMP and PSD writes `SrgbImage` in place of `Image::from_rgba8`.
  - A JPEG re-encoded by `compress_images` keeps the source's RGB profile, or gets sRGB.
- The sRGB profile is `assets/icc/sRGB-v2-magic.icc`, 736 bytes, ICC v2.1, from saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles under CC0. It is byte-identical to the copy krilla 0.8.2 ships for its own sRGB space, SHA-256 `af4efe28f6d311799865f325ba39184a2e978b113ca74124d60af7de22b105f4`. A v2.1 profile is one krilla embeds in a PDF 1.6 file. `ASSETS.md` has…

title: Smart Text Reflow: deleted pages and frames stay deleted
author: noah1400
body:
Refs #165 (its second half; manual threading is #84).

With Smart Text Reflow on, a page or frame deleted from the primary story came straight back: reflow ran after every command and added pages whenever the story was overset.

Steps on main: new document with a primary text frame, type until it fills four pages, delete page 2: still four pages. Delete the story's last frame instead: five pages.

InDesign puts such pages back too, and its forums treat that as expected ([example](https://community.adobe.com/questions-671/pages-won-t-delete-in-indesign-903233)). So this is a deliberate difference from InDesign, not a parity fix; close it if you would rather keep the InDesign behaviour.

**Deleted pages and frames stay deleted**
- Reflow adds pages for a command that edits the story, first makes it overset (resize, style edit, condition shown) or makes it the primary story.
- It adds none for a command that removes pages or frames of the story, and none for an edit elsewhere while the story is already overset. The text is left overset; the next edit of the story reflows as before.
- A story that is already overset when a document is opened, or when the preference is turned on, now gets its pages at the next edit of the story, not at the next command of any kind.
- Removing empty trailing pages is unchanged.

**A finished drag reflows like the command**
- Reflow did not run when a gesture ended: a primary frame dragged shorter got its pages at the next command, whatever that was. With the rule above it would get none, so the end of a drag now reflows as the same change by command does, in the drag's undo step.

**A rename or an undo doesn't bring deleted pages back**
- Renaming a style or condition the story uses is not an edit of the story, and the layout a command is compared against is composed exactly, so one left in the cache by an undo can't be mistaken for it.

Validation: 14 new tests in `reflow_tests`; 10 fail on main, 4 pin behaviour that is kept. Locally: `c…

- Corrected two assertions in an existing data-merge test to use the platform's path separators. The test previously failed on Windows because it hard-coded Unix separators; production data-merge behavior is unchanged.

author: dylanmtaylor

The OSTree repository is unsigned, matching the existing standalone Flatpak bundles; persistent signing requires a separate key-management design.

title: chore: satisfy clippy 1.99 lints in psd.rs and select.rs
author: kubuntugamer
body:
## Where this sits in the stack

This branch is one link in the repo's existing stacked-PR chain (the open PRs #202–#233 all stack the same way). The fork's `main` is 24 commits ahead of `storytold:main` because none of those have merged yet, so **this PR's diff shows those 24 commits too**. The change *unique to this PR* is just 2 files:

```
 crates/images/src/psd.rs   |  5 ++---
 crates/tools/src/select.rs | 12 +++++-------
 2 files changed, 7 insertions(+), 10 deletions(-)
```

Please review that delta. Merge order is #250 → #251 → #252; I'll rebase each onto `main` as the one below it lands so the diffs collapse to their true size.

- `crates/tools/src/select.rs` — `manual_clamp`: `(12.0 + dy).max(0.0).min(500.0)` → `.clamp(0.0, 500.0)`.

`cargo xtask ci` runs `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and both lints are new in the 1.99 toolchain, so the gate is red on a current toolchain. No behaviour changes — these are the exact expressions clippy asks for.

author: kubuntugamer
body:

title: fix(cli): --help prints usage to stdout and exits 0
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Fixes #243.

## What

`designcraft-cli --help` printed the usage block to **stderr** and exited **1**. It now goes to **stdout** and exits **0**.

| Command | stdout | stderr | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--help`, `-h`, `help` | usage + links | *(empty)* | 0 |
| unknown arg (e.g. `--bogus`) | *(empty)* | usage + links | 1 |

`--version` is unchanged (stdout, exit 0).

## Why

Asking for help is not an error. The old behaviour made `designcraft-cli --help | less` useless and broke the usual Unix convention, which the issue notes `--version` already follows.

## How

`--help` was falling through to the catch-all `_ =>` arm that serves unknown commands. I split it out into its own `Some("--help" | "-h" | "help")` arm, and hoisted the usage text and links line into a shared `const USAGE` and `usage_footer()` so the success and failure paths can't drift apart. The catch-all keeps printing the same text to stderr and failing, so genuinely unknown options still error as before.

`-h` and `help` are handled alongside `--help` — the issue only asked for `--help`, but they're the conventional aliases and it seemed odd to leave them failing. Say the word if you'd rather keep the diff to `--help` only.

## Verification

- New regression test `help_goes_to_stdout_and_unknown_args_to_stderr` in `apps/designcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`: all three help spellings succeed with usage on stdout and empty stderr; an unknown option still fails with usage on stderr and empty stdout.
- **The test is proven to catch the bug** — reverting only `main.rs` and re-running gives `--help: ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(256))`, i.e. exit 1, and the test fails. With the fix, all 5 tests in `tests/cli.rs` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-cli --all-targets` clean (the only warnings in the workspace are the pre-existing `designcraft-images` ones that #250 fixes).

title: Word import: keep tracked moved text (w:moveTo)
author: thaynej
body:
Fixes #256.

### What
Word (.docx) import dropped text inside tracked move destinations (`w:moveTo`), so a moved passage vanished from both its old and new places. `inline()` in `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs` now goes into `moveTo` the same way it already does for `ins`. `moveFrom` stays skipped, like `del`, so tracked changes keep importing as if accepted.

### Test
New regression test `tracked_changes_import_as_accepted_including_moves`. It uses a synthetic document with `ins`, `del`, `moveFrom` and `moveTo` together, plus a `del` nested inside the `moveTo` (text moved and then deleted, which Word produces in practice). It checks that the moved text appears exactly once, at its destination, and that the moved-then-deleted text stays out. I confirmed the test fails without the fix (`"Kept text.  Plain INSERTED\nEnd."`) and passes with it.

I also checked end to end with `designcraft-cli`: `file.place` of the #256 repro now gives `Kept text. MOVED HERE. Plain INSERTED\nEnd.`. A real manuscript whose only `moveTo` holds moved-then-deleted text imports byte-for-byte the same as before.

### Local CI (Rust 1.99.0, macOS arm64)
`cargo xtask ci`: fmt passes, then **clippy fails on `main` too**, not because of this change. Clippy 1.99 added `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, which flags `crates/images/src/psd.rs:147` and `:317`. Since your workflows use `stable`, CI will likely hit this soon. I left it out of this PR to keep it small.

With that one lint allowed (`-A clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`), every remaining step passes: clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (782 passed, 0 failed), `assets`, `layers` and `wasm`.

title: test(datamerge): pin facing-page record placement (#198 no longer reproduces)
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Refs #198.

## This is a test-only PR — please read before merging

**#198 no longer reproduces on current `main`.** I picked the issue up expecting to fix it, wrote the repro, and the behaviour the reporter describes is already correct. So there is no engine change here, and I'd suggest closing #198 rather than merging anything that claims to fix it.

## What #198 reported

Against **0.1.1**, with `facingPages: true`, merged records after the first "land at identical coordinates on the same page of one spread (overlapping), and a following page is left empty." With `facingPages: false` the same merge worked.

## Why it no longer reproduces

`data.merge` has since been reworked to **build a new document** rather than duplicating pages inside the template (the old `spread` parameter is gone and now errors). Following the issue's own repro shape — a 612×792 doc, a text frame with `<<Title>> - <<Clue>>`, three records — the three copies land on absolute pages **0, 1, 2**, one record per page, none stacked.

## What I'm adding

Two regression tests in `crates/engine/src/cmd/datamerge/tests.rs`, covering both tiling plans so a future refactor of `tile_records` can't silently reintroduce the stacking:

- `facing_pages_merge_puts_each_record_on_its_own_page` — a block taller than the usable page height, so only one record fits per page. Asserts `page_count == 3` and that each frame sits on a *distinct absolute page*.
- `facing_pages_merge_tiles_short_blocks_without_stacking` — the issue's actual repro shape (short block that tiles). Asserts the three frames occupy three distinct `(page, x, y)` positions.

Both resolve the absolute page via `doc.page_loc`, inverting spread+index → page. That matters: **item bounds are page-local**, so two frames on facing pages both sit at `(72, 72)` in their own page space while page 1 appears at spread offset `612`. Comparing raw `x0/y0` alone looks like an overlap and is a false positive — I hit exactly that while writing these, which is…

title: Paragraph Rules: a dialog for the selected paragraphs and a section in Paragraph Style Options
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #191.

- Type › Paragraph Rules… and a new menu in the Paragraph panel open a Paragraph Rules dialog for the selected paragraphs. Paragraph Style Options has the same section.
- Fields: Rule Above/Below, Rule On, Weight, Color, Tint, Width (Column/Text), Offset, Left and Right Indent. That's every field of `Rule`. Values inherited from the paragraph style show in the fields.
- OK applies only the fields that were edited, in one `type.para` or `style.paragraph.edit` call, so it's one undo step. Both commands now apply a partial `ruleAbove`/`ruleBelow` object on top of the current rule instead of resetting the missing fields. An unknown rule field is an error.
- Rule Above follows the Column/Text width setting, as Rule Below already did.

#233 also adds a Paragraph Rules section, but it reads `rule_above` while the properties are `ruleAbove`, so existing rules don't show. Each edit replaces the whole rule, and Width and Overprint write fields that `Rule` doesn't have.

Limitation: a rule is stored as one value. Editing one field of an inherited rule therefore stores the whole rule on the paragraph or child style.

Validation: `a_partial_rule_keeps_the_other_fields`, `a_partial_rule_edit_keeps_the_other_fields`, `rule_above_width_follows_column_or_text`, `paragraph_rules_dialog_shows_the_rule_and_applies_one_field` and `paragraph_style_options_edit_one_rule_field` fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Autoflow: add only the pages breaks ask for
author: thaynej
body:
Fixes #262.

### What
`autoflow()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/place_text.rs` estimated how many more frames a story needs from how much its existing frames hold. A frame that a column, frame or page break ends early holds only a few characters, so the estimate came out at a page per few characters, and all of those pages were added in one batch. The estimate now uses only the frames that no break cut short. While there are none yet, autoflow adds a single page and measures again. Nothing else changes for text without breaks.

### Test
New regression test `autoflow_adds_only_the_pages_breaks_ask_for` (synthetic RTF via `\page`):
- text that starts with a page break: 2 pages in all (was 23)
- a page break between each of four paragraphs: 4 pages in all

I confirmed the test fails without the fix and passes with it. The existing `place_text_file_with_autoflow` test still passes.

End to end with `designcraft-cli`, `file.place {page: 1, autoflow: true}`:

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| the #262 synthetic .docx (leading page break) | `pagesAdded: 33` | `pagesAdded: 1` |
| a real one-page Word section with a leading page break | `pagesAdded: 271` | `pagesAdded: 1` |
| the same files without the break | 0 | 0 |

### Local CI (Rust 1.99.0, macOS arm64)
fmt, `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (782 passed, 0 failed), `assets`, `layers` and `wasm` all pass. Clippy ran with one lint allowed, `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`. Clippy 1.99 added that lint, and it fails on `main` in `crates/images/src/psd.rs`, as noted in #257.

### AI disclosure
The bug was found, and this fix and test were written, with an AI assistant (Claude Code). I'm not a Rust developer: I reviewed the test results and the before/after behavior, not the code line by line, and approved submitting it.

title: Text frames: column rules on screen, in PDF and in IDML; Column Rules in Text Frame Options
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #157.

- Multi-column text frames draw a rule in each gutter between columns, on screen and in PDF. The rule is drawn as a decoration, so it follows the frame's transform, and tagged PDF marks it as an artifact. It stops above a paragraph that spans the columns and resumes below it. Right-to-left and vertical frames work.
- Text Frame Options › Column Rules: Insert Column Rule, Weight (pt), Color, Tint, Top Inset, Bottom Inset, Horizontal Offset. OK sends only the fields that were edited, so the frame's other options are kept, and it's one undo step. The inset field is now four fields, so unequal insets survive.
- The model gains tint, horizontal offset, and top and bottom insets. Their defaults keep old documents unchanged. `object.textFrameOptions` validates them, and an unknown swatch is an error. `document.inspect` reports the rule.
- IDML: column rules are imported from frames and object styles, and exported (`ColumnRuleOverride`, `ColumnRuleStrokeWidth`, `ColumnRuleStrokeColor`, `ColumnRuleStrokeTint`, `ColumnRuleOffset`, `ColumnRuleTopInset`, `ColumnRuleBottomInset`; on export also `ColumnRuleInsetChainOverride`).

#252 also draws column rules, but it reads the weight as picas, flattens unequal insets when the dialog is confirmed, has no IDML support, and carries the 22 stacked PRs below it.

Validation: new tests in compose, engine, pdf, idml and ui-egui (`column_rules_take_their_offset_insets_and_tint`, `column_rules_set_validate_undo_and_inspect`, `column_rules_are_drawn`, `imports_column_rules_from_frames_and_object_styles`, `column_rules_round_trip`, `text_frame_options_change_only_what_was_edited`). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix(engine): object.opacity accepts its documented lowercase blend modes
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Fixes #260.

## What

`object.opacity` documents `blend?: normal|multiply|…` but only honored **PascalCase** enum names. Every documented lowercase form was silently dropped — the command returned `{"changed": 1}` while the stored blend stayed exactly as it was. A client following the command's own parameter description could save and export the previous appearance with no error, and restoring `normal` after `Multiply` silently kept `Multiply`.

## Root cause

```rust
let blend = p.get("blend").and_then(|b| serde_json::from_value(b.clone()).ok());
```

`serde_json::from_value::<BlendMode>` matches the derive's exact variant names (`Multiply`, `ColorBurn`, `SoftLight`), and `.ok()` threw away the failure. The codebase already had the right tool for this — `BlendMode::parse` in `crates/color/src/blend.rs`, which is case-, space-, `_`- and `-`-insensitive and already unit-tested. It just wasn't being used here.

## Fix

One line in `crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs`, swapping the deserializer for `BlendMode::parse`, and returning an error instead of silently ignoring an unrecognized value — matching how sibling commands (`object.fill`, `frame.create`, `transform.resize`, …) treat a bad parameter.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `multiply` | silently ignored | `Multiply` ✅ |
| `MULTIPLY` | silently ignored | `Multiply` ✅ |
| `Color Burn` | silently ignored | `ColorBurn` ✅ |
| `soft_light` | silently ignored | `SoftLight` ✅ |
| `Multiply` | `Multiply` | `Multiply` (unchanged) |
| `normal` after `Multiply` | silently kept `Multiply` | `Normal` ✅ |
| `sparkle` | `{"changed": 1}`, unchanged | error: ``unknown blend mode `sparkle` `` |

The Properties panel is unaffected — it submits serialized variant names via `json!({"blend": m})`, which `BlendMode::parse` also accepts.

## Verification

Three tests in `blend_mode_tests` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs`), **proven to catch the bug**: reverted only the fix and re-ran — `lowercase_documented_blend_modes_apply` …

title: Text: text after a paragraph that spans columns flows below it
author: aiongg
body:
In a multi-column frame, text after a Span Columns paragraph started again at the top of the next column, on top of the text above and the span itself. A span reached in a later column wasn't widened at all.

- The columns between spanning paragraphs form a band. Text after a span starts below it in every column, after the span's space after.
- The text above a span is balanced across the columns before the span is placed: the band gets the lowest column height at which its text fits.
- A span that doesn't fit, or that a keep or start option moves, goes to the next frame.
- A span over fewer columns than the frame has covers the first columns in reading order (the rightmost in right-to-left frames).
- In a frame with a span, Center and Bottom vertical justification move the frame's text as a whole, and Justify is skipped.

Validation: `text_after_a_spanning_paragraph_flows_below_it`, `spanning_paragraph_at_the_top_and_end_of_a_frame`, `text_after_a_spanning_paragraph_threads_into_the_next_frame` and `spanning_paragraph_in_rtl_and_vertical_frames` fail before the change; `spanning_heading_kept_with_next_and_spanning_two_of_three_columns` covers keeps and partial spans. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Menus: menus taller than the window scroll
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #267.

At a large UI scale, the menu bar's menus ran past the bottom of the window, and the items at the end (Edit › Preferences…, which holds the UI scale) couldn't be reached.

- A menu taller than the window fits between its button and the window edge and scrolls with the mouse wheel or its scroll bar. It opens at the top each time.
- The height limit depends only on the button and the window: a menu bar menu uses the larger space below or above its button, a submenu the larger space from its item down or up. The popup's placement can't flip between frames.
- One helper, `menus::menu_button`, wraps `ui.menu_button` for the menu bar, submenus, the workspace and zoom menus in the bars, and the panels' menus. Short menus look as before.

Validation: `menu_taller_than_the_window_scrolls` (a 60-item menu in a 400×300 window opens below its button, fits in the window, and a wheel event brings the last item into view) fails before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Set a text selection as warichu inside the parent line
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary
- Type › Warichu (`type.warichu`) stacks the selection as smaller lines inside the parent line, then closes up the rest of that line. The edit undoes, and IDML reads and writes the warichu attributes.
- The caret, hit testing, the selection, and Up/Down follow each small line. The first and last small lines keep their break minimums, the rows split by width, and line spacing can tighten. Underlines sit on the small baseline.
- Right-to-left and tate-chu-yoko runs stay body text. The parent line break still measures full-size widths, so this does not pull more characters onto the line.

## Validation
- `rtk cargo test --offline --lib warichu` for `designcraft-compose`, `designcraft-engine`, `designcraft-render`, and `designcraft-pdf` — 9 passed (render and pdf compiled with no matching tests)
- `rtk cargo test --offline -p designcraft-compose --lib caret_and_hit` — 1 passed
- `rtk cargo test --offline -p designcraft-engine --lib arrow_keys` — 3 passed
- `rtk cargo check --offline -p designcraft-ui-egui` finished
- The desktop app was not launched.

title: Keep menus and dialogs usable at larger UI scales
author: skylartaylor
body:
Addresses #267.

Long menus and nested submenus now scroll within the space available around their button, including workspace, zoom, and panel menus. Reopening a menu resets it to the top. Scrollbar clicks keep the menu open, choosing a command closes it, and clipped submenu rows no longer react to hover outside the visible menu.

Dialogs keep their title and OK/Cancel buttons visible while oversized contents scroll. Preferences scrolls its sections and options independently, so selecting a lower section keeps its settings reachable.

A separate small commit fixes an existing Rust 1.95 Clippy blocker in xtask by moving a condition into a match guard, preserving the dependency-checking behavior.

### Validation

- Full `cargo xtask ci` passed all six stages: formatting, strict workspace Clippy, tests, asset audit, dependency layering, and WASM checks
- 790 tests passed, 3 ignored
- Native UI checked at 100% and 200%, including the 900×560 minimum window
- Regression tests cover scrolling, command activation, clipped submenu hover, top/middle/bottom popup anchors, reopen scroll reset, very short viewports, RTL layout and field editing, and dialog resize/cancel/reopen behavior

Arabic checks cover layout and interaction. The optional craft-fonts pack was not included, so full Arabic glyph rendering remains unverified.

Builds on @aiongg's shared menu wrapper, broader menu coverage, and anchor-aware sizing from #279. Thanks for that work! The combined version retains the scrollbar-click and clipped-submenu protections.

title: Text: a line with a tab wraps at the column edge
author: aiongg
body:
A line that held a tab could run past the right edge of its column by the tab's width. The line breaker counted a tab as zero wide, and the tab only got its width when the line was laid out. A footnote whose number is followed by a tab showed it on every first line: with the default tab stops, the first line ran about 30 pt past the column.

- The line breaker measures each tab up to its stop, from where the line starts (indents and text wrap included), as line layout does. Both use one function, `tab_advance`.
- For right, centre and character tabs, the breaker measures the text after the tab up to the next tab or break. When that text doesn't fit on the line, the tab counts as zero wide, as before.
- A hanging indent acts as a tab stop at the left indent: the tab after a bullet or number goes there, unless an explicit stop comes first. It went to the next default stop, so the first line of a list item started too far right.
- Paragraphs without tabs are unchanged.

Validation: `footnote_first_line_wraps_at_the_column_edge_after_its_number` (footnotes separated by a tab, the default tab stops, a space and em spaces, plus a body paragraph with a tab) and `list_first_line_wraps_at_the_column_edge_after_its_label` (bullets and numbers with a hanging indent, with and without explicit stops) fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Text: the line before a column, frame or page break is a last line
author: aiongg
body:
In a justified paragraph, the line before a column, frame or page break character was justified to the full measure, like a line ended by a forced line break. It is the end of the paragraph's text in that column, so it takes the last-line alignment: Left Justify sets it flush left, Justify All still justifies it.

- A line ended by a column, frame or page break uses the paragraph's last-line alignment. A line ended by a forced line break (Shift+Return) stays justified.
- The break character is read from the line's last glyph. The column and frame jump read the glyph before the next line's start instead, which is a space when one follows the break, so `text<column break> more` didn't move to the next column. It does now.

Validation: `line_before_a_break_character_is_a_last_line` (column, frame and page breaks with Left Justify, a page break with Justify All, a forced line break, and a column break followed by a space) fails before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Text: a justified line with a tab justifies the text after its last tab
author: aiongg
body:
In a justified paragraph, a line that held a tab wasn't justified at all, so it ended short of the measure. A footnote whose number is followed by a tab had a ragged first line while its other lines were justified.

- Only the text after the line's last tab stretches or shrinks (word spaces, letter spacing, glyph scaling, kashidas). The text up to the tab keeps its positions, so tab stops stay aligned.
- After a right, centre, character or right-indent tab, the line stays unjustified as before.
- Single Word Justification applies to a lone word after the tab: Full letter-spaces it; Center and Right widen the tab.
- Last lines and lines ended by a forced line break follow the same rules as lines without tabs.

Validation: `justified_line_with_a_tab_justifies_the_text_after_its_last_tab` (a left tab, a right tab, and a footnote with a tab separator in a justified note style) fails before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Text: a column, frame or page break ends its paragraph; odd and even page breaks
author: aiongg
body:
A column, frame or page break character ends its paragraph, so the text after it starts a new paragraph with its own style. On import, the break was kept inside the paragraph, so the paragraph after it merged into the one before and took its style: a chapter number after a page break was set in the body style. Odd-page and even-page breaks were imported as plain page breaks. - A break character is its paragraph's last character, followed by the paragraph end. IDML, .docx and .rtf import, and Type › Insert Break Character, store it that way. IDML export writes it as one `
` with its `ParagraphBreakType`. - New Odd Page Break and Even Page Break characters (Insert Break Character, GREP `~L` and `~E`, IDML `NextOddPage`/`NextEvenPage`). Layout moves the next paragraph to the next page with that page number parity; with no such frame, the rest is overset. - A page break and the Next Page start option go to a frame on a later page; a threaded frame on the same page is skipped. - No empty line after a break at a paragraph's end. Deleting a break deletes its paragraph end with it. A break inside a paragraph (older documents) still moves the rest of the paragraph on. Validation: `break_characters_end_their_paragraph_and_keep_page_parity` (compose), `odd_page_break_ends_its_paragraph_and_keeps_its_parity` (IDML import, export round trip, parity with renumbered pages), `page_break_ends_its_paragraph` (.docx) and `inserted_break_ends_its_paragraph` (insert, type after, delete) fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix(web): native document download Blob says application/vnd.designcraft+zip
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Fixes #94

## What

Saving a native document in the browser created the download `Blob` with MIME type `application/json`, but the `.designcraft` file is a ZIP container whose stored first entry says `application/vnd.designcraft+zip` (and whose bytes start `PK\x03\x04`).

`mime_for` now returns `designcraft_format::MIME` — the very constant the native writer stores in the archive's `mimetype` entry — for the `designcraft` extension, so the Blob type and the written bytes cannot drift apart. All other mappings are unchanged (`png`, `jpg/jpeg`, `pdf`, `idml`, and the `application/octet-stream` fallback).

## Test

`mime_for` moved from the wasm-gated `web.rs` into a new `src/mime.rs` (compiled for `wasm32` and for host unit tests) so it is reachable by `cargo test`. Two tests:

- `native_document_blob_matches_format_mime` — `.designcraft` (and `DOC.DESIGNCRAFT`) must equal `designcraft_format::MIME`, and must not be `application/json`;
- `other_extensions_unchanged` — pins the remaining mappings and the fallback.

Proven to catch the bug: run before the one-line fix → `assertion left == right failed, left: "application/json", right: "application/vnd.designcraft+zip"`. After the fix, both tests pass.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p designcraft-web` — **2 passed, 0 failed**
- `cargo fmt -p designcraft-web -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-web --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo xtask wasm` — green (the wasm build compiles the changed download path)

title: Fonts: the Document Fonts folder is found whatever its case
author: aiongg
body:
Packages name the fonts folder `Document fonts`. On a case-sensitive file system, opening a document from such a package loaded none of its fonts, so its text was set in substitutes.

title: IDML: resolve table styles and correct cell height fitting
author: skylartaylor
body:
## Summary

Fixes #162.

IDML tables were losing formatting supplied by table regions and inherited cell styles. This resolves that cascade, preserves explicit cleared edges, and draws a shared cell edge once instead of letting neighboring cells paint conflicting rules.

Restoring the missing padding also exposed a cell-height bug: the old calculation added descent and bottom inset together, making rows too tall. The cell-specific sizing correction is included here so applying the right styles doesn't introduce overflow.

## Changes

- Resolve `BasedOn` and body, left/right, header/footer, cell-style, and local overrides, including sparse insets and per-edge strokes.
- Preserve border priorities and explicit `None`/zero-width edges through import/export. Resolve shared edges across merged cells, RTL tables, and repeated headers/footers.
- Keep native table edits and style reapplication consistent with the imported formatting.
- Size cells using baseline and physical text/in-flow object bounds. Use the same measurement for row growth, fixed-height overflow, vertical alignment, and row spans; ordinary text-frame sizing is unchanged.

The commits separate the style/edge work from the cell-height correction. A small Clippy prerequisite in `xtask/src/layers.rs` is the same change already included in #281.

## Testing

- `cargo xtask ci`: all six gates passed, including WASM; **836 tests passed, 3 ignored**.
- Synthetic regression tests cover inheritance, sparse overrides, round trips, shared-edge conflicts, native edits, malformed values, and cell-height/fitting cases.
- Compared all **280 pages** of the Cairn Player's and Warden's Guides before and after the cell-height correction: no newly overset stories or reduced outer-story line counts; **48 existing overset stories cleared**. Visually checked representative changed pages and page-boundary reflows against the matching reference PDFs.
- Checked Redokun's table-styles example in the native app and exported PDF. With …

title: feat(mcp): confine automation file paths with --automation-read-root/--automation-write-root
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Fixes #242

## What

`designcraft-cli mcp` now accepts PhotoCraft's confinement flags so one client config works across the suite:

```sh
designcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project
```

- **With at least one root** the server is confined: reads only from the read root, writes only to the write root. An omitted root is an authority you don't grant (that side is refused — same fail-closed semantics as PhotoCraft's `AuthorizedWorkspace`).
- **Without either flag** nothing changes: the server is unrestricted, as documented today.

## How

New `PathGuard` in the `designcraft-mcp` crate (`crates/mcp/src/guard.rs`), enforced at the MCP layer before anything reaches a backend (headless or connected):

- Request paths are **relative to the matching root** and are rewritten to the resolved location under it, so the engine only ever sees paths inside the root. An absolute path is accepted only if already under the root.
- Untrusted input rules match PhotoCraft's: no `..`, no `\` separators, no drive/device prefixes, no empty/`.` components, no trailing dot/space, no Windows device names.
- Symlink escapes are resolved and refused (`..` through a link cannot leave the root) with a bounded ancestor walk.
- Every path-carrying command is classified read/write in a table covering `file.*`, `book.*`, `data.*`, `place.*`, `snippet.*`, `swatch.*`, `library.*`, `links.relink`, `table.placeGraphic`, `color.loadProfile`, `media.options` and `xml.loadDtd`; tool-level paths (`open_document`, `save_document`, `place_image`, `render_page`, `export_png`, `screenshot`) are guarded directly, and `execute`/`batch` steps are guarded per step.
- While roots are set, `script.run` (nested commands that would bypass the per-step check) is refused, as is an unmapped `file.*` command carrying a path — fail closed, not silently passed through. `file.save` without a path (which would write to the document's ambient location) must be given one explicitl…

title: Open Affinity documents (.afpub, .af, .afdesign, .afphoto); work inside groups
author: dwetscher
body:
> This contribution was written with an AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code) and tested by a human on their own Affinity Publisher documents.

## What

DesignCraft opens native Affinity documents: `.afpub`, `.afdesign` and `.afphoto` from Affinity 1 and 2, and `.af` from Affinity 3. It's **read-only**: an opened document starts unsaved, and nothing is ever written in Affinity's format. It works through File › Open, drag and drop, the web build, `designcraft-cli --in x.afpub` and the new command `file.openAffinity {path | base64, name?}`. `file.open` and `file.openBytes` hand these files on to it.

The new crate `crates/affinity` has two parts:

- **Reader**: a copy of `vectorcraft-affinity` from storytold/vectorcraft @ `35a6015` (PhotoCraft has its own copy, `photocraft-affinity`). It's bounded: limits on archive size, stream values and nesting depth, plus fuzz targets.
- **Mapping** (`src/import.rs`, new): turns the reader's model into a DesignCraft document.

What comes over (full table in `crates/affinity/README.md`):
- Publisher spreads and pages; master pages become one-page parents.
- Layers, groups and nested layers.
- Shapes with clipping (children pasted into frames).
- Colours: RGB, CMYK (kept as CMYK) and grey; gradients.
- Strokes with dashes.
- Text:
  - artistic and frame text, with fonts and character attributes;
  - paragraph alignment, indents, spacing, and fixed or automatic leading.
- Tables, as real DesignCraft tables, with merged cells, per-edge lines and cell insets.
- Images:
  - embedded images and pixel layers, including their pixel masks;
  - embedded Affinity documents (logos, QR codes), as editable content.
- Effects:
  - drop shadows, inner shadows, outer glows, outlines, and bevel & emboss (approximated);
  - colour and gradient overlays, in any of Affinity's blend modes. DesignCraft has no such effect, so they're baked into the fill, stroke and text colours and into the pixels.
- Pixel layers over 64 MP are read at a reduced resol…

title: Text: a word longer than the line breaks at the column edge; a line that exactly fills the measure fits
author: aiongg
body:
A word wider than the column ran past the frame, or in a justified paragraph was squeezed onto one line with overlapping glyphs (a 690-character line tracked 740 overlapped on one line). A line whose natural width equalled the measure, within rounding, was hyphenated or broken.

- A run of letters wider than the narrowest measure gets emergency break points between its glyphs. A legal hyphenation point still wins where one fits; no-break, kinsoku, soft hyphens and forced breaks are respected. In justified text the fullest piece wins, so the word breaks at the last glyph that fits.
- Justification never shrinks word spaces, letter spacing or glyph scaling past the paragraph's minimums. An overfull single word stays within the letter and glyph limits instead of getting negative letter gaps.
- A line that overruns the measure by less than 0.01 pt fits, in both composers.

Validation: `a_word_longer_than_the_line_breaks_at_the_column_edge` (paragraph and single-line composers, left and justified, tracking 0 and 740: every line fits, no glyph overlaps the previous one) and `a_line_that_exactly_fills_the_measure_fits` fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Text: Split Columns sets a paragraph in sub-columns within its column
author: aiongg
body:
A paragraph with Span Columns set to Split Columns was set at the full column width. It is now divided into sub-columns within its column.

- Consecutive paragraphs with the same split settings form one block. The block is inset by the outside gutter and divided into the split count (2–64) with the inside gutter between sub-columns. Text fills each sub-column from the block's top; a column break moves to the next sub-column; a block that runs out continues at the top of the next frame column.
- With text after it, the block's last part in a column is balanced, and the next paragraph continues at the full width below the deepest sub-column (the same balancing as Span Columns). At the end of a story the block fills its sub-columns in turn.
- Paragraph shading and borders get one box per sub-column; vertical justification moves a frame with split lines as a whole.
- New paragraph attributes Inside Gutter (default 6 pt) and Outside Gutter (default 0), read from and written to IDML (`SplitColumnInsideGutter`, `SplitColumnOutsideGutter`).

Not included: Space Between Paragraphs Using Same Style and the minimum space before and after a span or split block.

Validation: `split_paragraphs_are_set_in_balanced_sub_columns`, `split_block_in_the_second_column_and_at_the_story_end`, `split_block_flows_into_the_next_column` and `split_columns_import_and_round_trip` fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Desktop: pick the graphics backend before the window exists; DirectX 12 on Windows
author: JeremyYao
body:
## Summary

The desktop app crashed a few seconds after launch on an AMD hybrid-graphics laptop (ASUS G513QY: Radeon RX 6800M beside an integrated Radeon). The Windows event log showed an access violation inside `amdvlk64.dll`, AMD's Vulkan driver, and wgpu trace logging put it at the first swapchain present. Two versions of that driver were loaded into the one process (a 2026 driver for the discrete GPU, a 2021 inbox driver for the integrated one), with the Radeon Software and OBS overlay hooks alongside. Nothing reached the DesignCraft log: a fault inside a driver is a native crash the engine's panic guard never sees.

wgpu's default backend set enumerates Vulkan first, so every start took that path. `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` and `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` ran fine, and the headless CPU renderer was never affected.

## The fix

- **The backend is chosen before the window exists** (`apps/designcraft/src/gpu.rs`): DirectX 12 first on Windows (what browsers' WebGPU uses), then Vulkan, then OpenGL; Vulkan then OpenGL on Linux; Metal on macOS. OpenGL stays in the set as the in-process fallback when the chosen backend has no adapter.
- **Start-up fallback.** `gpu.json` in the settings directory records the backend being tried until the third frame begins or the app exits normally. A record left behind means that backend never showed a frame, so the next start skips it, tries the next candidate and says so in the status bar. The list starts over once every candidate has failed or the app version changes.
- **`WGPU_BACKEND` still overrides everything** and turns the fallback off; `DESIGNCRAFT_NO_PREFS` records nothing.
- The adapter, backend and driver version are logged at start-up for bug reports.
- README (environment table and a "Graphics backend" section) and ROADMAP updated.

## Verification

On the affected machine, with the release build:

- A default start runs on DirectX 12 and renders the sample magazine correctly (checked over the control channel with a screenshot).
- Writin…

title: Lists: numbering formats and expressions from IDML; an empty paragraph gets no bullet or number
author: aiongg
body:
A numbered list from IDML was always labelled "1.", "2.": its Number format (A, B, C; i, ii, iii; 01, 02 …) and its Number expression ("Tabel ^#^t") were ignored, on import and export. An empty paragraph in a list got a bullet or number and used up a number.

- Paragraphs have a number expression (default `^#.^t`); `^#` is the number and InDesign's special-character codes (`^t`, `^>`, `^m` …) expand. Level placeholders `^1`–`^9` are dropped (number levels aren't modelled yet).
- IDML `NumberingFormat`, `NumberingExpression`, `BulletsTextAfter` and Unicode `BulletChar` are imported and exported. New number styles 001 and 0001; formats with no counterpart (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) set decimal numbers. Footnote `DoubleLeadingZeros` and `TripleLeadingZeros` map to 001 and 0001.
- An empty list paragraph gets no label and isn't counted, in story lists, named lists across stories and cross-reference paragraph numbers.
- Counters saturate instead of overflowing after a start number of 4294967295, and Roman, letter and symbol formats fall back to digits above 3999.

Validation: `numbered_lists_follow_their_format_and_expression`, `numbering_from_the_largest_start_number_does_not_overflow`, `empty_paragraphs_get_no_bullet_or_number` (compose) and `list_numbering_format_expression_and_bullet_import_and_round_trip` (IDML) fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: IDML: text variables keep their text
author: aiongg
body:
IDML import dropped every text variable instance, so a running header "output <Output Date>" read "output". The document always got the default variable set, and export wrote the instance as a raw private-use character.

- Import reads the file's `<TextVariable>` definitions: Custom Text, Last Page Number (with its section scope), Chapter Number, File Name, Creation, Modification and Output Date (with `Format`), and Running Header by paragraph or character style. `TextBefore`/`TextAfter` are kept. A type DesignCraft doesn't compute (live captions, File Name with path) shows its imported result and is written back unchanged.
- `TextVariableInstance` becomes the variable's character in the story; an instance whose variable isn't defined imports as its result text.
- Creation and modification dates come from the package's XMP metadata, so date variables show the document's dates.
- Export writes the definitions, each instance with its current result, and the XMP dates, so variables round-trip.

Output Date shows the date of output, as it does in the original application, so it differs from a date baked into a reference PDF.

Validation: `text_variables_show_their_values_and_round_trip` (definitions, instances, the undefined-variable fallback, the composed text, and an export → import round trip) fails before the change; `predefined_variables_round_trip` covers the default set. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Warichu: hostile line spacing and break minimums can't break layout
author: aiongg
body:
Two values in a document's warichu settings reached layout unchecked:

- **Line spacing** was added to the row gap as is, so `warichuLineSpacing: 1e308` (from IDML or `type.char`) put an infinite coordinate into the layout and `inf` into the PDF content stream, which makes the PDF invalid. It is clamped to ±16 em of the parent size, and a non-finite value counts as 0.
- **Break minimums**: `before + after + n - 2` overflowed on 32-bit targets (wasm) for large `WarichuCharsBeforeBreak`/`AfterBreak` values, a panic in debug builds and a wrong line count in release. The sum saturates.

Validation: `warichu_line_spacing_from_a_document_stays_finite` (1e308, −1e308, ∞, NaN) and `huge_break_minimums_keep_one_line` fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Distinguish unknown MCP commands from registered UI commands
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Headless execute and batch now distinguish unknown command IDs and case typos from registered UI commands. A shared command catalog preserves desktop guidance for UI commands and keeps engine-command precedence intact. Failed batches stop before later edits.

Closes #63.

Validation on Linux: `cargo xtask ci` passed all six steps, and `cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p designcraft-web` passed. Regression tests cover direct command classification and stopping batches before later document changes.

title: IDML: text in a paragraph-level cross-reference source keeps its formatting
author: aiongg
body:
A `CrossReferenceSource` can sit inside a `CharacterStyleRange` or at paragraph level around one. In the paragraph-level form (the one the schema allows, and the one our own export writes), the inner range's local attributes were dropped: its text took only the paragraph range's attributes. A tracked cross-reference was set narrower, so its paragraph broke one line earlier.

- A range inside a paragraph-level source is formatted like any other range: its style plus its local attributes over the paragraph's.
- Markers directly at paragraph level (text anchors, a source without an inner range, page references) take the paragraph's character attributes instead of a bare default.
- Both nestings import to the same story, and our own IDML round trip keeps local formatting on cross-reference text.

title: fix(geom): prevent invalid zoom values from breaking ruler ticks
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Invalid or extreme viewport zoom values can cause ruler tick calculations to produce non-finite spacing or enter an unbounded loop.

A negative zoom can prevent the ruler-spacing calculation from reaching its termination condition.

## Root Cause

`Unit::ruler_ticks()` calculates major tick spacing without validating the incoming zoom value.

The spacing adjustment loop assumes the zoom is positive, finite, and within a reasonable range.

## Changes

- Normalize zero, negative, and non-finite zoom values to a safe default.
- Clamp extreme positive zoom values to prevent arithmetic overflow.
- Preserve existing ruler behavior at normal zoom levels.
- Add regression tests covering NaN, infinity, negative values, zero, and extreme magnitudes.

## Validation

- Reviewed the affected geometry code and resulting diff.
- Added targeted regression tests.
- Rust tests and `cargo xtask ci` have not been executed in the current environment.
- GUI ruler verification and upstream CI remain pending.

## Scope

This change is limited to ruler tick calculations in `designcraft-geom`.

No unrelated rendering behavior, dependencies, or repository infrastructure was modified.

title: fix(layout): reject invalid spread rotation angles
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

The `layout.rotateSpreadView` command silently accepts unsupported rotation angles.

For example, an angle of 45 degrees is converted using integer division and can produce an unintended rotation.

Malformed angle values may also silently fall back to the default 90-degree rotation.

This is especially problematic when the command is invoked through automation or external tools.

## Root Cause

The command uses integer division to convert degrees into quarter turns without first validating the requested angle.

It also defaults to 90 degrees when an explicitly supplied value cannot be parsed as an integer.

## Changes

- Validate supplied rotation angles before modifying the document view.
- Reject values that are not integer multiples of 90 degrees.
- Return an explicit error for malformed angle values.
- Preserve valid clockwise and counterclockwise quarter turns.
- Preserve the zero-angle reset behavior.
- Add command-level regression tests verifying that invalid input leaves the view unchanged.

## Validation

- Reviewed the command implementation and resulting diff.
- Added regression coverage for valid and invalid rotations.
- Rust unit tests and `cargo xtask ci` have not been executed.
- UI verification and upstream CI remain pending.

## Scope

Changes are limited to spread-view rotation argument handling and its regression tests.

Document geometry and exported content are unaffected by the intended change.

title: fix(geom): correct pica and cicero rounding at unit boundaries
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Measurements close to a major unit boundary can be displayed incorrectly when formatted as picas or ciceros.

For example, a value of 11.9999 points formatted to three decimal places can produce:

`0p12`

The expected display is:

`1p0`

The same problem affects cicero measurements near their unit boundaries.

## Root Cause

`format_measure_prec()` checks whether the fractional component should carry into the next major unit before rounding it to the requested display precision.

Because the carry check uses a fixed tolerance, values that round to exactly 12 minor units can bypass the carry condition.

## Changes

- Round the fractional component to the requested display precision before evaluating the carry.
- Correctly carry rounded values into the next pica or cicero.
- Preserve ordinary measurement formatting.
- Add regression tests covering:
  - Positive pica values.
  - Negative pica values.
  - Different decimal precisions.
  - Cicero unit boundaries.
  - Parsing of the formatted measurement.

## Validation

- Reviewed the measurement formatter and resulting diff.
- Added focused regression tests.
- Rust tests and `cargo xtask ci` have not been executed.
- UI measurement-field verification and upstream CI remain pending.

## Scope

This change is isolated to measurement formatting in `designcraft-geom`.

No document geometry, serialization format, dependencies, or build infrastructure was modified.

title: Snap: smart guides beat the baseline grid; a box centres between two others
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #188

## What was wrong

Two things kept smart guides from working on the vertical axis:

1. **The baseline grid won almost every vertical move.** `first_on_axis` tried the baseline grid before the smart-guide passes. It snaps while hidden, and with lines every 12 pt and a box's top, centre and bottom each reaching 4 pt either side, one of them is nearly always in the zone. So it took the move and drew nothing, and object alignment and equal spacing hardly ever showed on y. The x axis has no such pass, which is why horizontal worked.
2. **No centring between two objects.** Smart spacing only matched the mover's gap to a gap between two *other* boxes, so a box dragged between two neighbours never found the point where both of its gaps are equal (either axis).

## Change (`crates/tools/src/snap.rs`)

- The baseline pass now runs after the smart-guide passes (grid → guides/margins/columns → alignment → spacing → dimensions → baseline). Hidden baselines still snap when nothing else applies, so `hidden_baseline_still_snaps_and_zero_increment_does_not` is unchanged. Ruler guides and margins now also come before the baseline grid; that follows from guides already beating object alignment.
- With a neighbour on each side, smart spacing also offers the shift that makes both gaps equal; it competes with the stationary-gap matches in the same zone, and both gaps are marked. The pass no longer bails out when there are no stationary gaps.
- `ROADMAP.md`: the snap-order sentence is updated.

## Tests

Six new tests in `snap::tests`:
- centring between two boxes, side by side and stacked; no centring outside the zone; none with Smart Spacing off
- `vertical_centering_beats_a_closer_baseline` and `vertical_alignment_beats_a_closer_baseline` (factory snap settings, 12 pt baseline grid)

The centring tests fail without the spacing change, and the two baseline tests fail with the old pass order.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, l…

title: Justification: tight word spacing doesn't isolate a word; fixed-width spaces don't stretch
author: aiongg
body:
**A single word letter-spaced across the line.** With a tight word-spacing range (for example 100/103/105 %), each word space can stretch only a little. A line that needed more than every tier allows was rated by its leftover in units of its own word-space stretch, so a line of several words got a huge ratio, while a single word (no word spaces) was rated against its letter and glyph stretch and came out cheaper. The composer then set one word per line, letter-spaced to the full measure, although the next words fit.

- Stretch past the maximum is rated in units of the line's word spaces, each at least 33 % of its width. With the default range (100/133 %) this is the same unit as before, so default paragraphs compose as before. Lines without word spaces are rated as before.

**Fixed-width spaces stretched.** On a justified line, stretch left over past every limit was shared by all spaces, so an en space, em space or thin space widened.

- Only word spaces take the leftover; a line without word spaces gives it to its letter gaps, matching how the composer rates such a line.

Validation: `tight_word_spacing_does_not_isolate_a_word` (100/103/105 % word spacing, widths 200–320: no single-word lines) and `fixed_width_spaces_do_not_stretch_on_justified_lines` fail before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Text: combining marks that start a run are shaped with their base letter
author: aiongg
body:
Each run is shaped on its own, so a combining mark at the start of a run was cut off from its base letter. In Hebrew from IDML this is common: the shin ends one run and its SIN DOT starts the next, which differs only in ligature or contextual-alternate settings. The mark was positioned on its own (marks stacked on one spot), and when the font was missing it took the run's substitute face and showed a missing-glyph box while the base letter came from a fallback face.

- Before shaping, combining marks at the start of a run join the previous run when that run ends right at them with a base character and the two runs differ only in ligatures, kerning or OpenType features. The shaper then attaches each mark to its base in the base's face.
- A mark in a run with another font, size, colour or condition stays in its run, so a font that lacks the mark still shows the box. No font fallback is added.

Validation: `a_mark_starting_a_run_is_shaped_with_its_base` (a mark run after a base in a missing font joins the base's face and cluster; a mark run in a present font that lacks the mark still shows the box) fails before the change. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: DTD: bound parameter-entity expansion, nesting and sequence matching
author: haranishi
body:
A DTD comes from the user (`xml.loadDtd`) or from a document: `xml.validate` parses the DTD stored in it and matches its content models against the document's tagged content. Three places in `crates/engine/src/dtd.rs` let a small input exhaust memory or the stack, which aborts the process, or freeze the editor.

## What changes

- **Parameter entities** (`parse`). They were expanded by up to 8 rounds of `text.replace` for every entity over the whole text. The size grew exponentially (an entity made of several references to the previous one: a few hundred bytes of DTD gave gigabytes, and every round cloned the text) and the work was entities × text length per round. `expand_parameter_entities` scans the text once per round with a map of the entities (the first declaration of a name wins, as before) and looks for the closing `;` only up to the next `%` or whitespace (a name has neither, and can be any length), so a round is linear. The result may not pass max(16 MiB, input length), checked before every append. References nest at most 64 levels (the old loop resolved one level per round in declaration order, so the depth it reached depended on that order); a cycle, an entity whose value is its own reference, or a chain deeper than that is an error, where the old code left `%x;` in the text to become an element name.
- **Content-model groups** (`particle`). Parsing recursed once per `(` with no limit, and `ends` and `show` recurse on the result, so about 10^5 parentheses overflowed the stack. Groups may nest 64 deep.
- **Sequences and repetitions** (`ends`). The positions after each item of a sequence, and after each round of a repetition, were kept as a list of every path, so `(a?, a?, …)` over as many `a` children doubled per item (40 optional items: 2^40 entries), and the same happened per round of a repetition. The positions are now sorted and deduplicated at both places (the result was already a set), and `ends` is memoized per group and start position while one el…

title: Links: Update Links Changed on Disk (Preferences › File Handling)
author: KattKnight
body:
## What this does

A placed file that another app saves now updates the layout by itself. The other app could be VectorCraft, PhotoCraft, Illustrator or Photoshop. You no longer need Window › Links › Update Link.

It's part of making the Craft apps work together like Adobe's: edit the artwork in VectorCraft, save, and the DesignCraft layout shows it.

### How it works

- **Setting:** Preferences › File Handling › Links › **Update Links Changed on Disk**, on by default.
- **Checking:**
  - The desktop app stamps the active document's linked files (size and modification time).
  - It does this every two seconds, and as soon as its window comes back to the front.
  - The stamps are taken on a worker thread, so a file on a slow network share can't stall the interface.
- **Updating:**
  - A file whose stamp moved is updated with the existing `links.update`.
  - That only touches a link whose bytes really differ.
  - It's an **Update Link undo step**, like a click on Update Link.
  - Undoing it leaves the link modified until the file changes again. The undo is respected, and the update isn't reapplied.
- **Stamps are kept per document.** A document in the background catches up when it comes to the front.
- **A file seen for the first time is only remembered.** A document opened with already-modified links leaves them to the Links panel, as today.
- **A file still being written** keeps its old stamp, so the next look tries again.
- **New command:** `links.updateChanged` runs one look (CLI, MCP, control channel).
- **Web:** the web build is unaffected. It has no files to look at and starts no thread.

The setting's label is translated in the shared table (zh) and in the ar, it, ja, pt-BR and uk catalogs. ROADMAP and docs/parity.md are updated.

## Tests

- **New tests:** `link_watch::tests` has 4 tests, working on real files:
  - A changed file updates as an undo step, and an undone update stays undone.
  - A half-written file is retried.
  - A document in the back catches …

title: Ruler: draggable zero point with double-click reset
author: zydvc26s67-web
body:
## Summary

The '+' crosshair in the ruler corner (top-left, where the horizontal and vertical rulers meet) was purely decorative. This implements a working ruler-origin feature matching InDesign's ruler behavior:

- **Click-and-drag** the ruler corner crosshair to reposition the ruler's zero point anywhere on the canvas, live-updating the ruler ticks as you drag.
- **Double-click** the crosshair to reset the zero point back to the default (the current spread's first page top-left corner).
- The crosshair is highlighted with the accent color whenever a custom zero point is active, so it's visually distinguishable from the default state.

## Implementation

- `View` (per-document/pane view state in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) gains `pub ruler_origin: Option<Point>`, defaulting to `None` (the default origin). This is view state, not persisted document content.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:
  - `draw_rulers()` uses `view().ruler_origin` when set, falling back to the existing default otherwise.
  - `fit()` preserves `ruler_origin` across fit-to-window.

title: Layout: section start numbers are bounded and page numbering can't overflow
author: aiongg
body:
`layout.section` stored `startNumber` with an unchecked `as u32` cast, and `page_number` added to it with plain `+`. A section starting at 4294967295 with two or more pages panicked in debug builds and showed page "0" in release; values from 2^32 up were truncated. `layout.documentSetup`'s `startPage` had the same cast.

- `layout.section` (`startNumber`) and `layout.documentSetup` (`startPage`) refuse anything but a whole number from 1 to 99 999 (`designcraft_doc::MAX_PAGE_NUMBER`); `null` still means "continue". A refused value leaves the document unchanged.
- `Document::page_number` walks back through continuing sections in a loop with saturating arithmetic, so values loaded from a file can't overflow and many sections can't build a deep call stack. Book pagination's running page count saturates too.

Validation: `hostile_section_start_numbers_saturate` (a document built with start `u32::MAX` on a two-page section; panicked before) and `section_start_numbers_are_bounded` (refusals for both commands; 99 999 accepted, pages named 99999 and 100000). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Type tool: fix double-click word selection and triple-click line selection
author: zydvc26s67-web
body:
## Symptom

In DesignCraft's Type tool, double-click (should select the word) and triple-click (should select the whole composed line) did nothing. The only way to select text was dragging.

## Root cause

egui 0.36.2's `pointer.button_double_clicked()` / `button_triple_clicked()` only become `true` on the **release** event of the 2nd/3rd click, never on press — but `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` was checking them inside the `if pressed { ... }` branch, so they could never fire.

## Fix

- Detect double/triple click at release time in `canvas.rs` and emit a `DoubleClick`/`TripleClick` pointer event before the `Up` event.
- Add a new `text.selectLine` engine command (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`), reusing the existing `line_of()` helper, for triple-click-to-select-line.
- `TypeTool` dispatches word selection on double-click and line selection on triple-click (`crates/tools/src/text.rs`).
- `SelectionTool`'s double-click-to-enter-text-edit now also triggers on triple-click (`crates/tools/src/select.rs`).
- Control-protocol (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs`, `docs/control-protocol.md`) and MCP (`crates/mcp/src/headless.rs`, `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs`) pointer events gain `tripleclick` support.
- New unit tests in `crates/tools/src/tests.rs` and `crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs` cover double-click word selection and triple-click line selection.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask ci`: fmt ✅, clippy ✅. Test suite passes except the pre-existing, unrelated flaky failure in `gpu::tests::a_start_records_its_backend_until_a_frame_is_presented` (confirmed via `git stash` to exist without this change too).
- Ran the affected crates directly with no failures: `designcraft-tools` (43 passed), `designcraft-engine` (281 passed), `designcraft-ui-egui` (144 passed), `designcraft-mcp` (17 passed).

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Route macOS text clipboard commands through egui
author: ironinthesoul
body:
## Summary

Fixes #201. Route native macOS Copy, Cut, and Paste commands through egui when editing canvas text, so the desktop integration can exchange text with the system clipboard.

## Issue and root cause

On macOS, ⌘C/⌘X/⌘V are handled by the native menu bar before they reach the application window. When text is selected in the canvas Type tool, the native menu handler ran the engine command directly. That bypassed egui's clipboard events, which the desktop integration uses to read pasteboard text and write copied text.

The canvas text editor is not an egui `TextEdit`, so egui does not automatically route those native menu actions to it.

## Change

For active canvas text editing, native Copy and Cut now emit egui copy/cut events, and native Paste requests clipboard text through egui. This uses the existing eframe/egui-winit clipboard integration rather than adding a second system clipboard implementation.

The change is limited to text editing. DesignCraft's object clipboard stores structured document fragments for in-app layout operations. Sending those fragments through text clipboard events would lose their structure; interoperable object copy/paste needs a separate representation and is outside this fix.

## Testing

Automated:
- Added `native_copy_and_paste_use_the_system_clipboard_for_canvas_text`, which verifies that native Copy produces egui's `CopyText` output and native Paste requests clipboard text and inserts the supplied text into the selection.
- `cargo test --locked -p designcraft-ui-egui --lib`: 145 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p designcraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.

Manual:
- Tested the locally built Apple Silicon app by copying text between DesignCraft and another macOS app in both directions; copy and paste behaved as expected when using both the menu items and keyboard shortcuts.

title: IDML: a font name with the $ID/ prefix imports as the plain family
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #338.

InDesign writes some `AppliedFont` values with its `$ID/` prefix (`$ID/Arial`). Import kept the prefix as part of the family name, so the font was reported missing and the text was set in the fallback font. Import now drops the prefix for text, styles and composite font entries, as it already does for `KerningMethod`, `AppliedLanguage` and a composite entry's `FontStyle`.

The prefix is file encoding, not part of the name, so it is dropped at import rather than next to #247's suffix lookup: the document, the font list and re-exported IDML carry the plain name.

The issue's table now reads ok / ok / ok / missing, and `$ID/Source Serif 4 (OTF)` resolves through the format-suffix lookup from #247.

Validation: `a_font_name_with_the_id_prefix_imports_as_the_plain_family` fails before the change. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.
