title: IDML: part names match leniently, and missing parts are reported
author: aiongg
body:
Import looked up each part listed in `designmap.xml` by its exact zip entry name and skipped a part it didn't find without a word. A package whose writer spelled a spread's name differently opened with that spread's frames missing and no message.

- Part lookup falls back to a normalised name: percent-decoded, `\` read as `/`, leading `./` and `/` removed, lower case. An exact match still comes first; among entries that normalise alike, the first in the zip wins.
- A part listed in `designmap.xml` but absent from the package is a warning that names it. `designcraft_idml::import_idml_report` returns the document with its warnings; `import_idml_with` is unchanged. `file.open` and `file.openIdml` return them in `warnings`, next to the font warnings.
- When every spread part is missing, the import error names the missing parts.
- Crash fix: `uri_to_path` sliced the text after a `%` by byte offsets, so a link URI such as `file:/a%bé` panicked (the slice ended inside `é`). Percent-decoding works on bytes and keeps a malformed escape as written.

Not included: `file.revert` and placing an IDML with `file.place` still drop the warnings.

Validation: `designmap_parts_match_leniently_and_missing_ones_are_reported` (encoded, upper-case and backslash spellings resolve and keep their frames; a missing spread is one warning; with every spread missing the error names the part) and `percent_decode_keeps_malformed_escapes`. `cargo xtask ci` passes (on the combined branch).

title: Text: the paragraph mark's size counts in its line's auto leading
author: aiongg
body:
The paragraph mark is a character of its paragraph's last line, but compose left it out of the line's leading. A 12 pt line ending in a 14 pt return was set 14.4 pt below the line above; in the reference PDF it is 16.8 pt (14 pt × 120 %).

- On a paragraph's last line, the mark's leading (auto: its size times the auto leading percentage; or its fixed leading) takes part in the largest-leading rule.
- It doesn't change the line's ascent or descent, and earlier lines of the paragraph are unaffected.
- A deleted mark (Track Changes) or one hidden by a condition takes no room.

Validation: `paragraph_mark_size_counts_in_its_line_auto_leading` (a 14 pt mark puts 16.8 pt above its line and leaves 14.4 pt below; a 12 pt mark changes nothing; fails before the change). `cargo xtask ci` passes (on the combined branch).

title: Rulers: a document zero point, a ruler origin, and guides from the ruler corner
author: aiongg
body:
Closes #337.

Clicking or dragging the ruler corner did nothing, and the rulers always measured from each spread's top-left corner.

**Zero point**
- It is document state: `zeroPoint`, an offset from the ruler origin of each spread, so every spread measures from the same relative place and split views share it; and `zeroPointLocked`. Documents saved without it read with the zero point at the origin.
- `view.zeroPoint {at?, reset?}` moves or resets it and `view.lockZeroPoint {on?}` locks it; both report the state. Moving it is not an undo step, and undo and redo leave it where it is. A locked zero point refuses moves and resets. Values from commands, files and IDML are kept on the pasteboard.
- Rulers and the X/Y fields (Control, Properties, Info, `transform.set`) measure from it.
- IDML reads and writes the document's `ZeroPoint`.
- Canvas: drag from the ruler corner to place it where you release, with crosshair lines while dragging; a click that stays in the corner does nothing; a double-click resets it; the corner's context menu has Lock/Unlock Zero Point.

**Ruler origin**
- Preferences › Units & Increments › Origin: Spread, Page or Spine (`document.preferences {rulerOrigin}`, IDML `ViewPreference` `RulerOrigin`). The zero point is an offset from it.
- With Page, the horizontal ruler restarts on each page and an object measures from the page it is on.

**Guides from the corner**
- Cmd-drag (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) from the ruler corner adds a horizontal and a vertical spread guide through the drop point, in one undo step. `guide.add` takes `orientation: "both"` with `point: [x, y]` for this.

New strings (Origin, Spine, Lock/Unlock Zero Point) in the shared table and in ar, it, ja, pt-br and uk (machine-translated).

Validation: engine tests `the_zero_point_moves_resets_and_locks_without_undo_steps`, `x_and_y_measure_from_the_zero_point_on_every_spread`, `x_measures_from_the_chosen_ruler_origin`, `old_documents_read_with_the_zero_point_at_the_corner`, `both_or…

title: IDML: `$ID/` font names, placed PDF page and crop, package IDML without embedded images
author: aiongg
body:
Closes #338. Closes #339. Closes #340.

Three interchange fixes for IDML files that other applications write or read.

**`$ID/` font names (#338).** `AppliedFont="$ID/Arial"` imported as a family named `$ID/Arial`, which no font matched, so the text fell back to another family.

- Import strips the prefix in paragraph and character styles, text ranges and composite font entries.
- The font database also looks a family up without the prefix (and without a format suffix such as ` (OTF)`), so documents already saved with a prefixed name draw in the named font.

**Placed PDFs (#339).** Export wrote no `PDFAttribute`, so the page and crop were lost, and import always showed page 1.

- The asset stores its Crop to choice (crop, art, trim, bleed, media, or the content bounds with visible or all layers) and where that box sits on the page. The graphic spans that box. The screen, PDF export, raster exports and clipping-path tracing draw only that part of the page, so a frame larger than the box doesn't show the bleed.
- Export writes `PDFAttribute` with `PageNumber` and `PDFCrop` (`CropTrim`, `CropMedia`, …), with `GraphicBounds` spanning the box. Import reads both back.
- After import, relink and update, the engine finds the box on the PDF page and maps it onto `GraphicBounds`; a graphic without bounds gets the box's size. A PDF placed with a trim or media crop elsewhere imports with that crop.
- Documents saved without a choice load with the crop box. The Place PDF dialog also offers the content bounds, and `links.list` reports the choice.
- A placed PDF page that the PDF doesn't have (a hostile `PageNumber`, or a document holding one) is left out of PDF export with a warning. Before, the whole export failed at the end.

**Package IDML (#340).** `file.package` copied the images to `Links/` and pointed the IDML at them, but also embedded a copy of each. The packaged IDML links the files in the package's `Links/` folder and embeds nothing. The links stay absolute `file:` URI…

title: CJK: ruby, kenten, shatai, auto tate-chu-yoko, grid references and the leading model
author: aiongg
body:

title: Text: input method (IME) composition in the Type tool
author: aiongg
body:
Builds on #84 (text editing and frames); review after it, or merge it first.

Closes #322.

The Type tool ignored input method events, so Japanese, Chinese and Korean input methods couldn't type into a story.

- The marked text shows in the story as a preview of `text.insert`: no undo step, nothing journaled. It is underlined, the clause being converted twice. The candidate window sits at the caret or the converting clause, also in vertical frames and at any zoom or view rotation.
- The commit is one `text.insert` and one undo step, in the format chosen at the caret. A committed newline confirms the marked text without a paragraph break. A cancelled composition leaves the document and selection as they were.
- While the IME composes, keys, shortcuts, the clipboard and Undo/Redo wait, and the menus disable them. A click, a tool or document switch, or any journaled command keeps the marked text as typed.

Per platform:
- **macOS:** when the tool keeps the marked text (after a click elsewhere, for example), the app tells the input context to discard it (`NSTextInputContext discardMarkedText`). winit clears only its own copy, so the IME would type the text again. The native menu holds ⌘Z and the clipboard back during a composition.
- **Windows, Linux (IBus, fcitx5):** egui-winit's IME events as they arrive. An empty preedit after a commit is ignored when nothing is marked, so it neither holds keys back nor deletes a selection.
- **Web:** eframe's hidden text input sends preedit and commit events while the canvas has a text caret. `DeleteSurrounding` (mobile Backspace and corrections) deletes around the caret.

Fixed along the way:
- **Split window typed twice:** both panes read the same keyboard events. Only the pane last clicked takes them.
- **Cancel and revision:** cancelling a drag, a preview or a composition restored the document but bumped its revision, so an unchanged document showed unsaved changes. Revisions come from one counter, and a cancel puts back the rev…

title: Paste: lands on the page in view instead of always the first spread (#348)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #348.

`edit.paste` (and `edit.pasteInPlace`, which calls it) always duplicated the clipboard onto `SpreadRef::Doc(0)`, so Paste and Paste in Place put the copy on page 1 whatever page was shown.

- Engine: `edit.paste` and `edit.pasteInPlace` take an optional `spread` (read with the shared `spread_param`, like the other commands that take a spread). Without it they still paste onto spread 0, so scripts keep their behaviour.
- egui app: when no `spread` is given, Paste and Paste in Place fill in the spread of the page in view (`canvas::current_page` + `page_loc`), the same way `app.deleteAllGuides` picks its spread. The menu items, shortcuts and the canvas paste event all go through `DesignApp::run`, so they all get it. While editing parent pages it is left as before.

Tests:
- `paste_lands_on_the_requested_spread` (engine): Paste in Place with `spread: 1` lands on spread 1; Paste without it still lands on spread 0.
- `paste_lands_on_the_page_in_view` (ui-egui): with page 2 in view, both Paste and Paste in Place put the copy on spread 1.

Both fail on main (the copy lands on spread 0).

Not in this PR: the issue also mentions that Move Page cannot move a new last page to the front and that pages cannot be dragged in the Pages panel. Those are separate problems.

title: Paste: copied objects land on the spread in view
author: noah1400
body:
Part of #348: the paste complaint. The Move Pages and Insert Pages dialogs that issue also mentions are not touched here.

Paste and Paste in Place put copied objects on the first spread, whatever page was in view: `edit.paste` had spread 0 hard-coded. Choosing a page in the Pages panel and pasting always filled page 1.

- `edit.paste` and `edit.pasteInPlace` take `spread`, like `frame.create`. Without it they still use the first spread.
- The app passes the spread in view (a parent spread while parents are edited), for the menu items, the shortcuts and the control channel. A caller that names a spread keeps it.
- With facing pages the objects keep their distance from the spine instead of from the spread's left edge. The first page sits alone right of the spine, so an object copied from a right-hand page lands on page 1 and not beside it.
- Single-sided pages have no spine and are measured from their left edge, as before.

Paste in Place is spread-based: content of a left-hand page lands on the left-hand page of the spread in view (left of a first page that sits alone), not necessarily on the page that was clicked. Ordinary Paste still offsets the copy by 12 pt from where it was copied; it is not centred in the window.

Validation: the five new tests (`paste_tests` in the engine, `paste_lands_on_the_spread_in_view` in the app) fail on main. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Compose: No Break runs and nonbreaking spaces stretch on justified lines
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #368.

Justification left out every glyph with `no_break` when it collected the stretchable spaces. A line whose spaces were all inside a No Break run had its extra width spread as letter spacing; on other lines the No Break spaces kept their natural width while the rest stretched. A typed nonbreaking space (U+00A0) was treated as a letter, so it got letter spacing too.

- No Break only stops line breaks inside the run. Its spaces stretch and shrink with word spacing like any other space.
- U+00A0 is a word space for justification and word spacing, and is still never a break opportunity. Fixed-width spaces (U+2002–U+200A, U+202F) keep their width.
- The line breaker gives those spaces the same word-space stretch and shrink as the justifier, so both agree on how full a line is. Break points don't change.
- A line whose only spaces are U+00A0 or No Break spaces widens those spaces instead of falling back to Single Word Justification.
- Spaces inside a character-fitting (jidori) run stay rigid in both the breaker and the justifier, so the run keeps its fitted width. A U+0020 there could stretch before.

New on `Glyph`: `is_word_space` (U+0020, U+00A0, an elastic U+3000) and `is_justify_space` (`is_space` plus U+00A0). `is_space` is unchanged.

Validation: `no_break_spaces_stretch_on_justified_lines` (No Break over one and over both spaces of a justified line: the spaces match and grow, letters keep their advance), `nonbreaking_space_stretches_and_fixed_width_one_does_not` and `jidori_run_keeps_its_width_on_a_justified_line` failed before the fix; `nonbreaking_space_alone_fills_a_justified_line` covers the Single Word Justification case. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: fix(#201): paste from other apps via system clipboard fallback
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Fixes #201.

## Problem

On macOS (and potentially other platforms), copy/paste from outside DesignCraft did nothing: the Paste event can carry no text when the content was copied in another app, and the paste command can also fail outright. Neither case tried the system clipboard.

## Changes

- Extract the paste handling into `paste_with_fallback(app, id, text, system_text)`:
  - event text present → run the Paste command with it, never touch the system clipboard;
  - event text empty (the macOS cross-app case) → fall back to the system clipboard;
  - paste fails → log, then fall back to the system clipboard; only report a status error if the fallback has nothing either.
- `system_text` is an injected closure — the seam the regression tests use, so no test touches the real clipboard.
- `arboard` now comes from the workspace dependency (same version/features as before).
- Move `read_system_clipboard` above the test module (fixes a pre-existing `clippy::items_after_test_module` error that `--all-targets` surfaces).

## Tests

Three new regression tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:
- empty Paste event falls back to the system clipboard text;
- failed paste falls back (no caret → nothing pasted, no crash; caret restored → text arrives);
- event text pastes as before and the fallback closure is never invoked (asserted by panicking in the seam).

## Verification

- `cargo xtask ci` — all 6 gates pass (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm)
- `cargo test -p designcraft-ui-egui --lib` — 147 passed

title: Layers: drag layers and objects to reorder them
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #371.

The Layers panel had no drag and drop: layers couldn't be reordered, and objects moved between layers only through Move Selection Here.

- **Layer order:** the panel lists layers frontmost first, matching `Document::layers` and `layer.new` (which adds at the top). It listed them backmost first before, so a new layer appeared at the bottom.
- **Drag a layer** to reorder it (`layer.move`). A line shows where it will land.
- **Drag an object row** onto a layer to put it at the top of that layer, or onto the upper or lower half of another object to put it in front of or behind that object, on its layer. Dragging a selected row moves every selected sibling with it.
- **Groups** expand to list their members. Members can be restacked inside their own group only; top-level objects can't be dropped into a group.
- **Selection square:** the square on a layer that holds selected objects can be dragged to another layer (`object.setLayer`, as Move Selection Here).
- Dropping onto a locked or hidden layer needs Cmd/Ctrl held.
- Every drop is one command and one undo step.

Commands:
- New `object.reorder {ids?, above?: id | below?: id | index?: n, layer?}`. The objects must be siblings on one spread; they keep their relative order. `above`/`below` place them next to a sibling on that sibling's layer; otherwise they go to `index` in `layer`, counted from the top. Bad input (unknown ids, index out of range, a target inside the moved set, mixed parents, a group member leaving its group…) is an error and changes nothing.
- `layer.move` is an error when `id` or `to` is missing or `to` is out of range (it defaulted or clamped before).
- `object.setLayer` moves a group member's whole top-level group, so a group's members stay on one layer, and returns `{changed}`. A missing or unknown `layer` is an error (it defaulted to the first layer before).
- A reorder that changes nothing records no undo step.

title: Tables: cell edge strokes in the Stroke panel and Cell Options, with gap colour and tint
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #370.

Cells stored a stroke per edge, and `table.setCell` could set weight, colour, tint and type, but nothing in the UI edited them, and cell edges had no gap colour or gap tint.

**Model and rendering**
- `CellStroke` and the cell/table style edge attributes gain `gap_color` and `gap_tint`. Files without them load as before, and default values aren't written.
- Cell edges draw every stroke type the model has: solid, dashed, dotted, the striped types, wavy, hashed and named stroke styles. Non-solid edges paint the gap colour under the stroke, on screen and in PDF.

**Commands**
- `table.setCell` `stroke: {weight?, color?, tint?, type?, gapColor?, gapTint?, edges?}`. `edges` is one name or a list: `all`, `outer`, `inner`, `top`, `left`, `bottom`, `right`, `innerHorizontal`, `innerVertical`. `top`, `left`, `bottom` and `right` are the outer sides of the selected range, as in the edge proxy. An edit starts from the stroke each chosen edge shows (the cell with the higher priority, else the table's alternating pattern or border), and writes the result to both cells that share the edge. One call is one undo step.
- Bad values are errors that change nothing: weights outside 0–1000, tints outside 0–1, unknown swatches, types or edge names. `table.setCell` clamped or ignored some of these before.
- New `table.getCellStroke {story?, table?, rows?, cols?, edges?}` reports the drawn stroke and the fill of the chosen edges; values that differ are `null`; `edges` counts drawn edges.
- `table.options` `border` takes the same stroke fields.
- `style.cell.create`/`edit` `stroke` and `style.table.create`/`edit` `border` take `type`, `gapColor` and `gapTint` with the same checks.

**Dash patterns:** `table.setCell` and `strokeStyle.new` accept 1–64 lengths, each 0 or 0.1–10 000 pt, not all 0. On screen and in PDF, a dash or dot pattern that would repeat more than 20 000 times along its path draws solid, for object strokes too, so a pattern from a file can't stall drawing.

title: Startup: pick the GPU that drives the display, fall back across adapters and backends, and log startup errors
author: aiongg
body:
For #273 and #334 (untested on the affected machines, so neither is closed by this PR).

DesignCraft let egui pick the high-performance adapter, kept the wgpu validation that fails on older Intel GPUs under Metal, and lost every startup error: the Windows build has no console and nothing was logged. This ports VectorCraft's startup handling, which fixed the same reports there.

From VectorCraft:
- **Validation (dc39146d):** the instance is created without `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL`, the check that fails with `Device(Lost)` on Intel Iris GPUs (#334's first error). `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` turns it back on.
- **Adapter choice (d12d5195, ac043129, 77a3cef4):** hardware before software, native before GL, DX12 before Vulkan, and the GPU that drives the display first (Windows display devices, Linux sysfs). Adapters that can't present are skipped. `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` and `WGPU_POWER_PREF` override the choice.
- **Recovery (d12d5195, 199a4641):** a panic in the graphics stack or an adapter that fails restarts the app without that adapter. The skip list travels as a `--gpu-skip=` argument, so child processes don't inherit it, and the file arguments are passed on. The status bar says which adapter was skipped. Every restart adds a new entry to the skip list, so restarts end.
- **First frame:** if no frame appears within 20 s, the app logs it and shows a note. It restarts without the adapter only when the UI thread has been stuck in the graphics stack for 60 s; a busy UI thread, or time while the window is minimized, hidden or unfocused, never counts. VectorCraft restarts after 20 s; this waits for a real hang so a locked screen or a long first compose doesn't switch adapters.
- **Software last:** software adapters (WARP, llvmpipe) are tried only after every hardware adapter on every backend.
- **Errors (VectorCraft's `main`):** when every option fails, `DesignCraft stopped: …` goes to stderr and `logs/designcraft.log`.

Recovered documents: reopening a recovered docu…

title: Layout: text wrap set on a placed graphic wraps text
author: aiongg
body:
A text wrap set on a placed image or PDF (the graphic inside a frame, not the frame) did nothing: the model had no place for it, IDML import read `TextWrapPreference` only from the frame, and layout only looked at top-level items. Text ran over such images.

- **Model:** `Graphic.wrap`, saved only when set; older files load unchanged.
- **IDML:** a `TextWrapPreference` on an `Image` or `PDF` element is imported and exported in its place.
- **Layout:** the graphic's wrap uses the part of the graphic the frame shows, plus the offsets. Wraps on items inside groups and pasted-into frames count too (up to 64 levels); the frame being composed is skipped.
- **Command and panel:** `object.textWrap` takes `content?: bool`; without ids it follows the selection, so with the graphic selected (Direct Selection) the Text Wrap panel shows and sets the graphic's wrap.

Validation: `wrap_on_a_placed_graphic_wraps_text_like_a_wrap_on_its_frame`, `wrap_on_a_placed_graphic_follows_its_crop_and_round_trips` (IDML) and `text_wrap_on_selected_content_sets_the_graphic_wrap` (engine); each fails without the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Layout: right-to-left binding puts parent page items on the right side
author: aiongg
body:
With right-to-left binding, every page showed the other side's parent page items (running heads, folios). `Document::parent_page_for` picked the parent page by list position (first for a left page, last for a right page), but right-to-left spreads list the right page first, parent spreads included.

- The parent page is chosen by position: the leftmost page of the parent spread for a left page, the rightmost for a right page (`Spread::parent_page_for_side`). Render, PDF export, the canvas, overrides and snapping all go through it.
- New parent spreads list their pages in binding order, and changing the binding in Document Setup reorders existing ones, so IDML export writes them as files from right-to-left documents have them.
- Spread bleed on the canvas and in spread PDF export takes its edges from the outer pages by position, not list order.

Validation: `right_to_left_binding_shows_the_parent_page_of_the_same_side` (engine: four pages, each shows its side's parent item, also after an IDML round trip) and an IDML import test with a right-to-left master spread; both fail without the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Sections: Kanji page numbers
author: aiongg
body:
IDML's `Kanji` page number style imported as Arabic, so folios read 1, 2, 3.

- New numbering style `kanji`, written digit by digit with 〇: 5 → 五, 10 → 一〇, 38 → 三八, 2026 → 二〇二六. Page names, page number markers, the Pages panel, PDF page labels, the table of contents and the index all follow.
- `layout.section`, `footnote.options` and `endnote.options` accept `kanji`; the Numbering & Section Options and Footnote Options dialogs offer it.
- IDML: sections and footnotes read and write `Kanji`. Sections also read and write `SingleLeadingZeros`, `DoubleLeadingZeros` and `TripleLeadingZeros` (01, 001, 0001), which imported as Arabic before. The list numbering format "一, 二, 三, 四..." imports and exports as Kanji.
- One new string, "Kanji", with entries in every table (machine-translated; native review welcome).

Validation: `kanji_numbers_are_written_digit_by_digit` (0 to `u32::MAX`), `kanji_page_numbers` (IDML section with Kanji style starting at 5: pages 五 and 六, round trip, a page number marker draws the same glyphs), and the list numbering import test. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Layout: wrap both sides of an object and around its contour
author: aiongg
body:
Text wrap treated every contour as the object's bounding box, and Wrap To Both Sides set text on one side only: a line could hold one segment.

**Wrap sides.** Lines can have several segments. Text runs on from one segment to the next on the same baseline.
- Both Sides leaves the segments on both sides of the object; Left Side and Right Side block the other side; Side Towards Spine and Side Away From Spine follow the obstacle's page; Largest Area picks the wider side once per obstacle and column.
- Segments narrower than 1.5 em are skipped (the existing threshold; there is no minimum segment width setting).
- When a line's segments turn out narrower or wider than the line breaker assumed, the rest of the paragraph is broken again with the real widths (at most 256 times per paragraph). This also stops text overrunning an obstacle at its top and bottom edges.
- Clicking, caret up/down and vertical justification handle lines with several segments.

**Contour wrap.** The obstacle follows the object's outline for each line's whole band (top to bottom of the line), widened by the top offset. The outline is the frame path with its corner options. For a graphic frame, Bounding Box uses the graphic's rectangle; Graphic Frame and Same as Clipping use the frame path.

**Model, commands, IDML, UI**
- `TextWrap.contour` (`ContourType`) with all six IDML values; older files load unchanged.
- `object.textWrap` takes `side` (all six values) and `contour` (`boundingBox`, `graphicFrame`, `sameAsClipping`). Given only `side` or `contour`, it keeps the mode. An unknown mode is an error (it fell back to bounding box before).
- IDML imports and exports `ContourOption/@ContourType`.
- The Text Wrap panel has Wrap To and Contour Type menus.

Not included: Detect Edges, Alpha Channel and Photoshop Path contours. They need the image's pixels or paths in layout. They're kept for the round trip, wrap around the frame path meanwhile, and can't be chosen in the panel or the command. Invert wrap …

title: fix(ui): Show the Pencil stroke while drawing
author: moppeeer
body:
The Pencil tool's stroke only appeared after the mouse button was released.

**Cause:** the tool reports the stroke so far as an `Overlay::Path`, but the canvas's overlay painter skipped path overlays (`Overlay::Path { .. } => {}`, there since the first commit), so they were never drawn. The Smooth and Erase tools' dashed drag previews were missing for the same reason.

**Fix:**
- The canvas draws path overlays: curves are flattened to about a quarter of a screen pixel, and dashed overlays are drawn dashed.
- The Pencil's preview was black, which disappears on a dark pasteboard; it is now drawn in the colour of the layer the path goes on, as InDesign does.

Validation:
- New UI test drives the real window: with the Pencil, press on the page and drag without releasing; the stroke is painted in the layer's colour, starting at the press and following the pointer, and nothing is created yet; releasing creates the path and ends the preview. It fails without the fix ("the stroke is painted while the button is down").
- The tools test now also checks the overlay while drawing (the stroke so far, in the layer's colour) and that it ends with the stroke.
- Rendered mid-stroke with `examples/ui_shot.rs`.
- UI and tools tests pass (one existing timing test ignored); formatting, Clippy, layers and the WASM build pass.

title: UI: no crash on textures past the GPU limit
author: con3code

title: UI: CJK interface text from installed fonts, on the Latin baseline
author: con3code
body:
Split from #353.

Without the craft-fonts build input the interface had no CJK glyphs: egui can't find system fonts, so Japanese and Chinese menus and labels drew as boxes. Korean and Traditional Chinese font names in the font menus did so in every build.

- The first installed UI face of each script (Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean; macOS, Windows and Linux families) is added as a fallback for the scripts craft-fonts doesn't cover.
- A fallback face sits on the UI face's baseline. egui centres a fallback's line height in the primary's, so a CJK face with a taller ascent or a line gap sat above or below the Latin text beside it. The tweak is computed from the two faces' line metrics (`designcraft_fonts::line_metrics`).
- The interface language's script comes first, before the built-in CJK faces, so Han characters take that language's forms.

The RTL measuring test now uses the built-in faces only, so its glyph widths don't depend on the machine's fonts.

Testing: new tests in `theme` with synthetic faces (glyphs without craft-fonts, the baseline tweak, Hangul, the order per interface language). `cargo fmt --check`, clippy and the `designcraft-fonts` / `designcraft-ui-egui` tests pass, except the font-menu test that also fails on a clean `main` on this Mac. Looked at on macOS (Hiragino Sans, PingFang, Apple SD Gothic Neo); Windows and Linux family names are untested. The web build has no system fonts, so nothing changes there.

title: UI: the welcome screen's Discord button clears the text beside it
author: con3code
body:
Split from #353.

In Japanese the line under "Join the ArtCraft community" is longer than the 640 px card allowed and ran under the Discord button.

title: fix(ui): Color Picker keeps the typed hex text and commits typed RGB values (#323)
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Fixes #323.

## Problem

The Color Picker's hex field rebuilt its string from the committed colour **every frame** (`color_picker` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`). egui's immediate-mode `TextEdit` shows whatever string it is handed, so every keystroke that didn't instantly parse as complete hex was wiped on the next frame — typing a code like `c0ffee` was impossible unless the whole value arrived at once (paste). This is the "automatically falls back … rather than respecting the user's wishes" symptom from the issue.

## Change

- The typed text now lives in the dialog state (`d.fields["hexEdit"]`). It resyncs to the canonical `rrggbb` only when the colour changes elsewhere in the same frame (picker square, eyedropper, RGB fields), never mid-keystroke.
- The colour commits when the typed text parses (`Color::from_hex` — 3/6/8 digits, optional `#`, names), exactly as before.
- RGB fields now round instead of truncating (`128.9 → 129`).
- Scope: `crates/ui-egui` only; the OK action (`object.color` with the committed `hex`) is unchanged.

## Tests

Two new dialog tests in `dialogs.rs`:
- `typing_hex_one_keystroke_at_a_time_survives_frames` — types `c0ffee` one character per frame with an idle frame between keystrokes (the exact broken pattern), asserts the buffer survives and the colour commits. **Fails on the old code** (verified by reverting just the fix: `typing_hex… FAILED`, RGB test still passed).
- `typing_an_rgb_value_commits_it` — types `128` into the R field of `#010203` and defocuses, asserts `#800203`. Note: Return can't be used to commit in a test — the dialog framework OKs on any Enter (`dialogs.rs:1715`) — so the test defocuses instead, which is also DragValue's normal commit path.

## Verification

- `./ci-lite.sh designcraft-ui-egui` (fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests): **146 passed, 0 failed**

title: Text: pair kerning crosses a change of colour, stroke or underline
author: MaridWSH
body:
Fixes #29.

## What happens

Giving one letter of a word another colour changes its kerning. The same `ay` set twice, once with the `a` in another colour, no longer lines up: the coloured pair sets wider. Stroke, underline and strikethrough changes do the same.

## Why

`shape_para` (`crates/compose/src/shape.rs`) shapes every story run on its own. The shaper gets the text around a run as pre/post context, which lets Arabic letters join across a change of style, but HarfBuzz never applies pair kerning (or any other GPOS adjustment) across a run boundary. Every attribute change, including a change that only affects how the glyphs are painted, broke the pair.

## What changes

- Consecutive runs whose resolved character properties differ only in how they are painted (fill, stroke, skew, underline and strikethrough options, conditions, change marks, XML tags) are shaped as one run. Every other difference (font, size, scale, tracking, kerning, OpenType features, language, CJK settings, jidori) still splits the run, so no shaping output changes there.
- After shaping, each glyph takes the style of the run its bytes belong to, so colours, strokes and rules draw exactly as before.
- A ligature can't be painted two ways: if the merged run produces a glyph whose cluster straddles a change (an `fi` ligature with `f` in another colour), the runs are shaped apart again, as they were before this change.
- Deleted or hidden conditional text and runs holding note references keep their own paths, unchanged.

## Tests

`crates/compose/src/tests.rs`:
- `kerning_crosses_a_change_of_colour`: `ay` sets identically whether or not `a` is painted in `[Paper]`, the two glyphs keep different styles, and the pair really is kerned (`a` before `y` advances less than `a` alone). Before the fix: `y sits 5.988 after a in one colour, 6.108 in two`.
- `ligature_is_not_painted_two_ways`: `fi` ligates in one colour; with `f` in another colour it sets as two glyphs in two styles.

title: Undo: a command that runs another is one undo step
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #406.

Some commands are written as "run another command": Cut runs Clear, Duplicate runs Move, Paste in Place runs Paste, Bring to Front and its siblings run Arrange, and pasting text runs Type. Both recorded an undo step, so after the first Undo a second one did nothing.

- A command run by an undoable command no longer records a step of its own; the outer command's step covers both.
- A command that is no undo step itself (placing the caret, which may turn an empty frame into a text frame) leaves the steps of the commands it runs alone.
- A script's steps still record while it runs, so an Undo step in a script works as before, and the script remains one step.
- A command that fails after changing the document now records its step. Before, a script that stopped at a bad step left its earlier steps in the document with nothing to undo.

Validation: `a_command_that_runs_another_is_one_undo_step` and `a_command_that_fails_partway_can_be_undone` fail on main. Four more tests pin the rest: a command that fails after the one it ran changed the document, a script that undoes its own step, the step of a command run by one that is no step itself, and a command that panics. The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Fonts: a pan-CJK font's family name decides its font menu group
author: con3code
body:
A Simplified Chinese face was listed under Japanese in the font menus: on my Mac, "RODE Noto Sans CJK SC R" and "… B" (a vendor's copy of Noto Sans CJK SC).

**Cause.** A font of a pan-CJK family lists the code pages of every language it covers (here JIS, Chinese Simplified and both Korean ones). This copy has no `meta` languages and only English family names, so the code pages decided, and with several of them the first group in menu order won: Japanese.

**Change.** When a font lists several CJK code pages, the region tag in its family name decides, if the font lists that language:

- `JP` → Japanese
- `SC`, `CN`, `GB` → Simplified Chinese
- `TC`, `HK`, `TW`, `MO`, `HC` → Traditional Chinese
- `KR` → Korean

The tag must be a whole word in capitals, so "Script" or "Sc" don't count. Fonts with one CJK code page, or none, are grouped exactly as before, and `meta` and name-table languages still come first.

**Testing.**
- New test `a_region_tag_in_the_family_name_decides_between_several_code_pages`: the tags above, names without a tag, a tag for a language the font doesn't list, a single code page, and no CJK code page.
- On this Mac I listed the group of the 47 installed families with a region tag before and after: only the two RODE faces moved (to Simplified Chinese). PingFang, Songti, Heiti, Hiragino Sans GB and the Noto Sans/Serif CJK families kept their groups.
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy and the `designcraft-fonts` tests pass. In `designcraft-ui-egui`, only `typing_in_the_font_menu_searches_and_never_reaches_the_story` fails, as it does on a clean `main` here (this Mac has "Source Sans Pro" installed, so ↓ picks it).
- I haven't looked at the menu itself in the running app, only at the data it lists.

If you would rather not read anything from the family name, an alternative is to leave such fonts in the first group and only fix the tie order. I went with the name because these families carry their language nowhere else.

title: Tools: move a placed graphic inside its frame
author: aiongg
body:
A placed image couldn't be moved inside its frame: every drag, arrow key and Select › Content move moved the frame and the image together, and the content grabber was drawn but did nothing.

- **Direct Selection:** a click on a graphic frame selects its content; a drag moves the content and leaves the frame where it is. Shift locks the drag to one axis. While dragging, the whole image shows at reduced opacity, including the part outside the frame, with its bounds outlined.
- **Content grabber:** with the Selection tool, the circle at the centre of a graphic frame shows on the selected frame and under the pointer (not on frames smaller than 36 px on screen). Pressing it selects the content; dragging it moves the content. Resize handles and the rotate zone take priority. Dragging elsewhere in the frame moves the frame, as before.
- **Double-click** a frame with content to switch between the frame and its content. Text frames still switch to the Type tool.
- **Arrow keys** nudge the content when the content is selected.
- Items pasted into a frame move the same way. Text frames, empty frames and groups have no content to move.

`transform.move` takes `content?: bool`. Without `ids` or `copy`, it follows the selection's content flag, so the tools, the arrow keys, Transform Again and the control channel share one path. The delta is converted into the frame's space, so content in rotated or scaled frames moves along the page axes. Auto-fit is left on; the next frame resize refits as before. Each drag or nudge is one undo step. `transform.move` with `ids` naming an item inside a group or frame now moves it in its container's space.

No format change: the graphic's transform is already saved and exported to IDML.

Not included: scaling or rotating content from the Control and Transform panels, and resizing content by its own handles.

title: Documents: Save adds .designcraft, and the OS opens DesignCraft and IDML files
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #158, #211 and #375.

A document saved under a name without `.designcraft` got no extension, File › Open showed only `.designcraft` and `.idml` files, and the macOS app claimed no document types (its plist still declared another app's), so Finder, the Dock and Open With couldn't open documents.

**Saving**
- `file.save`, `file.saveAs` and `file.saveACopy` add `.designcraft` to a path that lacks it and report the file written. Saving a document opened from a file without an extension writes back to that file.
- The save dialog filters by the suggested extension, so macOS and Windows add it and ask about replacing the final name. Linux dialogs don't, so the app asks "Replace File?" itself before overwriting. Exports get their extension the same way when the typed name has none.

**Opening**
- `file.open` recognises IDML and DesignCraft files by their content, so the extension may be missing. Anything else is an error ("not a DesignCraft or IDML file").
- File › Open adds an "All files" choice. A file without an extension dropped on the window opens when it is a document, and is placed otherwise.

**The OS**
- macOS: `Info.plist` exports a `.designcraft` document type, imports `.idml`, and declares both in `CFBundleDocumentTypes` (editor for `.designcraft`, viewer for IDML). Finder double-clicks, Dock drops and Open With arrive as Apple events, handled through `fmv-macos-events` (pinned `=0.1.0`, MIT OR Apache-2.0, as in PhotoCraft, PdfCraft and WordCraft, because the workspace forbids `unsafe`). Files that arrive before the window is ready open once it is.
- Windows: the installer registers `.designcraft` with an Open verb and adds DesignCraft to `.idml`'s Open With list without taking over the default.
- Linux: `mime.xml` defines `application/x-designcraft` and the IDML type, and the `.desktop` file lists them.

Not tested on a running system: the macOS events and plist, the Windows installer associations, the Linux MIME registration. The macOS and Windows code…

title: IDML: frames take corners, effects and text wrap from their object style
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #389.

IDML writes on a page item only the values that differ from its object style. The importer read corners, drop shadow, feather and text wrap from the item alone, so a frame that overrode only its corner radius or shadow offsets lost the style's rounded corners and its shadow.

Page items now take every value they lack from their applied object style, then the styles it is based on, one attribute at a time; values on the item win:
- corner shape and radius per corner (`CornerOption`/`CornerRadius` for all corners apply at a level only when that level sets no single corner);
- `TransparencySetting`: blending, drop shadow and feather, merged element by element and attribute by attribute;
- `TextWrapPreference` (mode, side, invert, each offset), `TextFramePreference`, `BaselineFrameGridOption` and `FrameFittingOption`.

A style whose `ObjectStyleObjectEffectsCategorySettings` turns an effect off (`EnableDropShadow="false"`) passes none of that effect's values on. The `BasedOn` chain stops after 16 levels or at a cycle.

Export writes the column rule attributes on every `TextFramePreference`, so a frame without a rule doesn't pick up its style's rule when the file is opened again.

Not included: inner shadow, glows, bevel and emboss, satin, and the fill, stroke and content transparency settings, which the importer doesn't read yet.

Validation: four tests in `tests/object_styles.rs` (the issue's case; a two-level `BasedOn` chain; an item or a style that turns an effect off; the column rule round trip, which fails without the export change). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: IDML: gradient and directional feathers import and export
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #390.

The model and renderer support gradient and directional feathers (`object.gradientFeather`, `object.directionalFeather`), but IDML import read only `FeatherSetting` and `DropShadowSetting`, and export wrote only `FeatherSetting`.

| IDML | Model |
|---|---|
| `GradientFeatherSetting` `Applied`, `Type` (`Radial`, else linear), `Angle` | `gradient_feather` `on`, `radial`, `angle` |
| `GradientStart`, `Length`, `Angle` | `gradient_feather.vector` (as for gradient fills) |
| first and last `OpacityGradientStop` `Opacity`, `Location` | `start`, `end`; the locations move the vector's ends |
| `DirectionalFeatherSetting` `Applied`, `TopWidth`, `LeftWidth`, `BottomWidth`, `RightWidth` | `directional_feather` `on`, `widths` |

Values that aren't finite or are out of range are ignored or clamped. Export writes two opacity stops.

Not converted (no model fields yet): stops between the first and last, stop midpoints, `HiliteAngle`/`HiliteLength`, and the directional feather's `Angle`, `Noise`, `ChokeAmount` and `FollowShapeMode`.

Validation: `imports_gradient_and_directional_feathers` and `gradient_and_directional_feathers_round_trip`. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Assets: one asset per image, and saves leave out unused ones
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #391.

Every placement of an image became its own asset, each embedded on save (16 photos placed 2466 times made an 8.9 GB file), and an asset stayed in the file after its frame got another image.

- **One asset per file.** Two assets are the same when their type, PDF page and bytes are equal (pointer, then length, then bytes; no hashing). Placements keep their own transform, crop and fitting on `Graphic`. Missing images merge only when they have the same link.
- **Every path that adds an image reuses an identical asset:** Place (also into a frame), `place.load`, media and posters, table cell graphics, math, data merge, IDML import (which also reads each linked file once), and paste, duplicate and data merge templates. Paste also used to point a pasted image at the wrong asset when ids collided, and didn't copy assets of anchored objects, table cells and media posters; both are fixed.
- **Saving** merges duplicates and leaves out assets nothing uses, on a copy of the document, so undo can still bring a removed image back. Package and Copy Links write only used assets; Links lists only used assets.
- **Opening** a file that holds duplicates merges them; identical bytes share one buffer while reading.
- `Document::used_assets()` follows spreads, parent spreads, groups, multi-state objects, anchored and inline objects, table cells and note text (to 64 levels; deeper documents keep every asset).

IDML can't share an image between placements (`<Contents>` belongs to each `Image`), so embedding stays per placement. `embedImages: false` writes linked images as links.

title: PDF: right-to-left text extracts in reading order
author: aiongg
body:
Part of #392.

Hebrew and Arabic in exported PDFs looked right but copied and searched reversed in viewers that order text by position, and pointed Hebrew letters extracted doubled (`אַא`): a mark's vertical offset started a new text run, so a base letter and its point were split across runs and mapped twice.

- Right-to-left glyphs are written in reading order, and ActualText spans hold single clusters only; they never nest. Line-wide ActualText spans made poppler drop the line's text, and PDFKit ignores them.
- A cluster of several glyphs (a letter and its marks) gives each glyph its own character when each glyph stands for one; ligatures and contextual forms keep one shared text, as before.
- Runs no longer split on vertical offsets: the offset is part of each glyph, with the skew applied, so glyphs land exactly where composed.
- Kashidas added by justification extract as no text.

Validation (new `rtl_tests.rs`, with synthetic Hebrew and Arabic fonts): `hebrew_extracts_in_reading_order_with_points_on_their_letters`, `hebrew_words_in_left_to_right_lines_extract_in_reading_order`, `kashidas_extract_as_no_text` (these three fail without the change), `pointed_letters_are_drawn_where_composed`, `arabic_ligatures_extract_their_letters`. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: PDF: generated text keeps its characters under small caps
author: aiongg
body:
Page numbers, other markers and list labels set in small caps extracted as U+FFFD (or as the previous glyph's text) from exported PDFs. Their glyphs point at a placeholder character or at no text, so the PDF text fell back to the font's reverse cmap, which has no entry for a substituted glyph such as `one.s`. Typed text was already right.

- Shaped glyphs carry `generated_text`: the generated cluster's text on its first glyph, empty on the rest. Page number and marker replacements and list labels fill it; hyphens, kashidas, tab leaders and ruby keep the cmap fallback.
- PDF export uses it before the cmap fallback.

Under All Small Caps, `A` and `a` share one glyph; the PDF holds the second spelling as ActualText, as before.

Validation: `small_caps_and_small_cap_figures_extract_as_typed` (Source Sans 3 under Small Caps and All Small Caps: typed figures, a page number and a list label; no U+FFFD). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: CJK: smaller runs align to the line's em box centre
author: aiongg
body:
With em box centre character alignment, a smaller CJK run in a line of Latin text sat too low. The alignment took each font's em box from its `hhea` ascender and descender scaled to one em, which puts a Latin font's em centre too low (0.30 em for DejaVu Serif instead of 0.38).

The alignment em box is the font's `BASE` ideographic em box when the font has one, otherwise 0.88 em above and 0.12 em below the baseline. Em box top, centre and bottom alignment use it; ICF alignment and the leading model are unchanged.

Validation: `smaller_cjk_run_aligns_to_the_line_em_box_centre` (a 6 pt CJK run in a 10 pt line: em centres equal within 0.01 pt; Roman baseline alignment keeps it on the baseline). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: CJK: custom mojikumi tables without a base set apply their rules
author: aiongg
body:
Builds on #129 (its commits are included; review the last commit only, or merge #129 first).

A custom mojikumi table imported from IDML without `BasedOnMojikumiSet` was not applied: `Rules::resolve` looked the table's own name up as a preset, failed with "unknown base preset", and preflight reported the table as not applied. IDML files leave the base set out when it isn't one of the named sets.

A table without a base set now resolves on the default half-em set (`LineEndAllOneHalfEmEnum`) with its own rows on top. Preflight notes that the table names no base set and that its rules apply on the default set. Export still leaves `BasedOnMojikumiSet` out for these tables, so the assumed base is not written back. A name that matches no table, or a table naming an unknown base, is reported as before.

Validation: `cjk_mojikumi_table_without_base_set_applies_its_rows` (synthetic IDML table with one override row and no base: the override pair uses its values, an unlisted pair the half-em default, and the table round-trips unchanged); `preflight_notes_an_assumed_mojikumi_base_set_without_calling_the_table_unapplied`. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: M2.1: manual text threading (frame.thread, frame.unthread, out-port click)
author: kubuntugamer
body:
Implements manual text threading (alpha blocker Gap 0).

## Changes

### Engine Commands (`crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs`)
- `frame.thread` - thread one text frame to another
- `frame.unthread` - unthread after a frame (breaks the thread)
- `frame.startThread` - start threading mode by clicking an out-port
- `frame.clearThread` - cancel threading mode
- `frame.threadOrCreate` - create a new text frame and thread to it

### Session State (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`)
- Added `loaded_text: Option<(StoryId, ItemId)>` to track threading state

### Tooling (`crates/engine/src/tooling.rs`)
- Updated `ToolContext` to include `loaded_text`

### Selection Tool (`crates/tools/src/select.rs`)
- Added `threading` field to `Drag::Pending`
- Added `port_at()` to detect clicks on text frame in/out ports
- Out-port click - starts threading (calls `frame.startThread`)
- In-port click - unthreads (calls `frame.unthread`)
- Loaded text cursor: click frame to thread, drag empty canvas to create+thread
- `Cursor::LoadedText` shown during threading
- Escape key cancels threading

### Tools Library (`crates/tools/src/lib.rs`)
- Updated `ToolContext` with `loaded_text`

## User Workflow (InDesign parity)
1. Select a text frame with Selection tool (V)
2. Click the out-port (bottom-right) - cursor changes to loaded text cursor
3. Click another text frame - frames are threaded
4. OR drag on empty canvas - new frame created and threaded
5. Press Escape to cancel
6. Click in-port (top-left) to unthread

## Testing
- All existing doc, engine, and tools tests pass
- Follows existing command/tool patterns with undo/redo support

Closes alpha blocker Gap 0: manual text threading is now implemented.

title: Text: Optical kerning spaces pairs from their outlines
author: MaridWSH
body:
Fixes #181.

## What happens

`KerningMethod="$ID/Optical"` imports as `Kerning::Optical`, but shaping treated it exactly like Metrics: the font's kern pairs were applied and nothing else. Text set with Optical in InDesign (often noticeably tighter at display sizes) came out wider in DesignCraft, rewrapped, and went overset in tightly fitted frames.

## What changes

A new module, `crates/compose/src/optical.rs`, spaces pairs from the glyph outlines when the text's kerning is Optical. The font's own kern pairs are turned off for such text, as Optical replaces Metrics in InDesign.

- **Profiles.** Each glyph's outline is flattened and sampled into 28 horizontal bands across the em (from 1.0 em above the baseline to 0.3 em below). Each band keeps the leftmost and rightmost ink. A glyph drawn more than 8 em wide or tall (a hostile font) gets no profile.
- **Pair gap.** For two adjacent glyphs, the ink gap (left glyph's right edge to right glyph's left edge, at the shaped distance without tracking, including the glyphs' x offsets) is read in every band where both have ink. The mean and the smallest gap are kept. Pairs with fewer than two shared bands (an apostrophe over a period) are left alone.
- **Reference.** The font's natural stem-to-stem gap is the mean gap of `nn` (or of `HH`, then `oo`, when the font lacks them), measured the same way and cached per face.
- **Adjustment.** The pair moves 60% of the way from its mean gap to the reference gap, never taking the smallest gap under 30% of the reference, and never by more than −0.12 em or +0.06 em. `nn` itself stays as the font set it; diagonal pairs and letter-punctuation pairs close up; round pairs such as `oo`, and pairs that already touch, open slightly.
- **Scope.** Letters of the Latin, Greek and Cyrillic scripts, digits and Western punctuation. Spaces, combining marks, missing glyphs, right-to-left runs (Arabic, Hebrew, and the punctuation inside them), CJK, upright and tate-chu-yoko glyphs in vertical frames k…

title: Frame grids: CJK text frames set in a grid of character cells
author: con3code
body:
Split from #353, as discussed there: frame grids first, without mojikumi.

A frame grid is a text frame whose text is set in a grid of character cells, as Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is on squared manuscript paper (稿紙 / 原稿用紙 / 원고지). The aim of this PR is to let everyone see and try the grid itself, for all three languages.

Punctuation takes a whole cell each here. Language-specific spacing in a grid (half-width punctuation and bracket aki in Japanese, punctuation compression in Chinese) is not in it: I'll follow #129 and take the grid's aki from its engine once it lands, as you suggested.

## What it adds

- **Model** (`doc::framegrid`): font, size and scales (the cell), the space between cells along the line and between lines (`charAki`, `lineAki`), a line alignment override, grid and character alignment (em box, ICF, Roman baseline), count position and size, view, and which cell of a line is shaded. `DocSettings.frame_grid` is the grid new frame grids get. Counts aren't stored: they follow from the frame size.
- **Composition** (`compose::framegrid`, small): Han characters, kana, hangul and full-width punctuation of the grid's size sit one to a cell, a character pitch apart; Western text and other sizes keep their widths. A line takes as many rows as its em box needs (a larger heading takes whole rows) and is placed in them by the grid alignment. Overset and text wrap go by rows. Horizontal and vertical.
- **Commands**: `frame.create {grid}`, `object.frameGridOptions`, `object.frameGridInfo`, `object.frameType`, `type.applyGridFormat`, `document.frameGridDefaults`. Resizing a grid snaps to whole cells. A new grid size keeps the counts and resizes the frame; text that follows the grid takes the new format, and characters given their own keep it.
- **Tools**: Horizontal Grid Tool (Y) and Vertical Grid Tool (Q).
- **Interface**: Object › Frame Grid Options and Frame Type, Edit › Apply Grid Format, View › Show Frame Grids (cells, N/Z or outline view, character …

title: PDF: items with soft effects keep their text wrap
author: aiongg
body:
Builds on #381 (its commits are included; review the last commit only, or merge #381 first).

PDF export replaces each object with soft effects (feather, glow, bevel, satin) by a 300 ppi image of it in a copy of the document, and composes the stories from that copy. The image had no wrap and the original object was gone, so text that wrapped around a feathered frame or graphic ran straight through it in the PDF, though the canvas and PNG export wrapped it.

With PDF export, an object that wraps text stays in the export copy beside its image as a nonprinting stand-in. It keeps its id, path, transform and wraps (frame, placed graphic, grouped items). Its text, form field, button and media are cleared, so it adds nothing to the PDF. EPUB's rasterize option is unchanged (reflowable EPUB has no wrap).

Validation: `objects_with_soft_effects_keep_their_text_wrap_in_pdf` (a feathered frame with a contour wrap and a feathered placed graphic with a bounding-box wrap: the story's wrap exclusions are the same before and after rasterizing; the stand-ins don't print, their images do). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Objects: group siblings inside a group; refuse mixed levels and spreads
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #412.

`object.group` collected the named objects that are top-level items of the first object's spread and indexed the first of them, so objects already inside a group made it panic. Objects at different levels, or on different spreads, made a group of the top-level ones and silently left the rest out.

- Siblings inside one group are grouped into a new group inside that group, at the frontmost sibling's place; nothing moves, and undo restores the parent.
- Objects on different spreads or at different levels, a group with its own child, and objects inside a multi-state object are refused with an error that says what can be grouped. The document is unchanged.
- Group is disabled for a selection it can't group. A call that names its ids is checked against those ids, not the selection.

Validation: `grouping_objects_already_in_a_group_does_not_panic` (the issue's steps, a content selection, and `states.create`; panicked before), `grouping_siblings_inside_a_group_nests_them_and_undo_restores`, `grouping_across_levels_or_spreads_is_refused_and_changes_nothing`. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: feat(ui): standardize window decorations and title bar with VectorCraft (#440)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Resolves #440

### Overview
This pull request aligns window decorations and title bar handling in designcraft with the standard established in VectorCraft (PR #969) and PhotoCraft (PR #1903):
- Custom client-side titlebar dragging, caption buttons (Minimize, Maximize/Restore, Close), and edge resize zones on Windows and Linux.
- Support for `System Title Bar` preference under User Interface settings to restore OS-native decorations on Windows and Linux if desired.
- macOS retains native window buttons and fullsize content view.

title: macOS: the window buttons sit centred in the title bar
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #333.

On macOS the app bar was taller than the band in which AppKit centres the window buttons, so the buttons sat high, and the empty bar didn't act like a title bar.

- The macOS bar is the 28 pt band AppKit centres the buttons in (the 7 pt band and border below it are unchanged); content starts 8 pt after the green button, and every control is centred on the buttons' line. On all platforms the bar's content row uses the bar's full height (egui kept 1 pt for its separator, so controls sat 0.5 pt high).
- Double-clicking empty bar space does what System Settings › Desktop & Dock › "Double-click a window's title bar to" says (zoom, minimize or nothing; read once at launch with `defaults read -g AppleActionOnDoubleClick`, zoom if unreadable). Dragging empty bar space moves the window. Controls in the bar keep their own clicks and drags.

Validation: `the_mac_app_bar_centres_and_clears_the_traffic_lights`, `the_empty_mac_title_bar_zooms_and_moves_the_window` (double-click and drag on empty spots send `Maximized`/`StartDrag`; on Home, Share and File they don't), `parses_the_defaults_output`, `zoom_toggles_and_minimize_minimizes`. macOS clippy passes; not yet tested on a Mac. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

AppKit drags the window from anywhere in the full-size title-bar band, so the app clears the window's `movable` flag (objc2-app-kit safe methods, no `unsafe`) while the pointer is on a bar control; empty bar space still moves the window.

title: Fonts: macOS fonts that font services and managers activate are listed
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #261, #327.

On macOS, Adobe Fonts (Creative Cloud), RightFont and other font managers register fonts with CoreText from their own folders. DesignCraft scanned only the font folders, so those families were reported missing and substituted, while other apps on the same Mac used them.

The font scan also reads the font files CoreText has available (`core_text::font_collection::create_for_all_families`, through the safe `core-text` crate, MIT/Apache-2.0, macOS only; no `unsafe`). Files the folders already gave and repeats are skipped, unreadable paths are ignored, and files without an extension are read too, since font services store some that way. The scan stays on its background thread, and a rescan asks CoreText again. The desktop app and `designcraft-cli` both see these fonts. Linux, Windows and the web build are unchanged.

Validation: `fonts_the_platform_lists_outside_the_font_folders_are_cataloged_once` (on Linux, with a stand-in for the CoreText list: a file with no extension in a hidden folder, listed twice, is cataloged once and loads; a font-folder file listed under another path isn't cataloged twice; missing paths and folders are skipped). macOS clippy passes; not yet tested on a Mac. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Tools: live corners round a frame's corners by dragging
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #186.

The yellow square beside a selected rectangle was drawn, but nothing handled clicks on it.

With the Selection tool, a single unlocked rectangle frame large enough on screen shows the square below its top-right corner. Clicking it shows a yellow diamond at each corner:
- Dragging a diamond along its edge sets the size of all four corners (one undo step, live preview); Shift changes only that corner. Sizes are clamped to half the shorter side, and a corner with no shape becomes rounded.
- Alt-click steps that corner through rounded, inverse rounded, inset, bevel and fancy; Shift+Alt-click sets every corner to the next shape.
- Escape, a click on empty canvas, another selection or another tool leaves the mode.
Rotated and sheared frames work in the frame's own axes. `object.cornerOptions` takes an optional `corners` list (four `{shape, size}` in path order). The square is no longer drawn for tools that can't use it.

Validation: `live_corners_click_widget_then_drag_rounds_all_corners`, `live_corners_shift_drag_and_alt_click_change_one_corner`, `live_corners_end_on_escape_empty_click_and_other_selection`, `live_corner_diamonds_follow_a_rotated_frame` (tools); `live_corner_gestures_are_one_undo_step_each` (engine); `live_corner_widget_and_diamonds_draw` (offscreen render: the square, then the diamonds after a click). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

Tested on macOS (Apple silicon): widget, all-corner drag with one undo, Shift-drag, Option-click shapes, Escape.

title: macOS: Settings… is in the app menu
author: aiongg
body:
On macOS, Preferences… sat under Edit, while Mac apps put Settings… in the application menu.

The native app menu lists About DesignCraft, Join the ArtCraft Discord…, Settings… (⌘K, runs `app.preferences`), Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All and Quit, and the native Edit menu leaves Preferences… out. The app menu is described as data in `menus.rs` (`MAC_APP_MENU`), and `native_menu_tree()` drops from the other menus the commands it already has, so ⌘K is registered once. Its labels are translated (About and the Discord item were English only). The in-window menus (Windows, Linux, web, and macOS without the native menu bar) keep Edit › Preferences….

Validation: `mac_settings_follow_about_in_the_app_menu_and_leave_edit` (order and separators, translated label, unique ids, Edit keeps Preferences… in the window menus but not in the native tree, no stray separators). macOS clippy passes. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

Tested on macOS (Apple silicon): app menu order, Settings… and ⌘K open Preferences once, Edit has no Preferences, Japanese label.

title: UI: document views have scrollbars, and Alt pans while editing text
author: aiongg
body:
Document views had no scrollbars: panning needed Space-drag, middle-drag, the wheel or the Hand tool. While editing text, Space types a space, so there was no temporary Hand tool there.

- Each document view (every split pane and the second window) has a vertical scrollbar on the right and a horizontal one along the bottom, 10 px, outside the rulers. The range is the pasteboard joined with the visible area; the thumb shows the visible fraction (18 px minimum). Dragging the thumb pans, clicking the track pages by one view, and the bars follow panning and zooming by any other means. Rotated views scroll along screen axes, like the wheel. Not shown in Presentation mode.
- With the Type tool in a text frame, Alt held at the press pans like the Hand tool (hand cursor) and leaves the caret and selection alone. Alt pressed after a text drag has started still copies the dragged text.

Validation: `document_views_have_scrollbars_beside_the_view`, `dragging_a_thumb_pans_and_clicking_the_track_pages`, `scrolling_the_view_moves_the_thumbs`, `alt_drag_while_editing_text_pans_and_keeps_the_caret`. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

Tested on macOS (Apple silicon): both scrollbars (thumb drag, track click), two-finger scrolling, Option-drag while typing keeps the caret.

title: UI: Return and Escape in the font menu stay in the menu, never reach the dialog under it
author: aiongg
body:
In Paragraph and Character Style Options (Basic Character Formats) and in Find/Replace Font, pressing Return in an open font menu picked the family and also confirmed the dialog, and Escape closed the menu and cancelled the dialog.

The font menu consumes the keys it uses (↑, ↓, Return, Escape) and closes itself on Escape, so a dialog's OK/Cancel no longer sees them. The hand-drawn font fields (Properties › Character, Contextual Task Bar) report as combo boxes with the current family as their value, for screen readers.

Every font field was checked for #86 and #335: each search field takes the click, stays open and filters in every workspace (Printing and Proofing included), so those reports describe 0.5.0, before c64e538 and #143.

Validation: `every_font_field_searches_in_every_workspace` (each font field in four workspace/window setups: open, click search, type, pick with ↓ and Return; the story is unchanged), `font_fields_in_panels_and_dialogs_search` (Glyphs, Paragraph Style Options, Find/Replace Font: Return and Escape leave the dialog open; failed before). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

Tested on macOS (Apple silicon): Control bar, Properties and Paragraph Style font menus filter, pick with Return and close with Escape without reaching the dialog.

title: M6: Adopt craft-print and support Windows PDF printing

title: Preserve editorial clipboard payloads and retrieve text before menu Paste
author: sanyamsingh001
body:

title: Respect explicit primary deletions and consumed reflow inputs
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Smart Text Reflow can recreate deliberately removed primary frames or pages after unrelated edits. Preserve the remaining story and flow chain after deletion or Cut, and resume reflow when content or layout inputs consumed by that story change.

Unused conditional-text definitions preserve explicit removals. Changes to the effective visibility of conditioned text in the primary overset tail still resume page growth as one undoable edit.

title: Layout: parent-page margins and guides, Create Guides on the current page, ruler-unit-aware Margins and Columns
author: soro-82
body:
## Description

Four related fixes in the Layout menu and parent-page workflow. I hit all four using DesignCraft v0.4.0 on CachyOS (Linux) with the ruler units set to millimeters.

### 1. Margins of a parent page did nothing on the parent

**Reproduce:** Pages panel → edit a parent page → change the margins in Properties.
**Expected:** the margin box on the parent page moves.
**Actual:** nothing changed on the parent; the *document* pages changed instead.

**Cause:** `layout.marginsAndColumns` only walked `doc.spreads`, never `doc.parents`, and while parents are being edited `canvas::current_page` returns page 0, so the Properties panel read and wrote document page 1.

**Fix:**
- `layout.marginsAndColumns` takes a new `parent: index` parameter (with `pages` indexing that parent's pages). An unknown parent is an error, not a silent no-op.
- Document pages based on that parent follow the change only if their margins and columns still equal the parent's old values, so pages with their own margins keep them.
- New `canvas::current_parent_page`; the Properties margin fields read and write the parent page in view while parents are being edited.

### 2. Layout ▸ Create Guides always used the first page

**Cause:** the menu opened the generic command form, which never passed `spread`/`page`, so `spread_param` fell back to `Doc(0)` and the guides went on every page of the first spread.

**Fix:** a dedicated dialog (`open_create_guides`) targets the spread and page under the view centre, or the parent page being edited, via the new `canvas::current_spread_page`.

### 3. Guides placed on a parent page did not show on its document pages

New `Document::inherited_guides(abs)`. Parent guides stay stored on the parent page only (nothing is copied), so editing or deleting one updates every child page. Vertical positions are shifted from the parent page's place in its spread to the child page's place in its own, so facing pages work. They are drawn on child pages and used by guide s…

title: Moving a sheared, rotated text frame leaves no text trails
author: moppeeer
body:
## Problem
Moving a text frame that is sheared and rotated left fragments of its text behind on the canvas.

## Cause
After an edit, the canvas repaints only the damaged regions (`designcraft_render::damage`). A text frame's damage was its path's bounds plus a margin. Its text, though, is composed in the box around the path *in the frame's own coordinates* (`Item::text_area`), then transformed by the frame's matrix. When the path is sheared (its local box's corners lie outside it) and the frame is rotated, that turned box reaches well past the path's bounds. Glyphs drawn there were never repainted, so each step of a move left a strip of old text.

## Fix
`damage.rs` measures an item's painted area as its bounds plus, for text frames, the transformed text box (recursively for groups). Both damage paths use it: moved items, and story frames whose text changed.

## Tests
- `moving_a_sheared_turned_text_frame_leaves_no_trail`: moves a sheared, rotated, full text frame. The old render patched over the damage must equal a full render of the new document.
- The patch-and-compare steps of `patched_render_equals_full_render` are now a shared helper.

title: Honor IDML SameParaStyleSpacing between same-style paragraphs (#449)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #449.

IDML import dropped `SameParaStyleSpacing`, so consecutive paragraphs of the same style always got the ordinary space after + space before, even when the IDML set the same-style spacing to 0.

Changes:
- `crates/doc/src/attrs.rs`: new paragraph attribute `same_para_style_spacing: Option<f64>` (`None` = Ignore, the default), same shape as `paragraph_kashida_width`.
- `crates/idml/src/import.rs`: reads `SameParaStyleSpacing`. A number sets the spacing. An enumeration value (Ignore) is stored as an explicit "off", so it still wins over a value from a based-on style.
- `crates/idml/src/export.rs`: writes the numeric value back, so it survives a round trip.
- `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`: when a paragraph has the same paragraph style as the one before it (and that one is not a table) and the spacing is set, the gap between them is the same-style spacing. It replaces the previous paragraph's space after plus this paragraph's space before. At a boundary between different styles, the ordinary spacing still applies. Empty paragraphs are handled the same way.

Tests:
- `compose::tests::same_para_style_spacing_replaces_space_between_same_style_paragraphs` covers: ordinary spacing (unset), zero and 20 pt, an empty paragraph between two same-style paragraphs, and a style change at the last paragraph keeping the ordinary spacing.
- `idml::tests::same_para_style_spacing_imports_and_round_trips` covers importing `0` and `Nothing` (Ignore) and an export/import round trip of the numeric value.

An explicit Ignore on export is not written, matching how `ParagraphKashidaWidth` is handled. A paragraph that inherits no value still ignores the setting, as before.

title: Show the first parent page behind single-sided pages (#429)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #429.

In a single-sided document, a page that applies a two-page parent spread showed the parent's last page. `Document::parent_page_for` chose the parent's first page only for a left-hand page and the last page for every other side, `PageSide::Single` included. InDesign shows the parent page in the same position as the document page, so a single-sided page gets the first one. That is where templates keep their footers and running items.

Changes:
- `crates/doc/src/build.rs`: `parent_page_for` now picks index 0 for `PageSide::Left` and `PageSide::Single` when the parent has two or more pages. Right-hand pages in facing documents still get the last page, and a parent without pages still returns `None`. The canvas, the renderer, PDF export and override detection all go through this function, so they all pick up the fix.
- `crates/tools/src/snap.rs`: `shown_parent_page_index` copies the same choice for snapping to parent items (its doc comment says so). It now matches, so in a single-sided document snapping uses the items of the parent page that is actually shown, not the hidden second page.

Tests:
- `single_sided_page_shows_first_parent_page` (doc): a single-sided document with a two-page parent shows page 0 behind both pages, and `None` once the parent has no pages.
- `shown_parent_page_matches_page_side` (tools): the snapping helper picks the first page for single-sided and left-hand pages and the last page for right-hand pages.

Both tests fail without the fix.

title: CLI: --export writes the file type its extension names
author: noah1400

`designcraft-cli run --export` knew `.pdf`, `.epub`, `.idml` and `.designcraft` and saved a PNG of the page under every other name, with exit status 0. `script --export` had its own shorter list with the same catch-all.

The second commit fixes a crash in the same code: `--pdf-options` that is JSON but no object (`[1]`) panicked when the PDF's path was added to it. It is now an error.

2. IDML import: bring in text frames anchored inside stories, and groups holding them. All story ids are now allocated before any story is read, so an anchored frame no longer gets an empty orphan story. Partly addresses #124.

3. Render: compose and draw text in frames anchored inside stories.
