title: Files: saves and exports replace the file atomically
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #436.

Saves, Save a Copy, snippets, books, libraries, swatch files and every export (PDF, booklet, HTML, story text, EPUB, IDML, XML, MCP renders) wrote with `std::fs::write` over the existing file, so a crash, a full disk or a dropped network volume mid-write destroyed the document.

`designcraft_engine::atomic::write_atomic` writes a uniquely named temporary file in the same folder, flushes it, keeps the old file's Unix permissions, renames it over the target and flushes the folder. If any step before the rename fails, the temporary file is removed and the original is untouched; it never falls back to writing in place. A symlinked target is replaced through the link (bounded, loops are errors). On Windows a rename blocked by another process is retried with short backoff. A read-only file is refused on Unix, as an in-place write would be. Web builds are unchanged.

Validation: `atomic` tests (replace and create with no leftovers; a write failing partway leaves the original and no temporary file; rename retry stops on the last try and only for sharing errors; permissions kept and read-only refused; read-only folder; symlink replaced through the link, loop rejected) and `save_tests` (`file.save` and `file.saveACopy` over a 1 MB document leave only the document; a missing folder is an error naming the path). Windows clippy passes. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Tools panel: Selection is the filled arrow, Direct Selection the hollow one
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #437.

The Tools panel drew Selection as the hollow arrow and Direct Selection as the filled one, the opposite of the usual convention and of the Direct Selection cursor.

Validation: `selection_arrow_is_filled_and_direct_selection_hollow` (checks which icon's path is filled; failed before). `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Canvas: tools show their own cursors (Direct Selection, Pen states)
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #438.

Tool cursors mapped to system cursors: Direct Selection showed the default arrow and the Pen tool a crosshair, so the cursor didn't say what a click would do.

- Code-drawn cursors (black ink on a white halo): filled arrow (Selection), hollow arrow (Direct Selection), pen nib, and pen nib with +, −, ○ or ^ (add, delete, close, convert), and a rotate cursor. Text, hand, zoom, crosshair, move and resize stay system cursors.
- On Linux and Windows they are OS cursor bitmaps at system cursor size, cached per scale. On macOS, where cursor bitmaps are sized in points, the glyph is painted at the pointer with the OS cursor hidden, so it stays sharp on Retina. The web build keeps system cursors.
- The Pen tool shows close over the first anchor of the path being drawn; over a selected path it shows delete on an anchor and add on a segment, and a click deletes or adds the anchor. The Add, Delete and Convert Direction tools show their pen cursors.

Validation: `pen_cursor_shows_add_delete_and_close`, `anchor_tools_show_pen_state_cursors` (tools); cursor raster tests (every glyph at 1× and 2×, hotspot inside, filled and hollow arrows differ, cache reuse); `tools_show_their_own_cursors_over_the_page` (Pen and Direct Selection put their bitmap in the platform output; Type keeps the text cursor). macOS clippy and the web build pass. `cargo xtask ci` passes on a branch that combines this one with the other open PRs.

title: Fix needless horizontal scrollbar in the app bar at 115% scale (#481)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #481.

At 115% interface scale, the app bar's right-hand tools slot was sized to the full remaining width of the row. Fractional-scale rounding could make the row a fraction of a pixel wider than its horizontal scroll area, so a scroll bar appeared that scrolled only a tiny amount.

The slot is now one pixel narrower than the remaining width (`tools_slot_width`). It is still never narrower than the controls, so a narrow window keeps scrolling as before.

A unit test covers both cases: the slot leaves slack when everything fits, and it keeps the controls' width when the window is narrow.

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across DesignCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for DesignCraft.

title: UI: Alt + wheel zooms the view at the pointer
author: noah1400
body:
Addresses the first half of #470.

Turning the mouse wheel over a document view with Alt (Option on macOS) held scrolled the view like the plain wheel. It now zooms at the pointer, exactly as Ctrl/Cmd + wheel does.

Like egui's Ctrl/Cmd zoom, a wheel motion keeps its key to its end. The wheel is smoothed over a few frames and a trackpad swipe coasts on, so letting Alt go early does not turn the rest of the motion into scrolling.

Not changed: Ctrl/Cmd + wheel still zooms. The issue also asks for it to scroll sideways. A touchpad pinch reaches an app like this one as Ctrl + wheel on Windows, so that change would turn pinch-zoom into panning there (not tested on Windows); Shift + wheel already scrolls sideways. I left that half for a maintainer's call.

The `cargo xtask ci` steps (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Selection tool: Alt and Shift resize around the centre and keep side-handle drags centred
author: aiongg
body:
Problem: resizing with the Selection tool combined the modifiers in the wrong order and anchored them to the wrong points.
- Alt on a corner handle could only grow a frame. Dragging the corner inwards left the frame unchanged, because the opposite corner set the minimum half-size.
- Alt+Shift applied the aspect constraint to the edge-anchored rectangle first and then centred it, so shrinking failed the same way and the driving axis was chosen from the wrong measurement.
- Shift on a side handle scaled the other axis from one edge, so the frame grew to one side instead of staying on its centre line.

Change (`crates/tools/src/select.rs`):
- `finish_resize` applies Alt first, then Shift. With both, the frame scales by one factor around its centre, measured from the centre, and the dragged corner stays under the pointer on the driving axis.
- `apply_alt` mirrors only the dragged sides around the centre, so a drag inwards shrinks the frame and a drag past the centre flips it.
- `apply_aspect` keeps the edges opposite the handle fixed and centres any axis the handle does not move.

Validation: `cargo test -p designcraft-tools --lib -- resize` (`resize_side_shift_keeps_the_other_axis_centred`, `resize_corner_alt_shift_scales_around_the_centre`, `resize_corner_alt_mirrors_the_opposite_side`; all three fail before the change), `shift_alt_resize_keeps_aspect_and_center` and `resize_rect_modifiers` still pass; `cargo clippy -p designcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

title: Text: copied text keeps its endnotes and editorial notes
author: aiongg
body:
`Story::extract` copied footnotes, cross-references, index markers and anchored objects with a text range, but not endnotes or editorial notes, so copy/paste and drag-copy/move left those markers with empty payloads. It also sliced each payload list by marker count, and inserting a footnote, endnote or editorial note indexed the payload list, so a story with more markers than payloads (a damaged or hostile file) panicked.

- `extract` copies endnotes and editorial notes, reads every payload list with `get`, and fits the slice's lists to its markers (`fix_notes`, new `fix_endnotes`, `fix_marks`): a missing payload becomes an empty one.
- `insert_story` writes the payloads into the entries made for the pasted markers; they keep new ids, so a pasted copy is independent of the original.
- `footnote.insert`, `endnote.insert` and `note.new` repair the payload lists first and write through `get_mut`; `insert_note`/`insert_endnote` return `Option<u64>` (commands report an error, Word import a warning).
- Formatted paste into a table cell drops endnote references and note anchors, as it does footnotes. `set_story_text` resets endnotes and editorial notes too.

Validation: `slice::tests::copy_paste_keeps_endnotes_and_editorial_notes`, `slice::tests::extract_survives_more_markers_than_payloads` and `cmd::editorial::tests::notes_insert_into_a_story_whose_markers_lack_payloads` (both panicked before); existing copy/paste, drag, footnote, endnote and Word import tests pass.

title: UI: make the application bar's search field find and run commands
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #480.

**Problem.** The search field at the right of the application bar was only painted: clicking it did nothing and it took no text, on every platform.

**Change.**
- The field is a real text field. A click gives it the keyboard; typing lists the matching menu commands in a dropdown under it, labelled in the interface language with their shortcuts. Labels match in the interface language and in English.
- ↑/↓ move the highlight, Return or a click runs the command the way its menu item does (commands that open a dialog open it). Commands that are off show greyed and don't run. Escape clears the field. Both give the keyboard back to the widget that had it.
- While the field has the keyboard, keys reach neither the shortcuts nor the document. That includes the Escape press that leaves the field, so it no longer switches the tool.
- The search reuses Quick Apply's command list and matching (`menus::command_search`).
- New string "No matching commands" with de/fr/es/ja/zh/ar/pt-BR/it/uk rows; "Search" and "Search commands" get German, French and Spanish translations.

Validation:
- `chrome::tests::the_search_field_finds_and_runs_menu_commands` (German labels listed, a disabled command doesn't run, ↓ ↑ Return groups two frames, the field releases the keyboard)
- `chrome::tests::keys_typed_in_the_search_field_stay_out_of_the_document` (tool keys, Delete, Backspace, Cmd+A and Escape leave the tool and the frames alone)
- `menus::tests::command_search_matches_labels_in_the_interface_language`
- the i18n tests, Quick Apply tests, and `cargo clippy -p designcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: IDML: import and wrap around custom text-wrap boundaries
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #451.
Builds on #384.

## Problem

An IDML item's `TextWrapPreference/Properties/PathGeometry` holds a wrap boundary edited apart from the frame (a triangle on a rectangle, for example). Import read only the wrap mode, side, contour type and offsets, so text wrapped around the frame's bounds and every later line moved.

## Change

- Model: `TextWrap.path`, an optional custom boundary in the item's inner space (the space of its own path), with the offsets already included. Absent by default and not serialized when absent.
- Import: reads the boundary from `TextWrapPreference`'s `PathGeometry`. A boundary with more than 4096 points, a malformed or non-finite point, or no points is dropped with a log warning; the rest of the wrap still imports.
- Export: writes the boundary before `TextWrapOffset`, so it round-trips.
- Compose: with a custom boundary, bounding-box and contour wraps follow it through the contour machinery of #384, band by band; jump modes use its bounds. Offsets are not added again.
- Editing: resizing an item (`transform.resize`, layout adjustment, liquid layout and the other paths through `bake`) transforms the boundary with the frame's path. Setting `offset` or `contour` through `object.textWrap` drops the boundary, because both would otherwise have no effect; mode and side keep it. Other path edits keep it unchanged. The params doc says so.

Validation:
- `idml::tests::custom_wrap_boundary_imports_composes_and_round_trips`
- `idml::tests::hostile_custom_wrap_boundary_is_dropped`
- `engine::tests::custom_wrap_path_follows_resize_and_yields_to_offsets`
- existing wrap and contour tests in `designcraft-compose`, `designcraft-idml` and `designcraft-engine`

title: Layout: parent pages pass margins and guides to their pages
author: aiongg
body:
Margins and columns lived only on each page: changing them on a parent spread didn't reach the pages based on it, and ruler guides on a parent page didn't appear on those pages.

- A document page without its own margins takes its parent page's margins and columns (left parent page for left pages, right or only one otherwise) and follows later changes, also when it changes side or parent.
- Setting margins on document pages makes them the pages' own (`Page::local_margins`); parent changes then leave them alone.
- `layout.marginsAndColumns` takes `parent` (prefix, label or index). While parent spreads are shown, the Properties panel's margin fields edit the parent under the view centre. The dialog is unchanged.
- Parent ruler guides are drawn and snapped to on every page based on that parent, but can't be picked, moved, listed or deleted from the page. They are read in place, with no per-frame allocation.
- IDML import: a page whose MarginPreference matches its parent page follows the parent, one that differs is its own, one without takes the parent's. Older `.designcraft` files mark pages that differ from their parent as their own on load, so nothing moves.

Validation: `differing_margins_from_older_files_stay_local` (doc); `pages_follow_their_parent_pages_margins_unless_set_locally`, `parent_guides_show_on_pages_but_stay_on_the_parent`, `parent_and_page_margins_round_trip_through_idml` (engine); `parent_page_guides_snap_on_the_document_page` (tools); `parent_guides_on_a_page_are_not_picked_there` (ui-egui).

title: UI: set the interface language in Preferences

title: View: leave Presentation mode with Esc or Shift+W

Problem: Presentation screen mode hides the menus, panels and toolbar, and Esc did nothing in it, so there was no way back to editing short of quitting.

title: Color: retain ICC data and stable profile ids
author: KnottyDyes
body:
PDF/X-4 export always embeds the built-in generic CMYK profile as its output intent. Letting users pick a press profile (#159, #32) needs the colour crate to keep more of an imported ICC profile than it does today. This PR is that first step only.

- Imported ICC profiles keep their exact bytes, profile class and channel count, so a later change can embed them as a `DestOutputProfile`.

- Colour conversion and PDF export are unchanged. Choosing the output intent, finding installed profiles, saving the choice and the dialog would follow in later PRs.

Validation: the three new test files fail against `main` and pass with the change (13, 2 and 14 tests). `cargo test -p designcraft-color` (67 passed) and `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Recovery: each running app keeps its own recovery data
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #496.

Every running DesignCraft wrote its recovery entries into the one recovery folder, named by a document counter that starts at 1 in every process. Two running apps wrote over each other's `1.designcraft`, and an app that started reopened and removed the entries of one still running.

- Each run makes a folder of its own in the recovery folder (`run-<pid>-<n>`) and holds a file lock in it until the process ends.
- An app that starts moves into its own folder the entries of runs whose lock is free, and those an earlier version wrote straight into the recovery folder, then reopens them as before. A locked folder is left alone.
- The folder of a run that ended is removed once its documents are out. A document that could not be moved, or a file the app did not write, keeps the folder as it is.
- If a run's folder cannot be made or locked, the app writes to the recovery folder itself, as before, and logs a warning. Such a run does not see the folders of other runs.
- `file.recovery.*` with an explicit `dir` works on that one folder as before. `main.rs` is unchanged: `profile::recovery_dir()` returns the run's folder.
- Not solved from this side: a 0.6.0 app running beside a new one still writes straight into the recovery folder, so the new one takes its entries as before.

Overlap with #380: it changes the end of the loop in `recovery::open` so that a reopened document's entry stays on disk. This PR does not touch those lines, and with #380's `recovery.rs` change applied on top the recovery tests of both pass.

Validation:

- Twelve new tests in `recovery.rs` and one in `profile.rs`. `documents_of_two_apps_that_ended_are_both_recovered` and `a_running_apps_recovery_data_is_left_alone` are the two halves of the issue; both fail against a `run_dir` that returns the shared folder, which is the old behaviour.
- The desktop app on Linux, two instances on one profile (`DESIGNCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`), driven over `--control` and ended with SIGKILL. Before: the restart reco…

title: Color parsing: one scale per colour, not per component
author: japbcoelho
body:
`parse_color` chose the scale for each component on its own (above 1 → percent, otherwise a fraction), so a CMYK percentage of 1 or less next to larger ones was read as a fraction. `{"c": 0.7, "m": 0, "y": 12.2, "k": 0}`, a pale cream, became C 70 % Y 12.2 % and exported as `0.7019608 0 0.12156863 0 k`. The params docs say `{c,m,y,k}(0..100)`. RGB arrays had the same rule.

Now a colour is read on one scale: percentages (0..100, RGB 0..255) when any component is above 1, fractions only when every component is within 0..1, so the older fraction form keeps working. A colour whose percentages are all 1 or less is still read as fractions.

Validation: the bug reproduces with the v0.6.0 release CLI (`swatch.create` with the cream above, a frame filled with it, then `file.exportPdf`). New test `color_tests::percent_components_at_most_one_stay_percent` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/style.rs`. On main `ca343e8`: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p designcraft-engine` pass; the full `cargo xtask ci` is left to the checks here.

title: Place: PDF pages and SVGs keep their exact size
author: japbcoelho
body:
`file.place` took a placed PDF page's (and an SVG's) natural size from `image_size`, which rounds to whole points, and the export draws the page into that size. A 91.774 × 613.276 pt page became 92 × 613 and was drawn 0.25 % wider and 0.3 % shorter, so pieces of a cover laid edge to edge left gaps of up to 1.9 pt. A 100.4 × 50.4 pt page placed 100.4 pt wide came out `Rect { x0: 0.0, y0: 0.0, x1: 100.4, y1: 50.2 }`.

The natural size is now the exact page (crop box) or SVG size, through a new `designcraft_render::natural_size`; the rounded `pixels` stay for display and preflight. `place.load` (the place cursor) gets the same exact size.

Validation: the bug reproduces with the v0.6.0 release CLI (the placed page is drawn at x 1 by y 0.996). title: MCP: never replay a request after a lost reply
author: KnottyDyes
body:
When a request to the running app fails mid-flight, the MCP remote backend reconnects and sends the same request again. A lost reply doesn't mean the request wasn't applied, so an edit such as `frame.create` can be applied twice.

- A failed request now drops the connection and returns an error saying the operation may have completed and the document should be inspected before retrying. It is never resent.
- The next request reconnects as before, so a restarted app is still picked up. This matches how PhotoCraft's bridge behaves.
- `docs/mcp.md` describes the uncertain outcome in connected mode.

Validation: a loopback test server applies the edit and closes the connection before replying. Before the change the client resent it and the edit was applied twice; now it is applied once, the call returns an error and the next call reconnects. `cargo test -p designcraft-mcp` (18 passed) and `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

title: Compose: Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar break between words and justify without tearing marks
author: visarutforthaipbs
body:
Fixes #515.

Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar are written without spaces between words. Until now the composer had no word boundaries for them, so lines were split mid-word by the emergency path, and justified lines were letter-spaced through the Single-Word path, pulling combining vowels and tone marks off their consonants.

## What changes
- **`crates/compose/src/sea.rs` (new):** word boundaries from `icu_segmenter` (ICU4X 2.3, already in `Cargo.lock` through other deps; compiled data; wasm-safe). A boundary is kept where the dictionary and the LSTM segmenter agree — the dictionary alone is greedy longest-match and yields `ผลก|า|รตร|วจส|อบ`; the LSTM alone splits compounds. Results are cached per paragraph text. Extra rules: no line starts with ๆ ฯ ะ า ำ, none ends with เ แ โ ใ ไ.
- **`shape.rs`:** `Glyph::word_gap`, set at a boundary between two SEA letters.
- **`breaker.rs`:** in justified text a word gap is a zero-width stretch glue (`Spacing::sea_gap_stretch`, 0.5 of a word space), so Knuth–Plass sees stretch between Thai words. Ragged text keeps the `penalty(0)` path.
- **`lib.rs`:** `layout_line`/`distribute` treat word gaps as justification slots and never add letter space before an *attached* glyph (a mark, or a later glyph of the same cluster — `Glyph::ch` is the cluster's first char, so detection goes by cluster). Inside Thai words letter-space stretch is withheld when the line has word gaps.
- Only pairs where **both** glyphs are SEA letters get a boundary; ICU word boundaries around `(`, `.`, `-` are not line-break opportunities.
- Non-SEA paragraphs return before any of this runs; a Latin snapshot test shows identical breaks and widths.
